306.e: Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Page - 71.

306.q: A 6 year old child presents to the hospital with history of mouth breathing, mal-occlusion of teeth and conductive hearing loss due to glue ear. Which of the following will be best management plan for this patient?
o: Adenoidectomy with Myringotomy with grommet insertion
306.e: History of mouth breathing, mal-occlusion of teeth in a 6 year old child are features of adenoid facies arising from adenoid hypertrophy. Adenoid hypertrophy causes bilateral eustachian tube blockage leading to formation of glue ear(serous otitis media). This causes conductive hearing loss. This child would need adenoidectomy(for adenoid hypertrophy) along with Myringotomy with Grommet insertion(to treat glue ear). Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, pg. no. 288, 77

306.q: Which of the following best describes Trotter's Triad?
o: Palatal Palsy, Temporo-parietal pain, Conductive Hearing Loss
Palatal Palsy, Temporo-parietal pain, Sensorineural Hearing Loss
Palatal Palsy, Retro-orbital pain, Conductive Hearing Loss
306.e: Nasopharyngeal cancer can cause conductive deafness (eustachian tube blockage), ipsilateral temporoparietal neuralgia (involvement of CN V) and palatal paralysis (CN X)- collectively called Trotter's triad .

306.q: Cerebrospinal rhinorrhea is usually due to a fracture of:
306.e: CSF from anterior cranial fossa reaches the nose via Cribriform plate Roof of ethmoid air cells Frontal sinus. CSF from middle cranial fossa follows injuries to sphenoid sinus. In fractures of temporal bone , CSF reaches the middle ear and then escapes through the eustachian tube into the nose ( CSF otorhinorrhoea ) Overall most common site of CSF rhinorrhea is cribriform plate (Ethmoid bone). Most common cause now a days is iatrogenic (E.g. FESS) Second common cause is traumatic CSF leak – site of leak – Fovea Ethmoidalis (Frontal bone) Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat, 8 th edition, page 192

307.q: The main function of middle ear is
o: Conduction of sound energy to inner ear
307.e: The middle ear converts sound of greater amplitude but lesser force, to that oflesser amplitude but greater force. This function of the middle ear is called impedance matching mechanism or the transformer action. This is to counterbalance the loss of sound energy in the inner ear fluids. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Pg. no - 17, 18.

307.q: A 40 year old patient developed sudden hearing loss on right side within a span of 12 hours. On audiometry, the right ear has 70dB hearing loss over 500, 1000 and 2000 Hz. All of the below are proposed management options in this patient except
307.e: This is a case of Sudden SNHL. Treatment(Proposed) : Bed rest Steroid therapy. Inhalation of carbogen(5% CO 2 + 95% O 2 ) Vasodilator drugs Hyperbaric oxygen therapy Caroverine is not used in the treatment of sudden SNHL. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Page - 42.

307.q: A patient presents to the OPD with complaints of bilateral hearing loss with worsened right ear hearing loss. On examination, the doctor diagnoses otosclerosis and recommends stapedectomy as the final resort to the problem. What would be findings of tuning fork tests based on which doctor recommends stapedectomy:
o: Rinne's test - positive: Weber's test - lateralized to left ear
Rinne's test - positive: Weber's test - lateralized to right ear
Rinne's test - negative: Weber's test - lateralized to left ear
Rinne's test - negative: Weber's test - lateralized to right ear
307.e: Hearing loss is a presenting symptom in otosclerosis , usually starts in early twenties, often bilateral conductive type. In conductive type of hearing loss, Rinne's test shows negative result for frequencies (BC>AC) and Weber's test is lateralized to affected (worse) ear. Tuning fork test will show negative Rinne (BC>AC) first for 256 and then 512 Hz and after complete stapes fixation, for 1026 Hz. Weber will be lateralized to ear with greater conductive hearing loss. Absolute bone conduction may be normal.

307.q: One of the following is not the criteria to label a hearing loss as Sudden SNHL
o: Hearing loss should be more than 30 dB
Hearing loss should be seen on minimum 3 continuous frequencies in audiometry
Hearing loss should have occurred within 3 days
Bilateral Hearing loss should be there
307.e: SUDDEN SNHL Definition- It is defined as sudden hearing loss of minimum 30dB It should be visible in at least 3 continuous frequencies in PTA It should have happened within 3 days. It’s unilateral. And has Unknown etiology. Hypothesis- Inflammatory cochleitis. Viral cochleitis. Autoimmune disease. Vascular cause. Treatment – DOC-oral steroids. Other treatments- Transtympanic injection of dexamethasone (using MICROWICK). Hyperbaric oxygen therapy. Betahistine (It is a labyrinthine vasodilator). Antiviral drugs. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Page - 42.

307.q: A steel factory worker is suffering from noise induced hearing loss. Which of the following is most likely to be affected?
o: Outer hair cells in basal turn of cochlea
Inner hair cells in basal turn of cochlea
Outer hair cells in apex of cochlea
307.e: Noise Induced Hearing Loss causes damage to hair cells, starting in the basal turn of cochlea. Outer hair cells are affected before the inner hair cells. Outer hair cells are vulnerable to sounds and drugs while the inner hair cells are more resistant. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Page - 41.

307.q: All are the proposed treatment modalities for sudden sensorineural hearing loss except
307.e: Drugs such as cisplatin, mitomycin-C, 5-fluorouracil, pacititaxel, docetaxel and hydroxyurea have been used in concomitant chemoradiation. They act as radiosensitisers and potentiate the effect of radiation by their additive or synergistic effect. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose, AND Throat by PL Dhingra, Pg no. 426

307.q: A Patients presents to your clinic for evaluation of defective hearing. Rinnie's test shows air conduction greater than the bone conduction on both sides with Weber test lateralized to right ear. What is the next logical step?
o: This is indicative of Normal hearing
Repeat Rinnie's test on right side
307.e: Schwabach and ABC(Absolute Bone Conduction) test both are used to test the bone conduction(functioning of cochlea). To give proper meaning to Rinne and Weber test findings, they should be followed by either of these. In ABC, external auditory canal is occluded while in Schwabach's test, EAC is not occluded. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Page -

307.q: Patient has the complaint of right sided hearing loss and left ear hearing is normal. Tuning fork tests show that Rinne is Negative on right side and positive on left side. Weber test is lateralised towards left ear. What is the interpretation?
307.e: It is a situation of false negative Rinne. Rinne is negative in right ear but Weber is heard in left ear(better ear). This contradiction is the best hint for false negative Rinne which is seen in unilateral severe SNHL. Reference : Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8th Edition, Chapter name: Assessment of Hearing, Page number: 26

308.q: A 31 year old female patient complains of bilateral impairment of hearing for the past 5 years. The audiogram shows a bilateral conductive deafness. Impedance audiometry shows As type of curve. All constitute part of treatment, except:
308.e: The history and investigations done suggest the diagnosis as OTOSCLEROSIS. TREATMENT : Rx of choice is surgery called Stapedotomy>Stapedectomy. Other treatment for Otosclerosis Hearing aid- is given for patients unwilling for surgery. Sodium fluoride (NaF) oral therapy. It i is treatment of choice for Schwartz sign (+) patient. (Early stage of disease) Cochlear otosclerosis. NaF leads to stabilization of disease. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Page - 105, 106.

308.q: Abnormal perception of loudness is seen in?
308.e: Abnormal perception of loudness is seen in Meniere's disease. It is called Recruitment phenomenon. It is tested using ABLB testing(alternate binaural loudness balancing test). Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Page - 30.

308.q: High frequency audiometry is used in
308.e: Ototoxic drugs involve high frequency more commonly than the low frequencies. Hence high frequency audiometry is useful in its diagnosis. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Page - 39.

308.q: A 43 year old mechanical engineer has presented to outpatient clinic with the complaint of right sided hearing loss and Tinnitus. These symptoms have been troubling him for last one year. The hearing loss is progressive in nature. Ear examination of the patient is normal. Pure tone audiometry has shown right sided sensorineural hearing loss. MRI Brain shows space occupying lesion at right cerebellopontine angle. Which of the following is the most likely & earliest clinical finding which can be detected on nervous system examination in this patient?
308.e: Vth nerve. This is the earliest nerve to be involved. There is reduced corneal sensitivity, numbness or paraesthesia of face. Involvement of this nerve indicates that the tumour is roughly 2.5 cm in diameter and occupies the cerebellopontine angle. VIIth nerve. Sensory fibres are affected early. There is hypoaesthesia of posterior meatal wall (Hitzelberger's sign), loss of taste (as tested by electrogustometry) and reduced lacrimation on Schirmer test. Motor fibres are more resistant and are affected late. Delayed blink reflex may be an early manifestation. IXth and Xth nerves. There is dysphagia and hoarseness due to palatal, pharyngeal and laryngeal paralysis. Other cranial nerves. XIth and XIIth, IIIrd, IVth and VIth are affected when tumour is very large. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose & Head and Neck surgery by P L Dhingra, 9 th edition, Pg.no.132

308.q: The hearing at which frequency is affected first in noise induced hearing loss?
308.e: The audiogram in Noise Induced Hearing Loss shows a typical notch at 4 kHz, both for air and bone conduction. It is usually symmetrical on both sides. At this stage, patient complains of high-pitched tinnitus and difficulty in hearing in noisy surroundings but no difficulty in day-to-day hearing. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Page - 41.

308.q: Which of the following is not an ototoxic antibiotic?
308.e: OTOTOXICITY (DRUG INDUCED HEARING LOSS) Aminoglycoside-e.g.- Amikacin, Streptomycin, Gentamicin->Irreversible damage to outer hair cell of cochlea Loop diuretics-e.g.- Furosemide, ethacrynic acid. (Act at stria vascularis cochlea of cochlea) Antimalarials- e.g.- Chloroquine, Quinine. NSAIDs-e.g.- Aspirin, Ibuprofen, Indomethacin. Anticancer-e.g.- Cisplatin, Carboplatin. Deferoxamine. Vancomycin. Erythomycin. Reversible Ototoxicity- seen in Aspirin, diuretic, antimalarials. Ototoxicity shows High frequency SNHL in early stages, therefore high frequency Audiometry (9000 to18000Hz) is a special test used to diagnose Ototoxicity. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Page - 39, 40.

308.q: A young man has right side hearing loss following an accident. On otoscopic examination, right tympanic membrane was normal. Pure tone audiogram shows conductive hearing loss of 54 dB in the right ear. Which of the following will be the likely tympanometry finding?
308.e: Conductive hearing loss of 54 dB implies that hearing loss is due to ossicular chain disruption with an intact TM. Type Ad tympanogram is seen in such cases. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Page - 29.

308.q: In audiogram, symbol l(X) is used to mark
308.e: The hearing test results are plotted on a graph with the y-axis representing hearing threshold and the x-axis representing frequency. The right ear is generally plotted with a O and the left ear with a X. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose, AND Throat by PL Dhingra

309.q: Turbinate that articulates with maxilla is
309.e: Inferior turbinate articulates with the maxilla. Superior and middle turbinates are parts of ethmoid bone. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no 159

309.q: Which of the following is the treatment for atrophic Rhinitis?
309.e: ATROPHIC RHINITIS (OZAENA) is a chronic inflammation of nose characterized by atrophy of nasal mucosa and turbinate bones. The nasal cavities are roomy and full of foul-smelling crusts. Surgical management includes: (a) Young's operation . Both the nostrils are closed completely just within the nasal vestibule by raising flaps. They are opened after 6 months or later. In these cases, mucosa may revert to normal and crusting reduced. (b) Modified Young's operation. To avoid the discomfort of bilateral nasal obstruction, modified Young's operation aims to partially close the nostrils. It is also claimed to give the same benefit as Young's.

309.q: Which structure is most commonly involved in the compression of the anterior ethmoid nerve in Sluder's neuralgia?
309.e: Explanation: The anterior ethmoidal nerve is most commonly compressed at the middle turbinate followed by the inferior turbinate. Compression of the anterior ethmoidal nerve leads to anterior ethmoid neuralgia, also referred to as Sluder's neuralgia. Most common cause is a spur impinging on the lateral wall of nose. It is characterised by neuralgic pain in the lower half of the face with nasal congestion, rhinorrhea and increased lacrimation.

Ans. is 'b' i.e., Rhinion [Ref Textbook of general anatomy p. 10] Nasion → The depression at the junction of nose with forehead. Rhinion → The point located at the osseocartilagenous junction over the dorsum of the nose. Radix → Junction between the frontal bone and nasal bone. Columella → Column between the nostrils at the base of the nose..

309.q: The first pass of diagnostic nasal endoscopy passes through which area of nasal cavity?
309.e: Diagnostic nasal endoscopy has three passes. First pass – Examination of nasopharynx and inferior meatus . ( along the inferior turbinate) Second pass - Examination of the sphenoethmoidal recess , superior meatus and openings of sphenoid sinus and posterior ethmoidal cells. Endoscope is passed medial to middle turbinate. Third pass - Examination of the middle meatus in detail. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8th Edition, pg. no- 492, 493

309.q: The etiology of anterior ethmoidal neuralgia is:
o: Inferior turbinate pressing on the nasal septum
Middle turbinate pressing on the nasal septum
Superior turbinate pressing on the nasal septum
309.e: Sluder’s neuralgia = anterior ethmoidal neuralgia Due to middle turbinate pressing on the nasal septum . Characterized by neuralgic pain in lower half of face with nasal congestion, rhinorrhoea and increased lacrimation. Due to neuralgia of sphenopalatine ganglion This is treated by septoplasty . Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no – 549

309.q: Lymphatic drainage of lateral wall of nose
309.e: Ans. is 'd' i.e., All of the above Lymphatic drainage of nose is BY Anterior half of nasal cavity (Both septum and lateral wall) -s Submandibular nodes Posterior half of nasal cavity (Both septum and lateral wall)Retropharyngeal nodes and upper deep cervical nodes.

310.q: A 125-lb, 40-year-old woman with a history of nasal polyps and aspirin sensitivity since childhood presents to the Emergency Department with status asthmaticus and hypercapnic respiratory failure. She requires immediate intubation and is placed on a mechanical ventilator on an FIO2 of 40%, a control rate of 15 breaths/min, and a tidal volume of 500 mL. Which of the following is her approximate alveolar ventilation?
310.e: Alveolar ventilation ( VA ) equals the tidal volume ( VT ) minus the deadspace volume ( VD ) times the breathing frequency ( f ). The deadspace volume can be estimated as 1 mL/lb of body weight. VA = ( VT - VD ) x f VA = (500 mL - 125 mL) x 15 breaths/min VA = 5625 mL/min Reference: Ganong, pp 658-660. Kasper et al., pp 1508-1516. Levitzky, pp 67-71.

310.q: Maxillary bone does not articulate with:
310.e: Ans: B. Sphenoid (Ref Gray's 41/e p484, 40/e p473-476) Maxillary bone does not articulate with sphenoid. Articulation of maxilla: Each maxilla articulates with nine bones: Two of cranium: Frontal & ethmoid. Seven of the face: Nasal, zygomatic, lacrimal, inferior nasal concha, palatine, vomer & adjacent fused maxilla. Sometimes articulates with orbital surface & with lateral pterygoid plate of sphenoid.

310.q: Frontal sinus can be best visualized by:
310.e: Caldwell view (Occipitofrontal view or nose-forehead position) - Frontal sinus – seen best Shows all sinuses except sphenoid sinus Water’s view (occipitomental view or nose-chin position)- Maxillary sinuses (seen best). Shows all sinuses except ethmoid Sphenoid sinus seen only if the film is taken with open mouth Towne’s view is taken for acoustic neuroma and apical petrositis. Schuller’s view is taken for mastoiditis, cholesteotoma, longitudinal fracture of petrous pyramid. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no – 509- 511

310.q: Onodi cells and Haller cells of ethmoid are related respectively to:
310.e: These are variations of ethmoidal air cells. Onodi cell is a variation of posterior ethmoid air cells and lies in close relation to optic nerve . Haller cell is a variation of anterior ethmoid air cells and lies in relation to orbital floor . When present they can increase the chance of complications during FESS. Reference - Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra , 8 th Edition, pg. no – 159, 219

310.q: Which of the following is not true about ethmoid air cells
o: Posterior ethmoid air cells are 1 to 8.
Anterior and posterior ethmoid air cells are separated by basal lamella
Bulla ethmoidalis is the anterior most anterior ethmoidal air cell
Anterior ethmoid air cells are 2 to 8
310.e: The two named constant cells of the anterior ethmoid group include - Agger nasi is the anterior most anterior ethmoidal air cell . It is also called fourth turbinate. Bulla ethmoidalis is the largest and most consistent anterior ethmoid air cell. Anterior and posterior ethmoid air cells are separated by basal lamella or ground lamella. Posterior ethmoid air cells are 1 to 8. Anterior ethmoid air cells are 2 to 8. Reference - Scott Brown’s Otolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery, 8 th edition – Volume 1 – Page - 973

311.q: Which of the following is the best test for olfaction?
311.e: University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification Test or UPSIT Best test for olfaction. Can be self-administered in 10 to 15 minutes. Incorrect Options: Option A - Clove oil is not a standardized test of olfaction. Option C - Acoustic rhinomanometry records the total air flow and resistance to air flow. It is not a test of olfaction. Option D - Ammonia is an irritant and does not stimulate the olfactory receptors. Reference: Scott-Brown's Otolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery: Volume 1, 8th Edition, Page Number 1232, 991; Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Page Number-164.

311.q: Which structure cannot be approached through transnasal endoscopic surgery?
311.e: Think about the anatomy of the eye - lacrimal glands lie in lateral part of orbit . So cannot be approached via transnasal route. Endoscopic surgery can be used to access the orbit, optic nerve, lacrimal sac and pituitary gland in addition to the nose and paranasal sinuses. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, pg. no 494 Parson's Diseases of the Eye - 23 rd edition - Page - 422, 423 Scott Brown's Otolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery, 8 th edition - Volume 1 - Page - 1244, 1283

311.q: The odour receptor is present in:
311.e: Smell is perceived in the olfactory region of the nose, which is situated high up in the nasal cavity (upper 1/3 rd of nasal cavity). Olfactory area is also called the dangerous area of the nose. Esthesioneuroblastoma (Olfactory Neuroblastoma) arises from the olfactory epithelium. Olfactory pathway: Neurons of olfactory epithelium → Olfactory nerves → Pass through the cribriform plate → Mitral cells of the olfactory bulb → Olfactory tract → Prepyriform cortex and amygdaloid nucleus. Olfactory system is also associated with the autonomic system at the hypothalamic level. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Page Number-164, 239.

311.q: A teenager was brought to the hospital by her mother for the evaluation of delay in onset of puberty. While taking the history of the patient, she says that she has always had a very poor sense of smell. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
311.e: This is a case of Kallmann syndrome . Anosmia Congenital hypogonadism leading to delay in puberty Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra , 8 th Edition, pg. no – 547

312.q: A patient presents to her GP with recurrent nosebleeds and also complains of facial fullness and facial pain. Over the past 2 months she has developed progressive shortness of breath and on one occasion she coughed up some blood. What would be the most appropriate test to perform?
312.e: The mostly likely diagnosis in this case is Wegeners granulamotosis. Sinusitis is the commonest ENT manifestation of this auto immune disorder. Septal perforation (bony and cartilaginous), saddle nose deformity with epistaxis is commonly seen. The multi-system involvement leads to pulmonary symptoms. The biopsy from the nose reveals necrotising vasculitis in this case. ANCA(Anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies) testing is further helpful for the diagnosis. Reference: Scott Brown's Otolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery, 8th edition - Volume 1 - Page - 133

312.q: Which of the following is not ligated in case of epistaxis control?
312.e: Internal carotid artery is a very important source of blood supply to the brain. It is never ligated for control of epistaxis due to the risk of serious cerebral complications and mortality. The following arteries are ligated for control of epistaxis. Transnasal Endoscopic Sphenopalatine Artery Ligation (TESPAL) is done first. If uncontrolled, ligation of maxillary artery is done. Then ligation of external carotid artery above the origin of superior thyroid artery should be done. If still uncontrolled, ligation of ethmoidal arteries is done. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, pg. no - 210 Gray's Anatomy- The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice - 41 st edition - Page - 280

312.q: Which of the following is not a true statement regarding the Epistaxis?
o: Majority of the bleeds above the middle turbinate are from sphenopalatine artery
Posterior nasal pack has total 3 threads tied to it, one of them is kept hanging in throat
Woodruff plexus is on lateral wall of nose in the posterior part of nasal cavity
312.e: Above middle turbinate , the area is supplied by Internal Carotid Artery through the Ethmoidal arteries . Below middle turbinate , the External Carotid Artery supplies the area through its branches- greater palatine, sphenopalatine and superior labial. Option A – Hypertension and arteriosclerosis lead to posterior epistaxis . Option C - Posterior nasal pack has 3 threads. Two threads are tied at nostril . 3 rd hangs in throat . It helps in removal of pack. Option D - Woodruff is venous plexus in posterior part of lateral wall of nose. It is a site of posterior epistaxis. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no – 205, 207, 208

312.q: A 35 year old male presents with epistaxis conservative management was done to stop the bleeding but it failed which will be the next step of management
312.e: Endoscopic sphenopalatine artery ligation (ESPAL) is an effective intervention for severe or refractory epistaxis when conservative management fails. It involves the ligation of the sphenopalatine artery, which is the main source of blood supply to the anterior nasal septum. Other options: B. Maxillary artery: While the maxillary artery is the source of blood supply to the sphenopalatine artery, ligating the maxillary artery is an extensive and invasive procedure not typically performed for epistaxis. C. ICA (Internal Carotid Artery): The internal carotid artery is a major blood vessel supplying the brain. D. ECA (External Carotid Artery): This artery supplies blood to the face and scalp. It is not as likely to be the source of epistaxis.

312.q: Sunil, 7 year old child has presented at midnight to emergency with the history of putting a disc battery of his father's wrist watch in his nose few hours back. What would be the ideal management?
o: Next day removal of foreign body in elective operation theatre
312.e: Disc batteries contain alkali - sodium hydroxide, potassium hydroxide and mercury which leaks through them to cause injury. It is observed that a disc battery causes damage to mucosa in 1 hour. Hence disc battery should be urgently removed from the nose. Xylometazoline nasal drops decongest the nose and are used in management of rhinosinusitis. Anterior nasal packing is used in management of epistaxis. Next day removal of foreign body is not suggestive for disc batteries. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no - 409

312.q: Which of the following is false regarding rhinitis sicca?
o: Epithelium undergoes metaplasia from squamous to ciliated columnar
312.e: In rhinitis sicca, the ciliated columnar epithelium undergoes squamous metaplasia with atrophy of seromucinous glands. Rhinitis sicca - Crust-forming disease seen in those who work in hot, dry and dusty surroundings, like bakers, iron- and goldsmiths . Anterior 1/3 rd of nose affected since it is most exposed to the dry air. The ciliated columnar epithelium undergoes squamous metaplasia with atrophy of seromucinous glands. Crust removal → ulceration and epistaxis, and may lead to septal perforation . Treatment - Antibiotic and steroid ointment to the affected part. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no 180

312.q: Which of the following is a wrong match?
o: Mulberry appearance of nasal mucosa- --Inferior turbinate hypertrophy
Strawberry appearance of nasal mucosa-tuberculosis of nose
312.e: Strawberry appearance of nasal mucosa is seen in Sarcoidosis . Granulomatous disease It is a systemic disorder - involvement of lungs, lymph nodes, eyes or skin. In the nose , it presents with submucosal nodules involving septum or the inferior turbinate with nasal obstruction, nasal pain and sometimes epistaxis X-ray chest shows diffuse pulmonary infiltrate with hilar adenopathy . Serum and urinary calcium levels are raised . Serum ACE (Angiotensin converting enzyme) levels raised in active disease. Biopsy of the lesions helps to establish the diagnosis. Treatment is with systemic steroids. For nasal symptoms, steroids can be used locally as nasal spray. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no 187

312.q: Deviated Nasal Septum can lead to all of the following except
312.e: Nasal polypi form due to allergy or chronic inflammation. DNS cannot lead to polyp formation. The clinical features of DNS (Deviated Nasal Septum) include- Nasal obstruction Headache – due to a spur pressing the lateral wall of nose or sinusitis Sinusitis - By obstructing the opening of sinus ostia Epistaxis - drying effects of air currents on deviated septum leads to crust formation, which when removed cause bleeding. Anosmia/ Hyposmia – due to failure of the inspired air to reach the olfactory region External Deformity Middle Ear Infection Inferior turbinate hypertrophy on roomier side. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no 172, 173, 200

313.q: Prussak's space is bounded by all except-
313.e: Boundaries of Prussak's space: Superior - Fibers of lateral malleolar fold Inferior - Lateral process of Malleus Lateral - Shrapnell's membrane Medial - Neck of malleus Trautmann's triangle - This is a triangular space bounded by: Bony labyrinth anteriorly. Sigmoid sinus posteriorly. Dura containing superior petrosal sinus superiorly. Boundaries of Macewen's triangle are as follows: Superiorly: Suprameatal crest Anterior-inferiorly: Posterosuperior wall of external auditory canal. Posteriorly: A tangential line to the posterior canal wall. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8th Edition, Page Number-549.

313.q: The pathway of spread of infection to cochlea in meningitis is
313.e: Venous drainage of labyrinth is through three veins, namely internal auditory vein, vein of cochlear aqueduct and vein of vestibular aqueduct, which ultimately drain into inferior petrosal sinus and lateral venous sinus. Bacterial infections reach labyrinth through the middle ear (tympanogenic) or through CSF (meningogenic). Sensorineural hearing loss following meningitis is a well known clinical entity. Bacteria can invade the labyrinth along nerves, vessels, cochlear aqueduct or the endolymphatic sac. Membranous labyrinth is totally destroyed. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose & Head and Neck surgery by P L Dhingra, 9 th edition, Pg.no.38

313.q: Which ossicle has the least blood supply?
313.e: Incus has no muscle attached to it. Hence it has the least blood supply. Therefore, it is more vulnerable to be eroded in CSOM. Lenticular process followed by Long process of Incus are most commonly involved. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8th Edition, pg. no - 77

313.q: Which of the following is appropriate statement-
o: Ponticulus is the bony spicule between oval and round window
Subiculum is the bony spicule from promontory to pyramid
Donaldson's line is surgical landmark for Posterior cranial fossa
Facial recess is the surgical landmark for posterior tympanotomy
313.e: Facial recess is the surgical landmark for posterior tympanotomy Subiculum seperates oval and round window Ponticulus runs from promontory to pyramid Donaldson's line is surgical landmark for endolymphatic sac Trautmann's triangle is surgical landmark for posterior cranial fossa McEvan's triangle (suprameatal triangle) is surgical landmark for mastoid antrum. Reference : Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8th Edition, Chapter name: Rehabilitation of the Hearing Impaired, Page number: 147

Treatment of Rhinosporidiosis - Complete excision of the mass with a cutting diathermy and cauterization of its base. Recurrences are common after surgery. Dapsone has some role in preventing recurrence. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no – 185, 186

313.q: All are true about Rhinoscleroma except
o: Treatment stopped only when two consecutive cultures are negative.
Frisch bacillus is the causative organism
313.e: Dapsone has some role in preventing recurrence in Rhinosporidiosis. Rhinoscleroma is treated with streptogramin (1g/ day) and tetracycline (2g/day) for a minimum of 4-6 weeks. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no – 181, 185

313.q: Which of the following is not applicable statement of Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis?
o: Intralesional Cidofovir is helpful to reduce the recurrence rate
Indole-3-carbinol derived from cruciferous vegetables has shown some benefit
Microlaryngeal surgery with CO2 laser is the primary modality of treatment
313.e: Papillomas mostly affect supraglottic and glottic regions of larynx but can also involve subglottis, trachea and bronchi. REF:- Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no 360 Cummings Otolaryngeology, Head and Neck Surgery, 5 th edition – Page number - 2881

313.q: What is not seen in longitudinal fractures of temporal bone?
313.e: Longitudinal fracture This is due to falling on the side. 80% of total fractures. Less dangerous. Cause Ossicular dislocation. Cause CHL Vertigo is uncommon. EAC bleeding and CSF otorrhoea are more Common Facial palsy is less common and delayed , it is due to edema of nerve. So, treatment is or oral steroids. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Page - 116.

314.q: Which of the following is not true about physiology of nose
o: The inspiratory and expiratory air currents pass through middle part of nasal cavity
Sinuses are mainly ventilated during expiratory phase of respiration
Nasal cilia beat 10-20 times per second and the mucociliary clearance time is 10 -20 minutes
The rhythmic congestion and decongestion is seen in vasomotor rhinitis
314.e: Nasal cycle of rhythmic congestion and decongestion is seen in all normal individuals. The duration of this cycle varies every 2.5 to 4 hours . This occurs because of the autonomic nerve supply of the nose. Nasal mucosa has rich blood supply. Sympathetic stimulation causes vasoconstriction and shrinkage of mucosa, while parasympathetic stimulation causes vasodilation and engorgement. Autonomic system is unstable in cases of vasomotor rhinitis . So the rhythmic congestion and decongestion is disturbed. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no 162, 198

314.q: Causes of epistaxis are all except:
314.e: Allergic rhinitis presents with watery nasal discharge. Not epistaxis. Causes of epistaxis include- Local causes like trauma (nose picking, intranasal surgery), infections, foreign bodies, high altitude, DNS Adenoids, juvenile angiofibroma, tumors of nose and paranasal sinuses Systemic causes like disorders of blood, liver, kidney, cardiovascular system, general infections, vicarious menstruation. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no – 194, 205, 206

314.q: All of the following are true about Allergic rhinitis except
o: Type 1 Ig E mediated allergic reaction
Pollen is the most common allergen for perennial rhinitis
Ipratropium is helpful in reducing rhinorrhoea in this condition
Sodium chromoglycate is a mast cell stabliser and is useful in its management
314.e: The pollen is the most common allergens to cause seasonal allergic rhinitis . Allergic rhinitis is type I allergic reaction which is IgE mediated . A] Early phase is due to release of histamine from mast cells. B] Delayed phase is due to leukotrienes and prostaglandins. Sodium Cromoglycate is a mast cell stabilizer and hence helpful in its treatment. The most common allergen for perennial allergic rhinitis is house dust mite . Ipratropium bromide is an anticholinergic agent which is helpful in reducing the nasal discharge. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no – 194, 197

314.q: Which of the following is not associated with polyp formation in nose?
314.e: Behcet syndrome (ulcers in oral cavity, genital ulcers and uveitis) is not associated with polyp formation. Various diseases associated with ethmoidal nasal polypi include - Chronic rhinosinusitis due to chronic inflammation. Non-allergic rhinitis with eosinophilia syndrome ( NARES ) is a form of chronic rhinitis associated with polypi. Asthma Aspirin intolerance Cystic fibrosis - due to abnormal mucus. Allergic fungal sinusitis Kartagener syndrome - Bronchiectasis sinusitis, polyposis situs inversus and ciliary dyskinesis Young syndrome - Sinopulmonary disease, nasal polypi and azoospermia. Churg–Strauss syndrome - Asthma, fever, eosinophilia, sinusitis , polyposis vasculitis and granuloma. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8th Edition, pg. no –201

314.q: A 27-year-old man presents with complaints of chronic nasal congestion. About 2 months earlier, he had an upper respiratory tract infection with rhinorrhea and nasal congestion. Since then he continues to have severe nasal congestion for which he uses oxymetazoline nasal twice daily. Physical examination swollen turbinates and no purulent discharge. What is the most appropriate treatment?
o: Discontinue oxymetazoline and start steroid nasal spray
314.e: This is a case of Rhinitis medicamentosa . Caused due to prolonged use of topical nasal decongestants (α 2 -adrenergic agonists- xylometazoline, oxymetazoline). These drugs typically cause vasoconstriction. But in case of prolonged usage, they cause rebound congestion and rhinitis due to reflex vasodilation. Edema and redness of mucosa along with hypertrophy of turbinate may occur. Treatment - Stop using these nasal decongestant drops Short course of steroid nasal spray Turbinectomy – required in some cases if turbinates are hypertrophied. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no 199

315.q: Which statement is true about Ethmoidal polyp?
o: Endoscopic removal is the first treatment of choice
315.e: Recurrences are more common in Ethmoidal polypi after removal as they are allergic in origin. Antrochoanal (AC) polyp is more common in children and its better seen on posterior rhinoscopy. FESS is the treatment of choice for AC polyp. For recurrent AC polyp (second recurrence), Caldwell Luc’s operation is done. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no – 200, 202

315.q: The medial maxillectomy is the preferred treatment now a days for the management of
315.e: Medial maxillectomy is the treatment of choice for Ringertz tumor (Inverted papilloma of nose). These days endoscopic approach is preferred. Option a – Surgical approach is the treatment of choice for angiofibroma. The type of approach depends on the stage of the tumor. Radiotherapy and chemotherapy singly or in combination have also been used. Medial maxillectomy alone is not useful. Option c – Antrochoanal polyps is removed via FESS. Option d – Treatment of maxillary sinus malignancy depends on the stage of tumor. Treatment is usually surgery combined with radiotherapy and chemotherapy as needed. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no - 236

315.q: Lymphatic drainage of cervix is to
315.e: A. i.e. Iliac lymph nodes om 94. Maximum contribution to the floor of orbit is by: a) Maxillary b) Zygomatic c) Sphenoid d) Palatine Correct Answer - A Ans. A. Maxillary The maxillae are the largest of the facial bones, other than the mandible, and jointly form the whole of the upper jaw. Each bone forms the greater part of the floor and lateral wall of the nasal cavity, and of the floor of the orbit "Orbital surface of maxilla is smooth and triangular, and forms most of the floor of the orbit" Also know: Maxilla is also the most commonly fractured bone of orbital floor. The floor (inferior wall) is formed by the orbital surface of maxilla, the orbital surface of Zygomatic bone and the orbital process of palatine bone The seven bones that articulate to the orbit are

315.q: The most common organism to cause septal abscess is
315.e: Septal abscess is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus. AETIOLOGY- Secondary infection of septal haematoma – most common cause . Furuncle of the nose or upper lip Typhoid or measles - rare TREATMENT- Immediate incision and drainage Systemic antibiotics COMPLICATONS- Saddle nose Meningitis or cavernous sinus thrombosis – rare but serious Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no – 168, 174

315.q: A patient presents with nasal stuffiness and nasal obstruction. On nasal endoscopic examination, he has been found to have bilateral nasal polypi . He also mentions episodes of wheezing and difficulty in breathing which are resolved by the use of an inhaler. Which of the following drugs would you avoid in this patient?
315.e: This patient with a history of bronchial asthma (episodes of wheezing resolved by inhaler usage) has presented with a nasal polyp now. Aspirin should be avoided in this patient as he may be intolerant to it. Samter’s triad is classically described as - Nasal polypi ( Ethmoidal) Asthma ( Intrinsic) Aspirin intolerance ( NSAIDs) Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8th Edition, pg. no – 201

315.q: The most effective medical treatment of Ethmoidal nasal polypi is?
315.e: Nasal polyp means ethmoidal nasal polyp. Allergy is the main aetiology. So the treatment of choice is topical corticosteroid nasal spray (fluticasone, mometasone). They can be commonly associated with bronchial asthma. Early polypoidal changes with oedematous mucosa may revert to normal with antihistaminics. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra , 8 th Edition, pg. no – 203

315.q: A boxer has been hit on face by fellow player. He has developed nasal blockage on both sides and there is swelling around the nose. What is the further treatment?
315.e: This is a case of septal hematoma. Bilateral nasal obstruction is the most common presenting symptom. Treatment- Immediate aspiration or incision and drainage. Followed by bilateral nasal packing to prevent reaccumulation. Systemic antibiotics – to prevent formation of septal abscess. Complications - If not drained, may organize into fibrous tissue leading to a permanently thickened septum. Septal abscess Saddle nose deformity Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, pg. no- 173, 174 Scott Brown's Otolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery, 8 th edition - Volume 1 - Page - 434

315.q: You are an ENT surgeon. A patient with traumatic head injury presents to you after two weeks with a watery nasal discharge that cannot be sniffed back. He has visited a general physician two weeks ago and was put on bed rest and antibiotics. What is your treatment approach now?
315.e: A watery nasal discharge that cannot be sniffed back following head trauma is CSF rhinorrhea. Initial management is conservative – bed rest, antibiotics, elevating the head of the bed, stool softeners, and avoidance of nose blowing, sneezing and straining. If it does not resolve in 7- 10 days, surgical repair is planned. Transnasal endoscopic approach is the preferred modality these days. Most of the leaks from the anterior cranial fossa and sphenoid sinus can be managed endoscopically with a success rate of 90%. Cartilage graft - If bony defect is larger than 2 cm, it is repaired with cartilage (from nasal septum or auricular concha) followed by placement of mucosa. Fascial graft - Fascia can be obtained from thigh. Or fat from thigh or abdomen can be used. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat, 8 th edition, page 193

316.q: A patient with head injury presents with unilateral conductive hearing loss and bleeding in the ear. Tympanic membrane is intact on examination. The battle sign is positive in the patient. The most probable cause for deafness could be:
o: Collection of fluid in the middle ear
316.e: This is a case of longitudinal fracture of temporal bone. The ear bleeding is a feature of longitudinal fracture. This fracture is due to parietal blow. Battle sign is ecchymosis around the mastoid tip area which is seen in temporal bone fractures. This fracture causes ossicular dislocation and hence conductive hearing loss. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Page - 116.

316.q: A patient of head injury has bluish discolouration over mastoid area, bleeding from EAC and complaining of hearing loss with normal facial nerve function. After three days, patient starts having facial weakness. What is the possible diagnosis?
316.e: Longitudinal fracture This is due to falling on the side. 80% of total fractures. Less dangerous. Cause Ossicular dislocation. Cause CHL Vertigo is uncommon. EAC bleeding and CSF otorrhoea are more Common Facial palsy is less common and delayed , it is due to edema of nerve. So, treatment is or oral steroids. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Page - 116.

316.q: All of the following investigations are helpful in the diagnostic assessment of a patient of CSF Rhinorrhea except
316.e: X ray of paranasal sinuses has no role in the diagnosis of CSF rhinorrhea. Beta-2 transferrin is the best confirmatory test. CT cisternogram - requires intrathecal injection of iohexol and a CT scan to localize the site of leak in cases when beta-2 transferrin cannot be done. Nasal endoscopy can be done to identify the site of leak and for its repair. OTHER TESTS FOR LOCALIZATION OF SITE OF CSF LEAK- High-resolution CT scan - important to see the bony defects. MRI - requires that CSF leak is active at the time of scan. Intrathecal fluorescein study - Dye appears bright yellow but when seen with a blue filter it appears fluorescent green. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat, 8 th edition, page 192

316.q: An young adult presents with nasal deformity following a fall from a ladder. CT scan reveals a displaced nasal bone fracture. What is the optimal timing for fracture reduction in this case?
316.e: Explanation: In nasal fractures, the ideal time for closed reduction is typically within 5-7 days after injury . Timing of Nasal Fracture Reduction: Early reduction (within 12 hours): May be considered only if swelling is minimal and there is marked deformity. However, early reduction is often difficult due to swelling that can hinder the realignment of the nasal bones. (Option A ruled out) Delayed reduction (5-7 days): Preferred in most cases once swelling has reduced, allowing precise correction. This period allows swelling to subside , improving visualization and enabling accurate realignment of the nasal bones. Also ensures better cosmetic and functional outcomes while minimizing the risk of complications. Late reduction (>2 weeks) Not usually recommended, as bone healing begins, making manipulation difficult and resulting in suboptimal. (Option C, D ruled out)

316.q: 23 year old male had a history trauma to his nose with nasal bleeding which stopped on it's own. Following this trauma he developed deformity of his nose with crepitus felt on palpation. X-ray Nasal bone lateral view shows nasal fracture. Ideal time to reduce the nasal bone fracture in this patient is
316.e: The nasal bone fracture should be reduced immediately within 1-2 hours before edema starts. If edema is already there, then wait for 7 days for the edema to subside and then reduce the fracture. It is difficult to reduce a nasal fracture after 2 weeks because the process of callus formation would have started. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat, 8th edition, page 213

β2 transferrin is a protein seen in CSF and not in nasal discharge. Its presence is a specific and sensitive test and requires only a few drops of CSF. Perilymph and aqueous humour are the only other fluids which contain this protein. Another protein called beta trace protein is also specific for CSF and is widely used in Europe. It is secreted by meninges and choroid plexus. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat, 8 th edition, page 192

316.q: After parotidectomy paralysis of the lower lip occurs due to the injury to which structure
316.e: The cervical branch of the facial nerve is a branch of the facial nerve that supplies the muscles of the lower lip and chin region. During parotidectomy, which involves surgical removal of the parotid gland (a salivary gland located near the ear), the cervical branch of the facial nerve can be at risk of injury, leading to paralysis of the lower lip. Main trunk of facial - This is the main nerve that supplies the muscles of the face. It is not injured during parotidectomy. Parotid duct - This is the duct that carries saliva from the parotid gland to the mouth. It is not injured during parotidectomy. Temporal branch of facial - This is a branch of the facial nerve that supplies the muscles of the forehead and temple. It is not injured during parotidectomy.

316.q: All of the following are true about CSF rhinorrhoea except
o: Iatrogenic trauma is the most common cause now a days
Immediate transnasal endoscopic surgical closure of leak site should be done
HRCT skull base is the radiological investigation of choice to detect site of leak
CSF is secreted by the choroid plexus in lateral, third and fourth ventricles.
316.e: Early cases of CSF rhinorrhoea can be managed by conservative measures such as bed rest, elevating the head of the bed, stool softeners, and avoidance of nose blowing, sneezing and straining. Prophylactic antibiotics can be used to prevent meningitis. Acetazolamide decreases CSF formation. If it does not resolve, surgical repair is planned. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat, 8 th edition, page 193

317.q: All of the following are true about nose and sinus malignancy except
o: Tumours of Infrastructure of maxilla carry a poor prognosis.
Nickel exposure leads to squamous cell carcinoma of sinuses
Ringertz tumour of nose is a premalignant condition
Esthesioneuroblastoma is a malignant tumour which originates from the olfactory neuroepithelium of nose.
317.e: Ohngren’s line is from medial canthus of the eye to the angle of mandible. This line divides maxilla into superstructure and infrastructure. The malignancy of superstructure has poor prognosis due to proximity to orbit. In nickel exposed patients, the most common malignancy is squamous cell carcinoma. Ringertz tumour is other name of inverted papilloma of nose. It is a benign but locally invasive and can show malignant conversion. Esthesioneuroblastoma is a malignant tumour which originates from the olfactory neuroepithelium of nose. Also called olfactory placode tumour. Reference - Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra , 8 th Edition, pg. no – 241,242, 236, 239

317.q: A 15 year old male child presents with right sided nasal mass and profuse epistaxis with hyponasality of voice, findings suggestive of conductive hearing loss and cheek swelling. What is the possible diagnosis
317.e: Angiofibroma is a pink, firm, 1- to 2-mm dome-shaped papule most commonly located over the nasal bridge and cheeks and is a benign tumor made of blood vessels and connective tissue that can appear as small, red bumps on the face, particularly on the cheeks and nose. It's a type of vascular tumor that's common in patients with tuberous sclerosis, a genetic disorder.

317.q: All statements are true about Ringertz tumour of Nose except
o: Arises from upper part of nasal septum
317.e: Ringertz tumor arises from lateral wall of nose. Inverted Papilloma (Transitional Cell Papilloma or Ringertz Tumour or Schneiderian Papilloma) It is a tumour of the non-olfactory mucosa of nose ( Schneiderian membrane ) and paranasal sinuses. Most common site of origin is lateral wall of nose in the middle meatus It is a benign but locally invasive tumour and can show malignant conversion. Human papilloma virus is thought to be responsible for its aetiology. Clinically, men are affected more than women in the age group of 40–70. Treatment - Medial maxillectomy is the treatment of choice. These days endoscopic approach is preferred. Radiotherapy is not advised as it may induce malignancy. Reference - Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra , 8 th Edition, pg. no – 236

317.q: Type of carcinoma of the sinonasal tract in wood-workers is
317.e: In woodworkers , adenocarcinomas of ethmoid sinus are more common. Overall, maxillary sinus is the most common sinus to develop malignancy. Squamous cell and anaplastic carcinoma are more common in nickel industry workers. Reference - Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, pg. no – 241

318.q: An ENT surgeon is performing diagnostic nasal endoscopy in a patient of suspected sinusitis. He passes the endoscope at 0 degrees in the middle meatus, what is this pass called?
318.e: Diagnostic nasal endoscopy is done in three passes. First pass – Examination of nasopharynx and inferior meatus. Second pass - Examination of the sphenoethmoidal recess, superior meatus and openings of sphenoid sinus and posterior ethmoidal cells. Endoscope is passed medial to middle turbinate. Third pass - Examination of the middle meatus in detail. Endoscope is passed from the front into the middle meatus. Can examine uncinate process, bulla ethmoidalis, hiatus semilunaris, sinus of the turbinate (cavity on lateral side of middle turbinate) and the frontal recess. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no -492- 493

318.q: A 20 year old male patient with a long standing history of unilateral foul smelling ear discharge presents to the OPD with severe headache, spontaneous nystagmus and a staggering gait. What is the probable diagnosis?
318.e: A long standing history of unilateral foul smelling ear discharge is possibly due to atticoantral CSOM. The onset of severe headache, spontaneous nystagmus and a staggering gait is suggestive of cerebellar abscess. Treatment - High dose antibiotics, neurosurgical approach. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Page - 99, 100.

318.q: A diabetic patient presented to OPD with blood stained nasal discharge and progressive blackish nasal discoloration. Which of the following is the choice of therapy?
318.e: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of Mucormycosis . Mucormycosis is acute invasive fungal infection involving nose and paranasal sinuses, where fungal hyphae invade blood vessels causing ischaemic necrosis. Commonly involves lateral nasal walls and turbinates and quickly spreads to orbit, palate, face and cranium. Treatment is surgical debridement and Amphotericin-B.

318.q: According to Bent and Kuhn classification, which of the following is not a major criterion to diagnose allergic fungal rhinosinusitis
318.e: Fungal culture is a minor criterion. Bent and Kuhn Classification of Allergic fungal rhinosinusitis - Major Criteria – Type I Hypersensitivity Nasal polyposis Characteristic CT findings Eosinophilic mucin without invasion Positive fungal stain Minor Criteria – Asthma Unilateral disease Bone erosion Fungal culture Serum eosinophilia and charcot- leyden crystals Reference - Scott Brown’s Otolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery, 8 th edition – Volume 1 – Page - 1040

318.q: A post covid patient presented with black discharge from nasal cavity. On examination a black nasal mass extending onto orbit. Most likely cause is:
318.e: The most likely cause of the black discharge and nasal mass extending onto the orbit in a post-COVID patient is mucormycosis . Mucormycosis, also known as black fungus , is a rare but serious fungal infection that can affect individuals with weakened immune systems, such as those who have recovered from COVID-19. It typically invades the sinuses and can spread to nearby structures like the orbit. Prompt diagnosis and treatment, including surgical debridement and antifungal therapy , are crucial in managing mucormycosis.

318.q: A patient presents with a cyst like swelling in the superiomedial side of the eye. There is no pain when it is pressed. This entity affects which paranasal sinus most commonly?
318.e: The given description is suggestive of a mucocele . Mucocele of paranasal sinuses - Expansion of bony wall of sinus. Frontal sinus is most commonly affected followed by ethmoidal, maxillary & sphenoidal. Treatment of choice is FESS. Frontal mucocele Usually presents in the superomedial quadrant of orbit - displacing the eyeball forward, downward and laterally. Swelling is cystic, non-tender, egg shell crackling may be present Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no – 231

318.q: Which site is most commonly obstructed by a nasal polyp arising from the maxillary sinus?
318.e: Explanation: The most common location for an obstruction caused by a nasal polyp originating from the maxillary sinus is the middle meatus . Nasal polyps are benign, non-cancerous growths that develop in the nasal passages or paranasal sinuses due to chronic inflammation , often associated with chronic rhinosinusitis, asthma, or allergies . When arising from the maxillary sinus , these polyps typically expand into the middle meatus , which is the drainage pathway of the maxillary sinus . Obstruction at this site can lead to blocked sinus drainage, recurrent sinus infections, nasal congestion, and difficulty breathing.

318.q: What is the first step in functional endoscopic sinus surgery?
318.e: Uncinectomy where the uncinate process is incised with sickle knife and removed with Blakesley forceps is the first definitive surgical step in FESS. Also known as infundibulotomy. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no – 495

319.q: Which of the following is not true about ethmoid bone anatomy?
o: Lamina papyracea is a part of the ethmoid bone.
Inferior Concha is a part of the ethmoid Bone
Cribriform plate is a part of the ethmoid bone
Middle concha is a part of the ethmoid bone
319.e: Inferior concha is an independent bone . Superior and middle concha are parts of ethmoid bone. Uncinate process, lamina papyracea and cribriform plate are also parts of ethmoid bone. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Page Number-164.

319.q: All of the following are true about anatomy of ear except
o: Tensor tympani tendon arises from anterior wall of middle ear
Jugular bulb lies in relation to floor of middle ear
Endolymphatic sac lies in epidural space and reabsorbs endolymph
Epitympanum is the narrowest part of middle ear
319.e: Middle ear has three parts- epitympanum, mesotympanum and hypotympanum. Mesotympanum is the narrowest part - Epitympanum (Attic) is the deepest part of middle ear Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8th Edition, pg. no - 6, 13

319.q: All of the following are true about anatomy of ear except
o: Internal carotid artery lies in relation to anterior wall of middle ear
Pyramid lies on the posterior wall
Aqueduct of cochlea connects endolymph to the endolymphatic sac
Mesotympanum is the narrowest part of middle ear
319.e: Aqueduct of cochlea connects the perilymphatic space of the inner ear to the subarachnoid space of the brain. Reference: Scott Brown's Otolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery, 8th edition - Volume 2 - Page - 545 Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8th Edition, pg. no - 6, 13

319.q: 'Ludwig's angina' is characterized by all the following EXCEPT
o: Cellulitis of floor of the mouth
Aphthous ulcers in the floor of Mouth
319.e: Aphthous ulcers are recurrent and superficial, usually involving movable mucosa, i.e., inner surfaces of lips, buccal mucosa, tongue, floor of mouth and soft palate, while sparing mucosa of the hard palate and gingivae. Ludwig's Angina : Infection of submandibular space(sublingual space + submaxillary spaces) or floor of mouth. It is mainly Cellulitis. Dental Infections account for 80% of the cases. Roots of premolars cause sublingual space infection while roots of the molar teeth cause submaxillary space infection Mixed infections involving aerobes and anaerobes is seen. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingraz, 8 th Edition, pg. no. 255, 31

319.q: In Plummer-Vinson syndrome, the region involved is:
319.e: Plummer vinson syndrome(Paterson-Brown-Kelly syndrome) - Barium swallow shows a web in the postcricoid region and the same can be seen on oesophagoscopy. It is due to subepithelial fibrosis in this region. Predominantly affects females past 40 years. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, pg. no. 401

319.q: All of the following are part of Laryngopharynx (=Hypopharynx) except
319.e: Hypopharynx= laryngopharynx It has 3 parts Pyriform sinus - right and left(=Pyriform Fossa) post cricoid area posterior pharyngeal wall. Anterior pillar, posterior pillar, palatine tonsil, posterior one third tongue, Vallecula , lingual tonsil, soft palate, uvula are parts of oropharynx. So, Vallecula is a part of oropharynx. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Pg. no. 285

319.q: Nucleus ambiguus is not associated with which cranial nerve:
319.e: Ans. D: XII Nucleus Ambiguus Function: * Motor innervation of ipsilateral muscles of the soft palate, pharynx, larynx and upper esophagus. Pathway: * Axons of motor neurons in the nucleus ambiguus course with three cranial nerves: C.N. IX (glossopharyngeal), C.N. X (vagus), C.N. XI (the rostral or cranial portion of spinal accessory) to innervate striated muscles of the soft palate, pharynx, larynx and upper esophagus. Deficits: * Lesion of nucleus ambiguus results in atrophy (lower motor neuron) and paralysis of innervated muscles, producing nasal speech, dysphagia, dysphonia, and deviation of the uvula toward the opposite side (strong side). * No affection of the Sternocleidomastoid or Trapezius. These muscles are innervated by cells in the rostral spinal cord (caudal portion C.N. XI).

319.q: Treatment of choice in a case of Retropharyngeal abscess in a child 2 years of age presenting with stridor and respiratory distress is:
o: Antibiotics for 48 hours and then drainage
319.e: Retropharyngeal abscess Can present as a pediatric emergency . Airway management is the priority. Immediate incision and drainage of abscess should be done. This is usually done without anaesthesia as there is risk of rupture of abscess during intubation. A vertical incision is given in the most fluctuant area of the abscess. Suction should always be available to prevent aspiration of pus. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Pg. no. 313

320.q: A fire breaks out during laser vocal cord surgery. What is not to be done?
320.e: Oxygen will further support the fire being essential for combustion. So never use 100% oxygen when a fire breaks out. Reference - Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, pg. no - 417

320.q: Rhinolalia clausa occurs in all of the following except:
320.e: Explanation: Rhinolalia clausa is not seen in cleft palate. Instead, a cleft palate causes velopharyngeal insufficiency , leading to hypernasal speech (rhinolalia aperta) due to excessive nasal resonance, rather than the nasal obstruction characteristic of rhinolalia clausa. Rhinolalia clausa Rhinolalia clausa or hyponasality is the lack of nasal resonance for sounds that are normally resonated in the nasal cavity, such as m, n, and ng . It manifests as a nasal or blocked voice caused by obstruction of the nasal passages or nasopharynx. Common causes of hyponasality Common cold Nasal allergy Nasal polyp Nasal growth Adenoid hypertrophy Nasopharyngeal mass (Option A, B, D ruled out)

320.q: Which of the following is not a method for adenoidectomy?
320.e: Dissection and Snare method is used for tonsillectomy . The other three methods are used for adenoidectomy. These are endoscopy based newer procedures for adenoidectomy. Coblation is the best Method of Surgery. The traditional method for adenoidectomy is curettage which is a blind procedure. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, pg. no. 503, 507

320.q: Grisel syndrome is a possible complication of which of the following surgical procedure?
320.e: It is atlanto-axial dislocation. Can follow adenoid surgery or nasopharyngeal infections. Manifests with painful neck and torticollis. Treatment includes cervical collar and even traction. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose, AND Throat by PL Dhingra, Pg.492

320.q: Not a true statement regarding adenoids
o: Physiological enlargement continues up to 6 years of age
Digital palpation of adenoid tissue should be avoided before removal in adenoidectomy
320.e: Before adenoidectomy, the adenoid mass should always be palpated before surgery to: Confirm the diagnosis To rule out any abnormal vessel overlying the adenoid mass. Adenoid is irregular on palpation – like a bag of worms. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Pg. no. 507

320.q: A 52 year old female patient underwent total thyroidectomy. While surgery, both side superior laryngeal nerves got damaged accidentally. What are the expected postoperative symptoms of patient?
o: Poor quality of voice and aspiration
Respiratory distress with poor quality of voice
320.e: Cricothyroid is the main tensor of the vocal cord which is supplied by external branch of SLN. Paralysis of this muscle leads to bowing down of vocal cords and hence loss of pitch of voice. The sensory supply of the larynx till vocal cords is by the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve. The loss of this supply can lead to aspiration. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no – 350

320.q: The most likely symptom and laryngeal examination finding in a case of unilateral superior laryngeal nerve palsy are given below. Which is the correct combination?
o: Aphonia; vocal cord in cadaveric position
Weak voice and mild aspiration; bowing of affected vocal cord
Severe aspiration without voice change; fully mobile vocal cords
Asymptomatic; posterior commissure deviation to normal side
320.e: UNILATERAL SLN PALSY Anaesthesia of the supraglottic larynx on affected side - may pass unnoticed or cause occasional aspiration. Paralysis of cricothyroid on affected side – weak voice and pitch cannot be raised with decreased ability to sing. Bowing of affected vocal cord as cricothyroid is the main tensor of larynx. Askew position of glottis as anterior commissure is rotated to the healthy side. Reference – Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra ,8 th Edition, pg. no – 350

321.q: A 10 year old child of 2 weeks post tonsillectomy ate a packet of chips, 2 days after surgery and came to hospital with an oral bleed. What will be the best plan of management?
o: urgent surgical exploration and shift to operating room
Intravenous tranexamic acid and semi solid food for 5 days
321.e: Bleeding after tonsillectomy can be primary (within 24 hours after the operation) or secondary (after 24 hours until 2 weeks). The most likely explanation for secondary bleeding is infection with Streptococcus in the granulating tonsil bed. Treatment depends on the severity and potential cause of the bleed. Antibiotics are advised for secondary bleeding. Severe primary or secondary bleeds need to be controlled in there.

321.q: A 7-year-old post-tonsillectomy child was lying in the ward. He started severely bleeding in the ward and is turning pale and sick. What would be your treatment plan as an Intern in this case?
o: Start Intravenous line and Shift to Operation Theatre immediately
Adrenaline-soaked packing in the Tonsillar fossa and observation in the ward
321.e: If a patient is actively bleeding, the patient should be taken urgently for control of the hemorrhage. Until the patient is transferred to the operating room, if hemorrhaging is significant, direct pressure, either with a throat pack or gauze, should be applied to the tonsillar fossa if the patient is cooperative and an intravenous line can be started before the patient is shifted to the OT.

321.q: All of the following are closely related to the bed of the tonsil except
321.e: Palatopharyngeus muscle does not form the bed of the tonsil. Bed of the tonsil- Formed by the superior constrictor and styloglossus muscles . The glossopharyngeal nerve and styloid process , if enlarged, may lie in relation to the lower part of tonsillar fossa. Both these structures can be surgically approached through the tonsil bed after tonsillectomy. Internal carotid artery lies one inch lateral to the tonsillar bed Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Pg. no. 303

321.q: Secondary hemorrhage in tonsillectomy most occurs
321.e: Secondary hemorrhage occurs mostly after 5 th day of tonsillectomy. Hemorrhage of tonsillectomy- Primary hemorrhage – during surgery Reactionary hemorrhage - Within 24 hours of tonsillectomy. It is due to slippage of ligature and it should be immediately re-explored under GA. Secondary hemorrhage - after 5 th day of tonsillectomy. It is due to infection of tonsillar fossa and is managed with I/V antibiotics. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Pg. no. 506

321.q: A 5 years old child underwent tonsillectomy in the morning. The surgery went uneventful. The patient started having oral bleeding in evening and child has developed signs of hemorrhagic shock. What is the best further management?
321.e: This is a case of reactionary hemorrhage. Hemorrhage of tonsillectomy- Reactionary hemorrhage - Within 24 hours of tonsillectomy. It is due to slippage of ligature and it should be immediately re-explored under GA. Primary hemorrhage – during surgery Secondary hemorrhage - after 5 th day of tonsillectomy. It is due to infection of tonsillar fossa and is managed with I/V antibiotics. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Pg. no. 506

321.q: A 17 years old male patient underwent tonsillectomy on Monday. His post operative period was uneventful. He was discharged on next day. On Sunday morning, he has presented in the Emergency Department of hospital with the complaint of mild bleeding from oral cavity. What is the best further management?
o: It is normal to have mild bleeding in post-operative period, so patient can be reassured and sent home
Admission and Immediate Re-exploration in operation theatre
321.e: This is a case of secondary hemorrhage . Secondary hemorrhage is seen after 5 th day of tonsillectomy. It is due to infection of tonsillar fossa and is managed with I/V antibiotics. Reactionary hemorrhage is seen after 24 hours of tonsillectomy. It is due to slippage of ligature and it should be immediately re-explored under GA. Primary Haemorrhage is during surgery Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Pg. no. 506

321.q: Lakshaya, a 7-year-old school-going child underwent a tonsillectomy. He was shifted to the ward after an uneventful post-operative recovery period. In the evening, the nursing sister notices the patient is profusely bleeding from her mouth. What is the best further management?
o: It is normal to have mild bleeding in post operative period, so the patient can be reassured and sent home
321.e: The most common serious complication of tonsillectomy is delayed hemorrhage. If a patient is actively bleeding, the patient should be taken urgently for control of the hemorrhage. Until the patient is transferred to the operating room, if hemorrhaging is significant, direct pressure, either with a throat pack or gauze, should be applied to the tonsillar fossa if the patient is cooperative. Control of hemorrhage was historically managed with suture ligation, but suction cautery is more routinely performed

321.q: Secondary haemorrage in tonsillectomy is due to
321.e: Secondary haemorrhage: It is a delayed complication of tonsillectomy. Usually seen between the 5 th -10 th post operative day. It is the result of sepsis and premature separation of the membrane. Usually, it is heralded by bloodstained sputum but may be profuse. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Page Number-506.

322.q: Nasal angiofibroma of nose is common in:
322.e: The tumor is testosterone dependent and hence is more common in adolescent males. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Pg. no. 289

322.q: The investigation of choice for a 12-year-old male child presenting with polypoidal mass in the nose, which bleeds on touch is:
322.e: Angiofibroma is the most common benign tumour of nasopharynx seen in adolescent males. It’s a highly vascular tumour. CECT scan shows Holman Miller(= Antral) sign – It is the anterior bowing of posterior wall of the maxillary sinus. It is pathognomic of angiofibroma. Angiography is also done before surgery to identify the main blood supply source of tumour. Pre-op embolisation will reduce blood loss(Maxillary Artery). Debulking or biopsy of this tumour is never done as it is a highly vascular tumour. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Pg. no. 292

322.q: CECT scan of 13 year old male patient with Angiofibroma shows the tumor involving nasopharynx, nose and occupying the pterygopalatine fossa. What is the Radkowski tumour staging of this patient?
322.e: Radkowski staging of Angiofibroma Stage IA - limited to nasopharynx and nose IB - extension into one or more than one sinus IIA - minimal extension into pterygopalatine fossa IIB - full occupation of pterygopalatine fossa with or without erosion of orbital bones IIC - extending Infratemporal Fossa IIIA - erosion of skull base with minimal intracranial invasion IIIB - extensive intracranial invasion with or without cavernous sinus invasion Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Pg. no. 293

322.q: The main vessel involved in bleeding from juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma
322.e: The main feeding vessels of Juvenile Nasopharyngeal angiofibroma are the terminal branches of Maxillary Artery( which is a branch of External Carotid Artery) This artery is subjected to pre-operative embolization to reduce the blood loss during surgery. Resection of tumour should not be delayed beyond 24–48 h of embolization to avoid revascularization from the contralateral side. In very large tumors or those with intracranial extension, bloody supply may come from branches of Internal Carotid Artery. But these are not embolized. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Pg. no. 292

322.q: All of the following are helpful in reducing blood loss during Angiofibroma surgery except-
322.e: Angiofibroma is a highly vascular tumor and its blood vessels lack elastic tissue and muscle fibres and hence cannot contract. So pre-operative debulking of tumor results in massive hemorrhage. 75% of angiofibromas show androgen receptors accounting for growth in males at adolescence. So pre operative estrogen or flutamide(androgen blocker) play a role in preventing blood loss during surgery. Pre-operative embolization cuts off the feeding vessels and reduces blood loss during surgery. Feeders from only the external carotid system can be embolized. Resection of tumour should not be delayed beyond 24–48 h of embolization to avoid revascularization from the contralateral side. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Pg. no. 291, 295

322.q: Type of voice in nasopharyngeal angiofibroma is:
322.e: Rhinolalia clausa is hyponasality. This is due to nasal obstruction, nasal polyp, si nusitis, adenoid hypertrophy, angiofibroma. Rhinolalia aperta is hypernasality. This is due to cleft palate, palatal perforation, palatal palsy, palatal weakness( velopharyngeal insufficiency), submucous cleft palate, bifid uvula. Dysphonia Plica Ventricularis is the production of sound from false vocal cords. Mogiophonia is speech defect in public appearance only Hot Potato voice = Plummy Voice - Seen in Quinsy, paraphrayngeal abscess, retropharyngeal abscess, prevertebral abscess, supraglottic and base tongue cancer Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Pg. no. 366, 368, 311

323.q: A 52 year adult patient presenting with right sided hearing loss has been subjected to audiological investigations and was found to have a type B tympanogram. What will be the priority in further management of this patient?
323.e: This is a suspected case of Nasopharyngeal carcinoma(NPC). Type B tympanogram is suggestive of glue ear(serous otitis media). The unilateral serous otitis media(presenting as conductive hearing loss) in an adult patient should always arise the suspicion of nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Hence, nasopharyngoscopy should be done and biopsy of any suspicious area should be taken. Nasopharyngeal cancer is the occult hidden primary. Cervical lymphadenopathy is the most common presentation of NPC. Myringotomy and grommet insertion will be done for glue ear at a later date when NPC is ruled out. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Pg. no. 297

323.q: A 52 year old patient presenting with right side hearing loss has been subjected to audiological investigations and diagnosed to be a case of right sided serous otitis media. What will be the priority in further management of this patient?
323.e: This is a suspected case of Nasopharyngeal carcinoma(NPC). The unilateral serous otitis media in an adult patient should always arise the suspicion of nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Hence, Nasopharyngoscopy should be done and biopsy of any suspicious area should be taken. Myringotomy and grommet insertion will be done at a later date when NPC is ruled out. Reference: Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat & Head and Neck Surgery by P L Dhingra, 8 th Edition, Page - 75.

323.q: In Nasopharyngeal carcinoma, which of the following is true about the hearing loss in the patient?
o: Unilateral Sensorineural hearing loss due to 8 th nerve involvement
Bilateral Sensorineural hearing loss due to 8 th nerve involvement
Unilateral Conductive hearing loss due to serous otitis media
Bilateral conductive hearing loss due to secretory otitis media
323.e: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma will cause unilateral eustachian tube blockage and hence it will lead to unilateral serous otitis media= glue ear. This causes unilateral conductive hearing loss.
