Hypertension is the least common manifestation of ADPKD
527.e: Explanation: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) results from mutations in Polycystin-1 (chromosome 16) and polycystin-2 (chromosome 4) (Option A). Features: Renal size increases with age, leading to flank or abdominal masses in some patients. Cysts contain clear fluid, thick brown material or coagulated blood. Visible haematuria occurs in up to 40% of patients with ADPKD (Option C) . Cyst haemorrhage is a frequent complication with or without haematuria, depending on whether the cyst communicates with the collecting system or not. Hypertension is the most common manifestation of ADPKD and a major contributor to renal disease progression and cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. After the age of 20 years, most patients are hypertensive. Associated with intracranial aneurysms in 10% of cases (Option B) .

528.q: Identify the false statement regarding fluid therapy for shock.
o: First line therapy is putting a short wide bore intravenous cannula and start Infusion.
Albumin should not be the start in immediate period
Ringer lactate is most physiological fluid and ideal crystalloid.
It is ideal to give inotropic agents regardless of preload to heart.
528.e: If inotropic agents given before achieving adequate preload it will deplete myocardium of oxygen stores and decrease coronary perfusion, so this should not be first priority. In early period of shock vascular permeability would be high so albumin Will not stand in vascular system and start to accumulate in interstitial space. Ringer lactate is ideal physiological fluid as it has all contents required For plasma. Reference: Bailey & Love's short practice of surgery, chapter: 2, Edition: 28th, Pg: 18

529.q: A 22-year-old woman with a history of migraine is prescribed a progestin-only pill. What is the main contraceptive mechanism of action of this drug?
o: Creates an unfavorable endometrium for implantation
529.e: Progestin-only pills are useful for women who are unable to take regular oral contraceptives that contain estrogen due to their side-effects or to the exacerbation of existing conditions like migraine. Daily intake thickens the cervical mucus thus preventing the entry of sperm. The dose of progesterone is not sufficient to inhibit ovulation or reduce luteinising hormone (LH) secretion. Although it decreases tubal motility, this is more related to the occurrence of ectopic pregnancy. It may make the endometrium out-of-phase but not unfavorable for implantation. Reference : Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 21 st edition Page 3034

529.q: Liver transplant in a recipient is contraindicated for which of the following tumor
529.e: People with cancer who can donate liver for transplanataion are: Non melanotic skin cancer Endometrial cancer Brain tumours Any cancer > 5yrs before People who are recipient of liver for transplantation should not be suffering from any cancer

529.q: All of the following are localized variety of Basal cell carcinoma except?
529.e: BCC can be divided into localised (nodular; nodulocystic; cystic; pigmented and naevoid) and generalised (superficial: multifocal and superficial spreading; or infiltrative: morphoeic, ice pick and cicatrizing). Nodular and nodulocystic variants account for 90% of BCC. Typical naevi can be sporadic or familial (familial atypical multiple mole-melanoma [FAMMM] syndrome). Possession of more than five lesions confers a relative risk of melanoma six times greater than usual; within FAMMM syndrome, they confer a 100% risk of malignant melanoma and patients with FAMMM syndrome should be screened for melanoma 6-monthly, lifelong. Reference: Bailey & Love's short practice of surgery 28th Edition, Chapter 45 Pathophysiology of the skin and subcutaneous tissues, Pg: 651-652

530.q: Investigation of choice for screening of proximal internal carotid artery stenosis is :
530.e: Answer is A (Doppler flow USG): 'Stenosis at the origin of the internal carotid Artery can be identified and quantified reliably by ultrasonography that combines B mode ultrasound image with a Doppler ultrasound assessment of flow velocity.'

530.q: Which nerve gives rise to the recurrent laryngeal nerve?
530.e: Explanation: The recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) is a branch of the vagus nerve . The nerve recurs around the arch of the aorta on the left and the subclavian artery on the right. The clinical significance of this is that on the left, the nerve has a longer course to reach the tracheoesophageal groove and therefore runs in a medial plane. On the right, the course is shorter, and the nerve runs more obliquely to reach the tracheoesophageal groove. Approximately 2% of nerves on the right are non-recurrent and will enter the larynx from above.

530.q: 2 years old pediatric patient presented in an unconscious state. He was having profound diarrhoea and mild pneumonia. In the management of this baby when we are doing ABCDE, what does D stand for?
530.e: A- airway management B- breathing and ventilation C- circulation and haemorrhage control D- disability (neurological status) E- exposure

Answer- B. Beta blockade after alpha blocker Beta blockers such as propanalol at doses of 10 to 40 mg every 6 to 8 hours are often needed in patients who have persistant tachycardia and arrhythmias. n-blockers should only be added after adequate a-blockade and rehydration. a-adrenergic agonists may be needed in immediate post operative period to prevent post operative hypotension and cardiovascular collapse.

531.q: Fertile period of female is measured by ?
531.e: Ans, A. LH "LH surge from the anterior pituitary gland occurs 24 hours prior to ovulation. Radioimmunoassays of the morning sample of urine & blood gives results in 3 hours. Not only does the LH surge help in predicting ovulation, but the approximate time of ovulation can be gauged & coitus around this time can improve the chances of conception."

531.q: Which is/are a feature of testicular feminization syndrome:
531.e: In Testicular Feminization Syndrome Genotype – 46XY Gonads – Testis (intrabdominal) Phenotype – Female Internal Genitalia – Is of males (except a short vagina may be present) They are reared as female. Lab investigation : Testosterone levels may be normal/high/low depending on the degree of androgen resistance and the contribution of estradiol to feedback inhibition of the hypothalamus pituitary axis. Laboratory evaluation demonstrates elevated LH levels, normal or slightly elevated testosterone levels, and a 46 XY Karyotype. Reference: Dutta Gynae 6th/ed p 443

531.q: A 12 years old female is admitted as a patient of dys- germinoma of the right ovary 4x5 cm in size with an intact capsule. Best treatment will be:
531.e: Though Dysgerminoma is the most radiosensitive tumour known, treatment of choice is oophorectomy of involved side followed by cisplatin based chemotherapy to preserve fertility, as dysgerminoma is seen in young women with average age incidence being 20 years. BEP: Bleomycin, Etoposide, Cisplatin Reference : Devita 7 th /ed pg 1391; Reference : Williams Gynae 1 st /ed pg 741

531.q: Asymptomatic carriage of gonococcal infection in female is commonly seen in:
531.e: For identification of organisms in PID the materials are collected from the following available sources: Discharge from urethra or Bartholin's gland Cervical canal Collected pus from the fallopian tubes during laparoscopy or laparotomy. The material collected is subjected to Gram's stain and culture (aerobic/anaerobic). The findings of Gram-negative diplococci is very much suggestive of gonococcal infection. There are 2 important points which we should remember about gonorrhoea infection. Squamous epithelium is resistant to gonococcal infection Gonorrhoea is an STD (i.e. it is transmitted by ascending infection along with sperms) Now, since squamous epithelium is resistant to gonococcal infection, in vagina and ectocervix gonococcal infection cannot occur (as both are lined by squamous epithelium). Reference: Dutta Gynae 5th/ed p 143.

531.q: All of the following statements hold true for melanoma of vulva except:
o: It is the 2nd M/C vulvar cancer
531.e: Melanoma is the second most common vulvar cancer. The common sites are the clitoris and labia majora. It may arise from a junctional nevus. Radical vulvectomy and bilateral regional lymphadenectomy (en-block) is the preferred treatment. Pelvic lymphadenectomy does not alter the prognosis. Radiation therapy, adjuvant chemotherapy, or immunotherapy are ineffective. Overall prognosis is poor. Reference: Dutta Gynae 6 th /ed pg 337

531.q: The nerve roots blocked in pudendal nerve block is:
531.e: Pudendal nerve block typically involves blocking the nerve roots S2, S3, and S4, which are responsible for innervating the perineum and pelvic floor. Reference : Dutta Obs 7/e, pg 518

532.q: Suction evacuation can be done up to:
532.e: Friends- there are 2 different methods - menstrual regulation and manual vacuum aspiration . Both of them are based on the same principle i.e. creating a vacuum which helps in extracting out the products of conception. But menstrual regulation is done within 6 weeks whereas, manual vacuum aspiration is a safe method until 12 weeks. Reference:Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 174; Shaw Gyane. 13/e, p 243, 14/e, p 221

533.q: Highest funding for reproductive health is by -
533.e: Ans. is 'a' i.e., UNFPA [Ref Maternal health fifth report session 2007-2008] UNFPA works with a range of partners to promote reproductive health in India. It pools a significant proportion of its country programme resources in the reproductive and child health II (RCH II) programme, aimed at reducing maternal mortality and child mortality, as well as provision of range of contraceptive services. UNFPA also delivers technical assistance for effective implementation of RCH-II programme at the national as well as state level particularly in the state of Rajasthan, M.P. Maharashtra, Orrisa and Bihar.

533.q: Which of following most commonly clinically used?
533.e: Ans, A. Diagonal conjugate Most commonly used clinical conjugate is Diagonal conjugate.

533.q: Feto maternal transfusion is detected by:
533.e: Kleihauer-Betke test It is performed on maternal blood to assess the amount of fetomaternal bleed. In order to calculate the dose of Anti-D prophylaxis required. Principle: HbF is more resistant to acid elution than HbA. The maternal blood is subjected to an acid solution (citric acid phosphate buffer). Acid will elute the adult hemoglobins but not the fetal haemoglobin from the red cells. Hence, the fetal red cells appear stained dark red, unlike the light-coloured maternal red cells or ghost cells. The number of fetal red cells in 50 low power fields is assessed. Also Know Indirect Coombs test - detects antibodies in maternal serum. Direct Coombs test - detects antibodies in fetus/neonate. Reference : Dutta Obs. 7/e, pg 334, Sheila Balakrishnan Textbook of Obs 1/e, pg 368.

533.q: Consequence of maternal use of cocaine is:
533.e: It can lead to the following Malformations in the fetus: Microcephaly, cutis aplasia, porencephaly, subependymal and periventricular cysts, ileal atresia, cardiac anomalies, visceral infarcts, limb reduction defects and genitourinary malformations. It produces cerebral infarction and periventricular leukomalacia in the fetus. The risk of malformations in the embryo/fetus is highest after the first trimester. Reference : Sheila Balakrishnan, pg 696; Williams Obs. 22/e, pg 364, 23/e, pg 326, 327

533.q: The foetal blood is separated from syncytiotropho- blast with all except:
533.e: The maternal blood in the lacuna is never in direct contact with fetal blood. They are separated by: Syncytiotrophoblast Cytotrophoblast Basement membrane Together called as placental barrier or membrane (0.025 mm) Mesoderm Endothelium of fetal capillaries Reference: IB Singh, Embryology, p 66, 67

533.q: What is approx fetal weight, if height of uterus is above pubic symphysis is 35 cm and station of head is +2?
533.e: Estimation of fetal weight can be done using Johnson formula: If station of head below ischial spine [Height of uterus above pubic symphysis (in cm) - 11] × 155 If fetal head is at or above ischial spine- [Height of uterus above pubic symphysis (in cm) - 12] × 155 Here fetal head is at + 2, i.e., above ischial spine, so it will be (35 - 12) × 155 = 3.5 kg. Reference: Dutta Obs. 8/e, p 84

533.q: The prerequisites for internal rotation of the head are all except:
533.e: Factors facilitating descent are: (1) uterine contraction and retraction, (2) bearing down efforts and (3) straightening of the fetal ovoid specially after rupture of the membranes. Reference : Dutta Obs. 7/e, pg 125

533.q: All of the following are true about anencephaly except:
533.e: Anencephaly is characterized by absence of the cranium and telencephalic structures, with the skull base and orbits covered only by angiomatous stroma. Acrania is the absence of the cranium, with protrusion of disorganized brain tissue. Both are generally grouped together, and anencephaly is considered to be the final stage of acrania. Reference: Fernando Arias 3/e, p 64; Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 408, 409

534.q: Head is at what station when it is engaged?
534.e: Engagement of head rules out CPD at the level of pelvic inlet. If the head is engaged, it means the head is at ‘O’ station. Engagement can be: When sagittal suture of the head of fetus lies in the transverse diameter of pelvic inlet (midway between the pubic symphysis and the sacral promontory) It occurs in 25% cases It occurs commonly in nulliparous women. Causes of nonengagement of head in a nullipara at term: Malpresentations / Occipito Posterior position/deflexed head Cephalopelvic disproportion Placenta previa / Tumors in the lower segment Tumours of the fetal neck/Cord around the neck / Hydrocephalus Polyhydramnios Distended bladder and rectum. Reference : Dutta Obs. 7/e, pg 81, 82, 352

534.q: Most common cause of retained placenta is
534.e: Causes behind retained placenta: Placenta completely separated but retained is due to poor voluntary expulsive efforts. The commonest cause of retention of non-separated placenta is atonic uterus. Morbidly adherent placenta—partial or rarely, complete. Placenta incarcerated following partial or complete separation due to constriction ring (hourglass contraction), premature attempts to deliver the placenta before it is separated. Reference: D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 28

534.q: Granulosa cells produces estrogen with the help of the enzyme:
534.e: Estrogen produced by theca cells is converted to androgens in granulosa cells with the help of enzyme aromatase. Source Granulosa cells (E2 ) Theca cells (E1 ) (produce androgens which are converted to estrogen by enzyme aromatase in adipose tissue) Placenta-(with the help of precursors obtained from fetus) (E3) Corpus luteum (E2 ) Ref. Dutta Gynae 6th/ed p 72

534.q: Management of retained unseparated placenta is:
534.e: Management of retained placenta: Placenta is separated and retained: expell the placenta out by controlled cord traction. Unseparated retained placenta: Manual removal of placenta is to be done under general anaesthesia. Reference: D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 28

534.q: In non-immune hydrops which of the following is NOT seen:
534.e: "Hydrops is characterized by excess fluid in two or more body areas such as thorax, abdomen or skin. It is often associated with hydramnios and a hydropic thickened placenta". It is characterised by: Increased skin thickness (> 5 mm) / skin oedema (first sign seen on USG). Placental enlargement Pleural effusion Ascites The fetus is in Buddha position with a halo around the head. Reference : Williams 23/e, pg 626

534.q: Following hormones secreted by placenta exclusively:
534.e: The question says - hormones produced by placenta exclusively therefore we cannot include - estrogen which is produced by placenta but not exclusively because the precursors for synthesis of estrogen are made available to the placenta by the fetal adrenal cortex,without which it cannot synthesise estrogen: Reference: Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 58; Williams Obs. 23/e, p 62, 63

534.q: Which of the following statements is true regarding inversion of the uterus?
o: Inversion can be induced but in most cases it is spontaneous
Always occur with placenta in situ
Acute inversion can go in chronic one if left untreated
534.e: (A) Inversion can be induced but in most cases it is spontaneous: This statement is misleading; while inversion can occur spontaneously, but more commonly it is induced-Most common cause is mismanagement of third stage of labour. (B) Always occurs with placenta in situ: This is not true; inversion can occur with or without the placenta attached. (C) Acute inversion can indeed progress to chronic inversion if not treated, making this the correct statement. Reference: D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 28

534.q: A 30-year-old patient delivered in the labour room after spontaneous labour. Delivery was uneventful, patient vitally stable, uterus well contracted but after delivery placenta didn't expelled spontaneously. Diagnosis of retained placenta was made and she was taken in OT for manual removal of placenta under GA. During the procedure the plane of cleavage couldn't be made out between placenta and uterine wall. What is the most likely diagnosis?
534.e: During attempted manual removal if no cleavage between the placenta and the uterine wall is made out, diagnosis of a total placenta accreta is certain. Endometritis is a remote complication of retained placenta. Reference: D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 28

535.q: Where is the SRY region located in the body?
535.e: Explanation: The SRY gene/region is the sex-determining gene/region located on the distal region of the short arm of the Y chromosome . It has a significant role in determining male sex and expresses at the 5th to 6th week of development. In XX karyotype the absence of this gene expression leads to ovarian development. Mutation of the SRY gene leads to Swyer syndrome. Patients with Swyer syndrome have a 46XY karyotype , but their Mullerian system develops normally. These individuals are phenotypically female with both female external and internal genitalia. Their gonads are usually streak ovaries composed only of gonadal stroma, while the vagina, uterus, and fallopian tubes are all formed. Reference: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8840551/#:~:text=Abstract,testis%20from%20an%20undifferentiated%20gonad.

535.q: In cases of gonadal sex reversal syndrome with an XX karyotype, what is the most common underlying cause?
535.e: Explanation: In gonadal sex reversal syndrome with an XX karyotype, the most common cause is a translocation . Translocation is the rearrangement of chromosomal material between non-homologous chromosomes. Sex reversal syndrome, also known as disorder of sex development (DSD), arises when an individual's chromosomal, gonadal, and phenotypic sex do not align. In gonadal sex reversal syndrome with an XX karyotype, a translocation involving the SRY (Sex-determining Region Y) gene can cause the gene to be present on an X chromosome. Because the SRY gene initiates male development, its translocation to the X chromosome can cause individuals with an XX karyotype to develop testes rather than ovaries. Reference: https://afju.springeropen.com/articles/10.1186/s12301-021-00210-5

535.q: In Precocious puberty age limit of girls is-
535.e: Answer- A.�8 year Precocious puberty�in a girl is the appearance of any of the secondary sexual characteristics before the age of 8 years or the occurrence of menarche before the age of 10 years. Precocious puberty�in boys is the onset of secondary sexual characteristics before the age of nine years.�

535.q: Which of the following statements is not true regarding bartholin gland?
o: It is situated in superficial perineal pouch
Bartholin's gland is about 2 cm and duct measures 0.5 cm
Bartholin duct is lined by columnar epithelium
It secrets mucus which is alkaline in nature
535.e: Bartholin’s gland is situated in the superficial perineal pouch and measures about 0.5 cm. The duct measures 2 cm. The gland is compound racemose and lined by columnar epithelium. During sexual excitement, it secretes abundant alkaline mucus which helps in lubrication. Duct opens outside the hymen at the junction of the anterior two-third and posterior one-third in the groove between the hymen and the labium minus. The duct is lined by columnar epithelium except near the opening, where it is lined by stratified squamous epithelium. The Bartholin’s gland corresponds to the bulbourethral gland of male. Reference: D C Dutta’s textbook of gynecology, 7th edition, chapter 1

535.q: All of the following take part in male genital tract development except:
535.e: Genes for male development SRY gene-Master Gene for testis development SOX 9-SRY & SOX 9 induce testis to form FGF-9 (chemotactic factor) FGF-9 causes tubules from mesonephric duct to penetrate gonadal ridge SF1 (steroidogenic factor)-It stimulates differentiation of sertole or leydig cells WNT-4 is an ovary-determining gene. This gene upregulates DAXI-which inhibits the fraction of SOX 9 in females. Reference: Langman embryology 12/e, pg. 246-247

535.q: What is the cause for luteal phase defect?
535.e: Luteal Phase Defect During normal luteal phase, when there is adequate progesterone secretion by the corpus luteum, adequate development of secretory endometrium occurs for blastocyst implantation. Luteal phase defect refers to a condition when production of progesterone is suboptimal by corpus luteum. Inadequate progesterone secretion could be due to: Inadequate follicular development Inadequate FSH or LH secretion Hyperprolactinemia Reference: Novak 14 th /ed p 1225, 15 th /ed p 1161

535.q: With respect to embryological development which of the following structures has dual origin
535.e: Vagina has dual origin Upper 2/3 → from fused mullerian duct Distal 1/3 → from bilateral sinovaginal bulbs , which are cranial evaginations of the urogenital sinus. Junction of these two is called vaginal plate (forms hymen) Reference: williams obstetrics 26th edition chapter 3

535.q: GnRH analogue may be given in all of the following except:
535.e: Indications for using Synthetic GnRH In females: (In all those conditions where there is increased estrogen, GnRH analogues are useful). In males: Cryptorchidism: short-term intranasal nafarelin is used. Carcinoma prostate: GnRH agonists are as effective as orchidectomy in Ca prostate but if there are neurological symptoms or life-threatening metastatic disease - androgens should first be started followed by GnRH agonist. BPH: Daily administration of leuprorelin or nafarelin decreases obstructive urinary symptoms in 1-6 monthstime. Reference: Jeffcoate 7 th /ed p 652

536.q: Quickening" or the period when fetal movements are commonly first felt by the mother occurs:
o: Near the end of the first trimester
Around the middle of the second trimester
At the end of the second trimester
At the end of the embryonic period
536.e: Although reflexive fetal movements begin at the end of the first trimester, they typically cannot be felt until the fifth month of pregnancy. At the end of the fetal period, there is much movement, all of it extra-uterine. Reference - Textbook of Langman's, 12th Edition, General Embryology Page number - 51

536.q: 35 weeks pregnant diabetic female with NST non- reactive. What should be done next?
536.e: In the case of a 35-week pregnant diabetic female with a non-reactive non-stress test (NST), the next step should be (D) proceed to biophysical profile. This helps further assess fetal well being before deciding on intervention. Biophysical Profile (BPP): This test combines an NST with an ultrasound assessment to evaluate several aspects of fetal health. The BPP assesses: Fetal Heart Rate (NST component): Evaluates heart rate patterns. Fetal Breathing Movements: Checks for episodes of breathing. Fetal Movement: Assesses general body movements. Fetal Tone: Looks for muscle tone and flexion of the limbs. Amniotic Fluid Volume: Measures the amount of amniotic fluid. Reference: Management of High Risk Pregnancy, Manjupuri, SS Trivedi, p 62

536.q: A pregnant female has cramps in her legs. What will you suggest to relieve the pain?
o: Extend knee and dorsiflex the foot
Flex knee and dorsiflex the foot
Extend knee and plantar flex the foot
Flex knee and plantar flex the foot
536.e: Why do pregnant ladies get leg cramps? It may have to do with changes in blood circulation and stress on your leg muscles from carrying extra weight. Your growing baby also puts pressure on the nerves and blood vessels that go to your legs. And some doctors say low calcium, or a change in the way your body processes calcium, may cause cramps If you get a leg cramp, stretch the calf muscle. Walking and then sitting and raising your legs might help keep the leg cramp from coming back. A hot shower, warm bath, ice massage or muscle massage may help too. Reference: https://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/pregnancy-week-by-week/expert-answers/leg-cramps-during-pregnancy/faq-20057766#:~:text=Leg%20cramps%20are%20painful%20muscle,take%20steps%20to%20prevent%20them.

536.q: G2P1 woman at 35 weeks pregnancy complains of decreased fetal movement. Next step in Mgt is:
536.e: In a woman at 35 weeks of pregnancy (AG2P) who complains of decreased fetal movement, the next step in management is (B) do NST (Non-Stress Test). This test helps assess fetal well-being by monitoring heart rate patterns in response to movement. If the NST is non-reactive, further evaluation such as a biophysical profile (BPP) may be considered Reference: Williams Obs. 23/e, p 339

536.q: Pregnancy is confirmed by all except
536.e: Positive or absolute signs of pregnancy: Palpation of fetal parts and perception of fetal movements by examiner, at about 20 weeks. Auscultation of fetal heart sounds. USG evidence of embryo (at 6th week) and later on of the fetus. Radiological demonstration of fetal skeleton at 16 weeks and onwards. Friends there is no need to mug up the presumptive/probable signs of pregnancy. Generally it is not asked in exams. Also remember: These positive or absolute signs of pregnancy are never seen in pseudocyesis or phantom pregnancy. Reference: Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 72

536.q: In which of the following heart diseases is maternal mortality during pregnancy found to be the highest:
536.e: Eisenmenger's syndrome is the presence of secondary pulmonary hypertension that develops from any cardiac lesion. The syndrome develops when increased pulmonary blood flow due to left to right shunt produces a right side pressure more than the left side and hence reversal of shunt occurs and subsequently cyanosis develops. It is the heart disease with the worst prognosis during pregnancy with a maternal mortality of 50%. Hence, pregnancy is contraindicated in patients of eisenmengers. If diagnosis of Eisenmenger is made in the first trimester, termination of pregnancy is advised. Most common cause of death in Eisenmenger's syndrome is right ventricular failure with cardiogenic shock. Reference: Williams Obs. 22/e, p 1028, 23/e, p 970; Sheila Balakrishnan, p 283

536.q: 6 year old son of pregnant women is suffering from chicken pox. Which of the following is given to pregnant women ?
536.e: Ans. B. Acyclovir + immunoglobulin Varicella during pregnancy The risk of congenital malformations is nearly absent when maternal infection occurs after 20 weeks. VariceIa vaccine is not recommended in pregnancy. Varicella zoster immunoglobulin (VZIG) should be given to exposed non-immune as it reduces the mortality. Oral acyclovir is safe in pregnancy & reduces the duration of illness when given with in 24 hrs of rash but it cannot prevent congenital infection.

536.q: Dorsal lithotomy position contributes to hasten second stage of labour by which of the following methods
o: Increase in outlet diameter by 0.2 to 0.5 cm
Reducing diagonal conjugate by 1 to 1.5 cm
536.e: Pelvic joints have a limited degree of mobility but can relax remarkably during pregnancy. At term, the sacroiliac joint can glide upward. This is greatest in dorsal lithotomy position and may increase the diameter of the outlet by 1.5 to 2.0 cm for delivery. Sacroiliac joint mobility also likely aids the McRoberts maneuver to release an obstructed shoulder in cases of shoulder dystocia. These changes may also contribute to the success of the modified squatting position to hasten second-stage labor. Squatting may increase the interspinous diameter and the pelvic outlet diameter. Reference: williams obstetrics 26th edition chapter 2

537.q: A 22-year-old female with history of multiple contacts presenting with growth on vulva, the probable diagnosis is:
537.e: History of sexual exposure and growths on vulva is consistent with condyloma accuminata. Condylomata acuminata (singular: condyloma acuminatum) refers to anogenital warts caused by human papillomavirus (HPV). The most common strains of HPV that cause anogenital warts are 6 and 11 Condyloma accuminata : Warts are common in the regions affected most directly by coitus i.e. posterior fourchette and lateral areas of vulva. These verrucous growths may coalesce to form large cauliflower growths. Condyloma is associated with vulval, vaginal, and cervical cancers. Reference: Shaw 15th/ed pp 138, 139

537.q: Appropriate material for antenatal diagnosis of genetic disorders includes all of the following except:
537.e: Prenatal genetic diagnosis can be made by: Method Chorionic villus sampling Cordocentesis Amniocentesis Reference: Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 106, 07

537.q: In which of the following heart diseases maternal mortality is found to be highest?
537.e: Eisenmenger's syndrome is the presence of secondary pulmonary hypertension that develops from any cardiac lesion. The syndrome develops when increased pulmonary blood flow due to left to right shunt produces a right side pressure more than the left side and hence reversal of shunt occurs and subsequently cyanosis develops. It is the heart disease with the worst prognosis during pregnancy with a maternal mortality of 50%. Hence, pregnancy is contraindicated in patients of eisenmengers. If diagnosis of Eisenmenger is made in the first trimester, termination of pregnancy is advised. Most common cause of death in Eisenmenger's syndrome is right ventricular failure with cardiogenic shock. Reference: Williams Obs. 22/e, p 1028, 23/e, p 970; Sheila Balakrishnan, p 283

537.q: A 25 year old primigravida with a 10 week pregnancy patient comes to an antenatal clinic complaining of an increase in urinary frequency, which of the following can cause increased urinary frequency in pregnancy?
o: Failure of retroversion of gravid uterus
537.e: Frequency of micturition is quite a troublesome symptom during 8-12th weeks of pregnancy. It is due to Resting of the bulky uterus on the fundus of the bladder because of exaggerated anteverted position of the uterus, Congestion of the bladder mucosa and Change in maternal osmoregulation causing increased thirst and polyuria. As the uterus straightens up after the 12th week, the symptoms disappear. Reference: DC Dutta textbook of obstetrics, 8th edition; chapter 7
Reference: Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 99; SPM Park 19/e, p 417, 20/e, p 450

537.q: Peak in cardiac output antenatally occurs at
537.e: Cardiac output increases significantly during pregnancy to meet the increased metabolic demands of both the mother and the developing fetus. This increase begins early in pregnancy and peaks around 28-30weeks gestation. During this time, the volume of blood returning to the heart (venous return) increases due to increased blood volume and the effect of the growing uterus on venous return. Additionally, the cardiac output is supported by elevated heart rate and stroke volume. After reaching its peak around 28-30 weeks, cardiac output may slightly decline as the pregnancy approaches term, but it generally remains elevated compared to pre-pregnancy levels Reference : Arias 5 th edition pg no 177

537.q: Levels of progesterone indicate unviable pregnancy and viable intrauterine pregnancy are:
537.e: Serum progesterone concentration Reference: Williams 24/e, p 355

537.q: Which of the following tests is not used for diagnosis of rupture of membrane?
537.e: Confirmation of PROM: (1) Speculum examination is done taking aseptic precautions to inspect the liquor escaping out through the cervix; (2) To examine the collected fluid from the posterior fornix (vaginal pool) for: (a) Detection of pH by litmus or Nitrazine paper. The pH becomes 6–6.2 (Normal vaginal pH during pregnancy is 4.5–5.5 whereas that of liquor amnii is 7–7.5). Nitrazine paper turns from yellow to blue at pH > 6; (b) To note the characteristic ferning pattern when a smeared slide is examined under microscope; (c) Centrifuged cells stained with 0.1% Nile blue sulfate showing orange blue coloration of the cells (exfoliated fat containing cells from sebaceous glands of the fetus); (3) AmniSure—A rapid immunoassay is accurate; (4) Ultrasonography Reference : D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 22

538.q: In 46 XX female on doing amniocentesis complete gonadal dysgenesis was noted. Complete gonadal dysgenesis is caused by what in the SRY gene?
538.e: Complete gonadal dysgenesis is also known as SWYER SYNDROME. In this approximately 15-20% of patients, the disorder results from an inactivating point mutation in SRY gene, but in most cases cause is not known. (Deletion in SRY gene's DNA binding region 2 is present in 10-20 % of women)

538.q: Best method of induction of labour in hydramnios:
o: Abdominal amniocentesis followed by stabilizing oxytocin drip
538.e: Artificial rupture of membranes is C/I in polyhydramnios as it leads to sudden decompression of the uterus which can cause abruptio placenta. Method of induction in these patients is: low rupture of the membranes is done when the lie becomes stable and the presenting part gets fixed to the pelvis. This will minimize sudden decompression with separation of the placenta, change in lie of the fetus and cord prolapse. a stabilizing oxytocin infusion is started to check the favorable lie and presentation of the fetus drainage of good amount of liquor Amniocentesis Reference : Dutta Obs 7/e, pg 215
Answer- C. ANC USG Nuchal translucency is used for screening of down syndrome in antenatal USG.

538.q: Early date for detection of fetal heart:
538.e: Embryonic investigations suggest that cardiac contractions begin in the fetus at 36 days gestational age.' Cardiac activity should be detected routinely when the embryo attains a length of 4 to 5 mm. This corresponds to a GA of 6.0 to 6.5 weeks, at which time the MSD is 13 to 18 mm. Using a transabdominal approach, cardiac activity should be evident by 8 weeks GA, when the MSD is 25 mm.' Reference: USG in Obs. and Gynae. Callen 4/e, p 119, 120

538.q: Anita, 14-year-old, complains of heavy periods for 2 months. O/E: wt 40 kg and BP 120/80 mmHg. All of the following investigations are indicated, except:
538.e: Important causes of puberty menorrhagia are: HPO axis immaturity (anovulation) Bleeding disorders Endocrinological causes Hence TSH, platelet count and BT/CT are done S. estradiol levels are of no utility in the workup of this patient. Note: Always rule out bleeding disorder in patients of puberty menorrhagia Reference : Dutta Gynae 6 th /ed, pg no: 55

539.q: A patient presents for her first initial antenatal visit after performing a home pregnancy test and gives a last menstrual period of about 8 weeks ago. She says she is not entirely sure of her dates, however because she has a long history of irregular menses. Which of the following is the most accurate way of dating the pregnancy?
o: Determination of uterine size on pelvic examination
Crown rump length on abdominal or vaginal examination
Determination of progesterone level along with serum hCG level
539.e: The most accurate way of dating the pregnancy in first trimester would be (C): Crown rump length on abdominal or vaginal examination. This method is more reliable than relying on the last menstrual period, especially in cases of irregular menstrual cycles. Crown rump length provides a more precise estimation of gestational age based on the measurement from the top of the baby's head to its bottom. Reference: Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 106

539.q: A patient presents for her first initial OB visit after performing a home pregnancy test and gives a last menstrual period of about 8 weeks ago. She says she is not entirely sure of her dates, however because she has a long history of irregular menses. Which of the following is the most accurate way of dating the pregnancy?
o: Determination of uterine size on pelvic examination
Crown rump length on abdominal or vaginal examination
Determination of progesterone level along with serum hCG level
539.e: The most accurate way of dating the pregnancy in first trimester would be (C): Crown rump length on abdominal or vaginal examination. This method is more reliable than relying on the last menstrual period, especially in cases of irregular menstrual cycles. Crown rump length provides a more precise estimation of gestational age based on the measurement from the top of the baby's head to its bottom. Reference: Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 106

539.q: A P2 + 1 female comes with amenorrhea of 5 weeks. Her UPT is +ve. On USG, Gestational and yolk sacs are seen in the uterus. No fetal pole is visible. No fetal cardiac activity is seen. CRL is 8 mm and MSD = 28 mm. What is the next best step?
o: Advise MTP as it is nonviable pregnancy
High probability of nonviable pregnancy- but still repeat scan after 7 days to confirm
Can be ectopic pregnancy - give methotrexate
High probability of viable pregnancy-repeat scan after 7 days
539.e: An embryonic gestation is diagnosed when the mean gestational sac diameter measures 25 mm and no embryo is seen. Embryonic death is also diagnosed if an embryo measuring 7 mm has no cardiac activity. So in the question – MSD is 28 mm and CRL 8 mm and still no cardiac activity or fetal pole is visible. It has to be a nonviable pregnancy. In this case whether we should perform immediate MTP or repeat scan after 7 days is suggested by High Risk Pregnancy 4/e, p 108. If fetal pole is not seen and MSD 25 mm then there is high probability of a non viable pregnancy. Repeat scan with another examiner or after 7 days to confirm. If a fetal pole is seen then measure CRL. If CRL 7 mm there is a high probability of nonviable pregnancy. Repeat scan should be done after 7 days to confirm. Reference: Williams 24/e, p 355

540.q: A hypertensive pregnant woman at 34 weeks comes with history of pain in abdomen, bleeding per vaginum and loss of fetal movements. On examination the uterus is contracted with increased uterine tone. Fetal heart sounds are absent. The most likely diagnosis is:
540.e: The patient in the question is hypertensive and presenting with: History of pain in abdomen. Bleeding per vaginum. Loss of fetal movements. O/E = uterus is contracted. Increased uterine tone. Fetal heart sounds are absent. All these features confirm the diagnosis of abruptio placenta . As far as premature labour is concerned – Complaints of abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding will be present but loss of fetal movement, absence of fetal heart sounds and increased uterine tone go against it. (In normal labour - uterus contracts and relaxes intermittently i.e. tone increases and decreases intermittently). Reference: Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 255

540.q: A 29-year-old primigravida patient with and uncomplicated pregnancy undergoes spontaneous labour during second stage of labour she was given right mediolateral episiotomy to enlarge vaginal opening after delivery obstetrician notices extension of episiotomy laceration in mucosa with intact anal sphincter, degree of perineal tear in this patient will be classified as:
540.e: Classification of Obstetric Anal Sphincter Injury (RCOG–2007) First degree: Injury to perineal skin only Second degree: Injury to perineum involving perineal body (muscles) but not involving the anal sphincter- episiotomy Third degree: Injury to perineum, involving the anal sphincter complex (both external and internal) 3a : 3b : >50% of EAS thickness torn 3c : Both EAS and IAS torn Fourth degree: Injury to perineum involving the anal sphincter complex (EAS and IAS) and anal epithelium Reference: Shaw's textbook of gynecology, 16th edition, chapter 1(figure 1.12,A)

540.q: Which cardinal movements occur during labour?
540.e: Series of events that take place in the genital organs in an effort to expel the viable products of conception out of the womb through the vagina into the outer world is called Labour . Mechanism of normal labour is defined as the manner in which the fetus adjusts itself to pass through the parturient canal with minimal difficulty. There are 8 cardinal movements of the head in normal labour. E very – E ngagement (Synclitic or Asynclitic) D ecent – D escent F emale – F lexion I – I nternal rotation C hoose to – C rowning E mploy – E xtension R ises – R estitution E xtremely – E xternal rotation Mnemonic : Every Decent Female I Choose to and Employ Rises Extremely. Reference : Dutta Obs. 7/e, pg 128

540.q: Vas deferens and seminal vesicles are absent in:
540.e: CBAVD(Congenital bilateral absence of seminal vesicles and vas deferens) is seen in Cystic fibrosis and is a cause of post testicular/obstructive azoospermia and absence of fructose in semen . Typical hormone testing reveals: Normal FSH, LH, Testosterone levels The next step of evaluation is genetic analysis for CFTR gene. Other options are not related.

540.q: pH of vagina in pregnant woman is usually ?
540.e: Ans. A. 4.0 The vaginal acidity is due to lactic acid. The normal pH in the healthy women of the child bearing age group is 4.5

540.q: Which of the following is untrue regarding piebaldism?
o: amelanotic skin associated with a white forelock
Islands of normal or hypermelanotic skin
540.e: Ans. D. Usually improves with age Piebaldism Piebaldism is a rare autosomal dominant condition characterized by stable areas of vitiligo-like amelanotic skin associated with a white forelock. Present at birth and usually remain unchanged throughout life. Most common is a frontal median or paramedian patch, associated with a mesh of white hair (white Forelock). Often, white patches occur on the upper chest, abdomen and limbs, bilaterally but not necessarily symmetrically The hands and feet, as well as the back, remain normally pigmented Islands of normal or hypermelanotic skin occur in the white areas, or less often on normal skin.

540.q: All are the criteria for normal labour except:
540.e: The correct answer is (D): Vacuum delivery. Normal labor is characterized by being spontaneous, vertex presentation, and occurring without maternal or fetal complications. Vacuum delivery is an assisted delivery method and does not fit the criteria for normal labor. Normal Labor (EUTOCIA): Labor is called normal if it fulfills the following criteria. (1) Spontaneous in onset and at term. (2) With vertex presentation. (3) Without undue prolongation. (4) Natural termination with minimal aids. (5) Without having any complications affecting the health of the mother and/or the baby. Abnormal Labor (DYSTOCIA): Any deviation from the definition of normal labor is called Abnormal labor. Reference : Dutta Obs. 7/e, pg 113

540.q: Perineal infiltration with local anesthesia is most commonly used in:
540.e: Remember: Perineal infiltration with local anesthesia is most commonly used in (C) Episiotomy repair. This technique helps manage pain during the repair of episiotomy. Reference : Dutta Obs 7/e, pg 517-518 and William 23/e, pg 450

541.q: A 26-year-old pregnant woman is referred by her obstetrician for evaluation of anemia. This woman has macrocytic anemia, an increased serum concentration of transferrin, and a normal serum concentration of vitamin B12, the most likely cause of her anemia is deficiency of which of the following?
541.e: Deficiencies of folic acid or vitamin B12 are the most common causes of megaloblastic anemia. If a patient with this type of anemia has a normal serum vitamin B12 concentration, folate deficiency is the most likely cause of the anemia. Reference: Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, Fourteenth Edition By Bertram G. Katzung Pg no. 844-45

541.q: Not a method for delivery of after- coming head of breech ?
541.e: Ans. D. Half hand method Methods of delivery of aftercoming head are Burns - Marshall method ForcePs delivery Malar flexion and shoulder traction (modified Mauriceau-Smellie-Veit technique)

541.q: A 22-year-old pregnant woman presents with dysuria and increased frequency. A urinary tract infection is diagnosed. What is the most appropriate step?
o: Treatment if the c-reactive protein(CRP) is high
Treatment if the erythrocyte sedimentation rate(ESR) is high
541.e: Infections in pregnancy should be treated, as 25% of patients will develop acute pyelonephritis. Nitrofurantoin, cephalosporins and beta lactams are safe in pregnancy. Reference: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 21 st ed, Ch: 135, Pg: 1077.

541.q: Which of the mentioned drugs is not ideal for treatment of UTI in pregnant women?
541.e: Nitrofurantoin, ampicillin, and the cephalosporins are considered relatively safe in early pregnancy. One retrospective case-control study suggesting an association between nitrofurantoin and birth defects has not been confirmed Reference: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 21 st ed, Ch: 135, Pg: 1077

541.q: Which of the following statements is TRUE? Asymptomatic bacteruria needs treatment in?
541.e: Asymptomatic bacteruria means the presence of bacteria and WBC in the urine in the absence of symptoms. Microbiological criteria is >10 5 CFU/mL of urine. It requires treatment in: Pregnancy Those undergoing urological procedure Neutropenic patients Renal transplant recepients. The last 2 are relative indications. Reference: Harrison's Principles of internal medicine, 21 st ed, Ch:135, Pg:1075-1077.

Shoulder dystocia Mc Roberts manoeuvre (most commonly performed/first performed manoeuvre) Wood's manoeuvre Zavanelli manoeuvre. Breech extraction Burns Marshall technique (for after coming head of Breech). Modified Mauriceau Smellie-Veit technique (Malar flexion and shoulder traction). Lovset's manoeuvre (for extended arms). Pinard's manoeuvre (for frank breech extraction). Reference: Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 406

541.q: Commonest cause of nonengagement at term, in primi is:
541.e: In primi's the most common cause of non engagement at term is a deflexed head or occipitoposterior position followed by cephalopelvic disproportion (CPD). Since deflexed head or occipitoposterior is not given in option, we will go for CPD as the answer Also know : Engagement is said to occur when the greatest transverse diameter of the presenting part, has passed through the pelvic inlet. In all cephalic presentations, the greatest transverse diameter is always the biparietal. Engagement occurs in multipara with commencement of labour 38 weeks in the late Ist stage after rupture of membranes and in Nullipara during the last few weeks of pregnancy Reference : Dutta Obs. 7/e, pg 81, 82, 352

541.q: In brow presentation, presenting diameter (s) is/are:
541.e: Brow Presentation: Engaging diameter – Mentovertical (14 cm). There is no mechanism of labour. Diagnosed on P/V by palpating supraorbital ridges and anterior fontanelle. Delivery is by cesarean section. Reference : Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 392

542.q: A female at 37 weeks of gestation has mild labour pains for 10 hours and cervix is persistently 1 cm dilated but non effaced. What will be the next appropriate management?
542.e: The patient in the question has been having mild labor pains for 10 hours with no change in cervical dilatation and effacement. But again the question does not specify whether she is having regular uterine contractions or not. False labor can be differentiated from latent phase of labor by therapeutic rest i.eThe patient is sedated with morphine. So the correct option is Sedate and Wait. As far as augmentation with oxytocin is concerned - it is done only in those patients who even after therapeutic rest continue to be in prolonged latent phase (once the diagnosis of lack of progress of latent phase is confirmed following therapeutic rest.) Amniotomy is not useful and should be avoided in patients in prolonged latent phase. Also, there is no indication of cesarean section in this case. Reference : Fernando Arias 3/e, pg 376

542.q: All of the following drugs are effective for cervical ripening during pregnancy except:
542.e: Ripening of the cervix is changing the cervical matrix from sol to gel state by dissolving the collagen bundles. Ultimately the cervix becomes soft. Techniques for cervical ripening: Pharmacological: Dinoprostone gel (PGE 2 ) - it is the gold standard for cervical ripening Misoprostol (PGE1) tablet - vaginal or oral Steroid receptor antagonist Mifepristone Oxytocin Non pharmacological: Stripping the membrane Mechanical dilators: Osmotic dilators Balloon catheter/Transcervical catheter placed through internal os Extra-amniotic saline infusion Reference : Dutta Obs. 7/e, pg 524; Fernando Arias 3/e, pg 284-286; Williams Obs. 24/e, pg 525

o: To stop excess bleeding from uterus
542.e: Ans, C. To stop excess bleeding from uterus Methergin (methyl-ergo-novine) is a semisynthetic ergot derivative derived from lysergic acid. Indications Prophylactic:- Active management of 3rd stage of labour to prevent excess bleeding following delivery. Therapeutic:- To stop atonic uterine bleeding.

542.q: Which one of the following methods for induction of labour should not be used in patients with previous lower segment cesarean section?
542.e: Misoprostol It is an analogue of Prostaglandin E 1 . Indications: Medical abortion in the first trimester of pregnancy. Evacuation of uterus in case of anembryonic pregnancies or early fetal demise. Ripening of cervix prior to second trimester abortions. Ripening of cervix and induction of labour in term pregnancies. For treatment and prevention of postpartum bleeding. Pharmacokinetics: It is available in tablet form. Metabolized in the liver. Complication: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea. Uterine hyperstimulation. Contraindication: Women with previous uterine surgery particularly cesarean section. Reference : Dutta Obs. 7/e, pg 524; Fernando Arias 3/e, pg 286

542.q: Which of the following is a risk factor for atonic uterus?
542.e: Predisposing conditions: History of PPH Grand multipara Over distension of uterus: multiple pregnancy, polyhydramnios, big baby Malnutrition and anaemia APH Prolonged labour, induction/augmentation with oxytocin, precipitate labor Malformation of uterus, uterine fibroid Mismanaged 3 rd stage of labour Age>40 years, BMI> 35 Use of tocolytic drugs Reference: D C Dutta's textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 28

542.q: Which of the following is an indication for induction of labor?
542.e: After completing 42 weeks, labor induction is recommended to help avoid morbidity and mortality. Reference: Williams obstetrics 26 th edition, chapter 46

542.q: Management of PROM at 35 weeks of gestation:
o: Allow to go in spontaneous labor
542.e: PROM ≥ 34 weeks and Wait for spontaneous onset of labor for 24 to 48 hr If fails induction of labor Reference : D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 22

542.q: A 34 year old G2P1 comes to the labor room at 38 weeks of gestation with rupture of membrane, she denies having pain. Ideal management for her would be:
o: Steroid and allow to go in spontaneous labor
542.e: Rupture of membrane after 37 weeks Wait for spontaneous labor till 24 he if fails induction of labor Tocolysis, steroid, cerclage not recommended Reference : D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 22

543.q: Which of the following structures is attached at cervicovaginal junction
543.e: Pelvic cellular tissue around the vaginalvault, supravaginal part of the cervix and into the layers of the broad ligament is called parametrium. Condensation occurs especially near the cervicovaginal junction to form ligaments which extend from the viscera to the pelvic walls on either side. These are Mackenrodt’s ligaments/ cardinal ligament, uterosacral ligaments and vesicocervical ligaments (fascia). All these constitute important supports of the uterus to keep it in position. Reference: DC Dutta textbook of obstetrics, 8th edition; chapter 1

543.q: All are seen with scar dehiscence, except:
543.e: All are seen with scar dehiscence, except (A) Maternal bradycardia. Maternal bradycardia is not typically associated with scar dehiscence; the other options, such as fetal bradycardia, vaginal bleeding, and hematuria, can occur. Uterine rupture typically is classified as either complete (all layers of the uterine wall separated) or incomplete (uterine muscle separated but visceral peritoneum is intact). Incomplete rupture is commonly referred to as scar dehiscence. Scar dehiscence is an intraoperative finding always. The greatest risk factor for either complete or incomplete uterine rupture is prior cesarean delivery. "The most common sign of uterine rupture is a non-reassuring fetal heart rate pattern with variable deceleration evolving into late decelerations, bradycardia and undetectable fetal heart rate pattern". Reference: John Hopkins Manual of Obs. and Gynae 4/e, p 86

543.q: The only disadvantage of active management of IIIrd stage of labor is:
543.e: In this method the placenta separation is actively facilitated and powerful uterine contractions are initiated to reduce the incidence of third stage complications (like PPH) Duration is reduced to 5 mins so less bleeding, less chances of PPH and less maternal mortality Active management of labor includes Administration of a uterotonic soon after birth of baby Delayed cord clamping Delivery of placenta by controlled cord traction Uterine message The only drawback of active management of 3rd stage of labor is , since uterotonic agent is given at the delivery of shoulder before the delivery placenta, it can lead to increased chances of Retained placenta. Reference : Williams 24/e, pg 513

543.q: A 30-year-old primigravida patient delivered vaginally after a spontaneous labor. After delivery placenta did not deliver spontaneously so the obstetrician attempted controlled cord traction. During the procedure the obstetrician noticed a pear shaped mass protruding outside with a broad base pointing downwards and placenta attached to it. The next best step in management of such patient:
o: Removal of placenta followed by repositioning of uterus
Attempt to reposition uterus with placenta in situ
543.e: This is a case of uterine inversion If the placenta is still attached, attempts are made to reposition the uterus with the placenta in situ. In theory, the uterus contracts to a lesser degree and placenta-site blood loss is less with an attached placenta. Reference: Williams obstetrics 26 th edition, chapter 42

543.q: M/C nerve injured during a normal vaginal delivery is:
543.e: M/C nerve injured during vaginal delivery - Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve followed by femoral nerve. Risk factors: Nulliparity, prolonged second stage of labor, pushing for a longer period in semi fowler position. M/C nerves injured during cesarean section - Iliohypogastric nerve and Ilioinguinal nerve. Reference: Williams Obstetrics, 24th Edition, Page Number-677.

543.q: Lady with MS + MR with full term gestation, obstetrician planning to conduct normal delivery, what would be anesthesia of choice?
543.e: Pain relief is important for heart disease patients as pain can cause tachycardia, which in turn can cause cardiac failure. Epidural and spinal techniques are the most effective means of providing pain relief for labor. These are also known as regional techniques because pain relief is limited to a specific anatomical region. These modalities are also known as neuraxial techniques, since both the approaches involve administration of drugs that exert their effects in the axial portion of the CNS. Reference: Williams, 22/e, p 483

543.q: Role of lactobacilli in vaginal secretions
543.e: Ans., B. To maintain acidic pH The importance of Doderlein's bacillus is that its presence is associated with production of lactic acid contained in the vaigna and this acidity inhibits the growth of other organisms." Doderlein's bacillus is the only organism which will grow at the pH of 4-4.5 (normal pH of vagina).

543.q: An expectant mother feels quickening at:
543.e: Quickening (feeling of life) denotes the perception of active fetal movements by the woman. It is usually felt about the 18 th week, 2 weeks earlier in multiparous. Its appearance is a useful guide to calculate the expected date of delivery with reasonable accuracy. Reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics, 7th Edition, Page Number 68-72.

544.q: Which is responsible for fetal heart rate acceleration?
544.e: Explanation: Fetal heart rate acceleration is primarily mediated by the autonomic nervous system. Sympathetic stimulation (via noradrenaline) increases heart rate, especially during fetal movement or external stimuli. Parasympathetic (vagal) tone slows heart rate ; transient withdrawal of vagal activity can also cause accelerations. Fetal heart rate accelerations are considered a sign of fetal well-being and neurological integrity. Neither baroreceptors nor chemoreceptors play a primary role in causing accelerations, though they are involved in other fetal heart rate responses (Option A, B, D ruled out). Clinical episodes of acceleration often occur with fetal activity or stimulation, confirming autonomic system involvement. Reference: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8061630/ , http://www.perinatology.com/Fetal%20Monitoring/Intrapartum%20Monitoring.htm

544.q: Which of the following is false for vaginal anatomy in non pregnant state
o: Anterior and posterior walls are opposed together
It looks H shaped on sagittal section
Length of posterior wall is more than length of anterior wall
544.e: Vagina has got an anterior, a posterior and two lateral walls. The anterior and posterior walls are opposed together but the lateral walls are comparatively stiffer especially at its middle, as such, it looks “H” shaped on the transverse section. The length of the anterior wall is about 7 cm and that of the posterior wall is about 9 cm. Reference: DC Dutta textbook of obstetrics, 8th edition; chapter 1

544.q: A 39-year-old female with G6P3L3A2 came to OPD having full term pregnancy with previous 3 LSCS. She is diagnosed case of PAS. What will not be mentioned in the consent?
o: Chances of bowel injury due to PAS
Chances of bladder injury due to PAS
Chances of hysterectomy due to PAS
544.e: Placenta Accreta Spectrum(PAS) disorder has disastrous outcome for both mother and fetus. Chances of bowel injury are very rare It includes: Placenta A ccreta: Placenta A dherent to myometrium Placenta I ncreta: Placenta I nvading myometrium Placenta P ercreta: Placenta P erforating through myometrium Cause: Due to absence of Nitabuch's layer It should be terminated at tertiary care center. Complication of surgery for PAS includes: Long operative time Blood and blood product transfusion(Option D) Surgical complications like bladder injury(Option B) ICU admission Increased length of stay Management: Caesarean Hysterectomy(Option C)

544.q: A 30 years old lady presented with creamy white vaginal discharge with fishy odor, drug of choice is:
544.e: Creamy white discharge with fishy odor is characteristic of bacterial vaginosis (M/C cause Gardnerella) -Drug of choice for management of bacterial vaginosis/Gardnerella vaginitis is Metronidazole: Dose - 500 mg oral metronidazole is given twice daily for 7 days Alternatively, metronidazole gel (can be applied once daily for 5 days or clindamycin cream (2%) at bedtime for 5 days. Note: Treatment of male sexual partner is not required in bacterial vaginosis. In pregnancy : Bacterial vaginosis is associated with preterm birth and premature rupture of membranes. Treatment is reserved for symptomatic women who usually complain of fishy odor. DOC - Metronidazole (oral) in the 2nd and the 3rd trimester. Reference: Shaw 15th/ed p 131; William's Gynae 1st/ed p 51.

544.q: Which of the following is the most common site for uterine incision during cesarean delivery?
o: Just above the level of isthmus
In upper part of body of uterus
544.e: Most common site for uterine incision during cesarean is lower segment of uterus.(LSCS) The uterus is pear shaped and consists of two major but unequal parts. The upper, larger portion is the body or corpus, whereas the lower smaller cervix projects into the vagina. The isthmus is the union site of these two. It is limited above by the anatomical internal os and below by the histological internal os It is of special obstetrical significance because it forms the lower uterine segment during pregnancy. Reference: DC Dutta textbook of obstetrics, 8th edition; chapter 1

544.q: New born can be given breast milk after how much time following normal delivery?
544.e: Ans A. Half hour A healthy baby is put to the breast immediately or at most % to 1 hr following normal delivery. Following caesarean sections a period of 4-6 hours may be sufficient for the mother to feed her baby.

544.q: All of the following measures should be taken for prevention of uterine rupture except
o: Internal podalic version should never be done in obstructed labour
External cephalic version should not be done under GA
Vaginal delivery should never be attempted in case of previous LSCS
Forceps delivery for breech extraction should never be done in incompletely dilated cervix
544.e: The at-risk mothers, likely to rupture, should have mandatory hospital delivery. General anesthesia should not be used to give undue force in an external version. Judicious selection of cases with previous history of cesarean sections for vaginal delivery (VBAC) Judicious selection of cases and careful watch are mandatory during oxytocin infusion either for induction or augmentation of labor. Internal podalic version should never be done in obstructed labor as an alternative to destructive operation or cesarean delivery. Attempted forceps delivery or breech extraction through incompletely dilated cervix should be avoided. Destructive vaginal operations, Manual removal in morbidly adherent placenta—should be done by a senior person Reference: D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 29

544.q: A 24-year-old primigravida patient comes to ANC clinic at 32 weeks of gestation with complaints of abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. Her pulse is 100 bpm, BP 170/110 mmHg. Fundus reveals tenderness and FHS is 110 bpm. TVS shows no placental abnormality. Definitive management for this patient is:
544.e: Management options in abruption: (a) Immediate delivery (b) Management of complications if there is any (c) Expectant management (rare). Definitive treatment (immediate delivery): The patient is in labor: The labor is accelerated by low rupture of the membranes. Rupture of the membranes with escape of liquor amnii accelerates labor and it increases the uterine tone also. Oxytocin drip may be started to accelerate labor when needed. The patient is not in labor: Delivery either by (A) induction of labor or (B) caesarean section. Reference:-D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 19

545.q: Screening by using maternal serum alpha fetoproteins helps to detect all of the following except:
545.e: Some conditions associated with abnormal maternal serum alpha fetoprotein concentration. Elevated levels Error in dates Multifetal pregnancy Severe oligohydramnios Neural tube defects Pilonidal cysts Esophageal or intestinal obstruction (and atresia) Liver necrosis Cystic hygroma Sacrococcygeal teratoma Fetal death Abdominal wall defects: omphalocele gastroschisis Urinary obstruction Renal anomalies: polycystic kidney absent kidneys Congenital nephrosis Osteogenesis imperfecta Congenital skin defects Cloacal exstrophy Chorioangioma of placenta Low birth weight Placental abruption Placenta accreta Preeclampsia Improper adjustment for low maternal weight Maternal hepatoma or teratoma Low level G: G estational trophoblastic diseases O 2 : O verestimated gestational age, overweight mother A: Spontaneous a bortion T: T risomy (21 or 18) Reference: Williams Obs. 24/e, p 287

545.q: Obstetric shock Index (OSI) is calculated by:
o: Heart rate divided by Mean arterial pressure
Heart rate divided by Diastolic blood pressure
Heart rate divided by Systolic blood pressure
Heart rate divided by Pulmonary arterial pressure
545.e: Shock index (SI) refers to heart rate (HR) divided by systolic blood pressure (SBP). The normal value is 0.5–0.7. For obstetric shock index (OSI) normal value in pregnancy is 0.7–0.8. Increase in the pulse rate and a fall in systolic blood pressure that is seen with significant haemorrhage, results in an increase in the shock index. If it increases above 0.9–1.1, intensive resuscitation may be required. If OSI > 1 indicates massive blood obstetric haemorrhage that required blood transfusion. Reference:Arias practical guide to high risk pregnancy and delivery 4 th edition, chapter 23

545.q: A cesarean section was done in the previous pregnancy. All of the following would be indications for elective cesarean section except:
545.e: Some factors that influence a successful trial of labor in a woman with prior cesarean delivery Low risk Transverse incision prior vaginal delivery appropriate counseling sufficient personnel and equipment Favors success Teaching hospital white race spontaneous labor prior fetal malpresentation 1 or 2 prior transverse incision Nonrecurrent indication current preterm pregnancy Increase failure rate Single mother Increased maternal age Macrosomic fetus Obesity Breech Multifetal pregnancy Preeclampsia EGA > 40 weeks Low-vertical incision Unknown incision Labor induction Medical disease Multiple prior cesarean deliveries Education Short interdelivery interval Liability concerns High risk Classical or T incision Prior rupture Patient refusal Transfundal surgery Obstetrical contraindication, e.g. previa Inadequate facilities Reference : Williams 24/e, p 611

Some unique complications can rarely follow compression sutures Variations of uterine ischemic necrosis with peritonitis Rarely uterine wall defects or uterine cavity synechiae. Reference:Williams obstetrics 26 th edition, chapter 44

545.q: A pregnant lady has a history of delivering twins. If she is pregnant for the second time now, which of the following is her obstetric score?
545.e: Parity & Gravida Parity Is number of past pregnancies that have gone beyond period of viability i.e. 28 weeks gestation. Gravida Is the total number of pregnancies(past and present), a woman has had regardless of outcome. Living issue Number of living children In both cases, twins are counted as a single pregnancy As this pregnant woman delivered twins 4 years ago, her parity(P) is 1, gravida(G) is 2 and living issue(L) is 2 i.e G2P1L2

546.e: Ans, A. 14 days Menstrual regulation (lnduction/Aspiration) Aspiration of endometrial cavity within l4 days of missed period in a woman with previous normal cycle. Done as an OPD procedure. Helps to detect failed abortion, molar pregnancy or ectopic Pregnancy. Contraindicated in advanced pregnancy & in presence of local pelvic inflammation.

Laparoscopy is considered the "gold standard". While it is the most reliable aid to support the clinical diagnosis, it may not be feasible to do in all cases. It is reserved only in those cases in which differential diagnosis includes salpingitis, appendicitis or ectopic pregnancy. Nonresponding pelvic mass needs laparoscopic clarification. Hysteroscopy may also provide confirmatory evidence for salpingitis. "Fallopian tube culture can be obtained laparoscopically and recently the hysteroscopic approach has been introduced. The specimen is obtained during hysteroscopy with a cytobrush." Reference : Shaw 15th/ed pg 451; William's Gynae 1st/ed pg 74; Gynecology by Ostrzenski (Lippincott Williams 2001/ 282); Dutta Gynae 6th/ed pg 130

546.q: In which part of fallopian tube ectopic pregnancy will have longest survival:
546.e: M.C site of ectopic pregnancy – Fallopian tubes . In Fallopian Tubes – M/C sites in descending order are:Ampulla > isthmus > infundibulum > interstitium Rarest overall site of ectopic pregnancy is cervix or cesarean section scan Average period of survival of ectopic pregnancy is 8 weeks. Ectopic pregnancy survives for the longest time in its annual pregnancy. Reference: Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 179; CODGT 10/e, p 267

546.q: What is the treatment of choice of unruptured tubal pregnancy with serum b-hCG titre 2000 IU/ml:
546.e: The lady in the question is presenting with unruptured ectopic pregnancy with b-hCG levels - 2000 IU/L. So there is no doubt we can manage the patient medically (i.e. option d - ruled out) Expectant management as explained earlier is not better than medical management as it carries a risk of rupture of ectopic pregnancy (i.e., option C ruled out) and also it is done when b-hCG levels are Single dose therapy is more commonly used because of simplicity. It is less expensive, requires less invasive post therapy monitoring and does not require leucovorin supplementation. Reference: Williams Gynae 1/e, p 166, 167

546.q: Most common manifestation of ectopic pregnancy is:
546.e: Abdominal pain. It is seen in 95-100% cases. Most common and the most consistent symptom of ectopic pregnancy (undisturbed) is Pain is located in the lower abdomen/pelvic region. It can be unilateral or bilateral. In case of ruptured ectopic pregnancy: pain is due to hemoperitoneum and when internal hemorrhage floods the peritoneal cavity and irritates the undersurface of diaphragm and phrenic nerve, the patient also complains of shoulder tip and epigastric pain. In case of unruptured ectopic pain is due to stretching of the Fallopian tube Reference: Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 179; CODGT 10/e, p 267

546.q: Most important investigation for ectopic pregnancy:
546.e: Diagnostic Aids in Ectopic Pregnancy In hemodynamically stable patient presenting with a triad of amenorrhea, abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding 1st Test: UPT (+ve in 90% cases of ectopic) Reference: Shaw 14/e, p 244 Reference: Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 182, 183; Leon Speroff 7/e, p 1280-1285; Novak

o: Irregular vaginal bleeding may be a side effect
Used in with combination with oral contraceptive pills
546.e: Minipill can be used during lactation (i.e. option "c" is incorrect). It is not used in combination with other pills therefore option "b" is incorrect. Minipill "Ectopic pregnancy is not prevented as effectively as intrauterine pregnancy. Although the overall incidence of ectopic pregnancy is not increased, When pregnancy occurs (with mini pill use) the clinician must suspect that it is more likely to be ectopic. A previous ectopic pregnancy should not be regarded as a contraindication to the mini pill." —Leon Speroff 7 th /ed p 922 So option "d" is incorrect Main side effect of Minipill /progesterone only pill: Irregular bleeding and amenorrhea (i.e. option "a" is correct). Pearl index-3% Reference : Leon Speroff 7 th /ed p 922

546.q: A young woman with six weeks amenorrhoea presents with a mass abdomen. USG shows an empty uterus. Diagnosis is:
546.e: A young woman presenting with 6 weeks of amenorrhea and USG showing empty uterus could either mean it is an ectopic pregnancy or abortion. In abortion – patient will give history of bleeding, pain but mass in abdomen does not favour it. Reference: Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 182; Williams Obs. 22/e, p 258, 259, 23/e, p 242, 243.

547.q: Type of cerclage done in a non-pregnant patient with cervical incompetence?
547.e: The purpose of the Lash and Lash operation is to correct the defect in the cervical wall and restore competence to the cervix, thereby allowing gestation to proceed to term. Lash and Lash operation is a pervaginal procedure done in non pregnant females Benson Durfee is an abdominal cerclage procedure that can be done oin bothe pregnant as well as non pregnant females. Wurms cerclage is an emergency cerclage procedure done during pregnancy Still, Laparoscopic cerclage is the most preferred operative procedure in non pregnant females.

547.q: Comprehensive emergency obstetric care does not include:
547.e: Setting standards of emergency obstetrics and newborn care: Basic emergency obstetric and newborn care provided in health centres, large or small include the facilities for: Administration of antibiotics, oxytocics and anticonvulsants. Manual removal of the placenta. Removal of retained products following miscarriage or abortion. Assisted vaginal delivery preferably with vacuum extractor. Comprehensive emergency obstetric and newborn care, typically delivered in district hospital, includes all basic functions above, plus cesarean section, safe blood transfusion and care to sick and low birth weight newborns including resuscitation. It is recommended that for every 5,00,000 people there should be 4 facilities offering comprehensive essential obstetric care. Reference: KDT 6/e, p 251,484,488,Dutta Obs 7/e, p 288

547.q: A cross-sectional analysis across obstetrics and gynecology wards in several Indian hospitals reported an MMR of 4.21 per 1,000 live births. Based on WHO guidelines, how is maternal mortality defined?
o: Death from full-term pregnancy within 24 hr of delivery
Death during pregnancy and within 1 year after delivery
Death during pregnancy and within 6 weeks of delivery
547.e: Explanation: Maternal mortality refers to the death of a woman during pregnancy or within 6 weeks (42 days) after its termination. WHO Definition: Maternal mortality is defined as the annual number of deaths of women from causes related to or worsened by pregnancy or its management (excluding accidental or incidental causes), occurring during pregnancy or within 42 days of its end, regardless of the pregnancy's duration or location. Late Maternal Death: This refers to the death of a woman from direct or indirect obstetric causes occurring more than 42 days but less than one year after the end of pregnancy. Options A, B, and C are incorrect. Reference: https://www.who.int/data/gho/indicator-metadata-registry/imr-details/4622 https://sciencedirect.com/topics/medicine-and-dentistry/maternal-mortality

547.q: A lady has recurrent abortions in the 1st trimester with a history of autosomal recessive disorder in the family. The true statement regarding this is:
547.e: Explanation: Autosomal recessive inheritance is the single largest category of Mendelian disorders. They have following features: The trait does not usually affect the parents but siblings may show the disease (Option "c" is correct). Siblings have one chance in four of being affected (i.e. recurrence risk is 25% for each birth). Consanguineous marriage may be the cause ( Option "a" is correct). The expression of the defect tends to be more uniform than in autosomal dominant disorders. Complete penetration is common (Option "b" is correct). Onset is frequently early in life. In the question the lady has recurrent abortions and H/o autosomal recessive disorder in the family, therefore all features of autosomal recessive disorders apply to her.

547.q: A patient had a spontaneous abortion, then she came with amenorrhea and FSH 6 pm IU/mL. What the most probably diagnosis?
547.e: Normal FSH values range from 5 to 20 mzU/mL. in the question, FSH levels are 6 mzU/mL, that means this is a case of secondary amenorrhea with normal FSH values. In case of pituitary failure - as is evident from the flow diagram ® values of FSH should be lower than the normal values. So Option 'd' is ruled out Incase of ovarian failure → estrogen is deficient so negative feedback on FSH will be absent, thus values of FSH will be more than normal. In case of ovarian failure/menopause, FSH is above 40 m IU/mL so option a is also ruled out. Normal FSH and amenorrhea point towards uterine pathology. The patient had a spontaneous abortion following which a curettage is generally required which would be responsible for intrauterine synechiae (Asherman's Syndrome). Thus, the most probable diagnosis is uterine synechiae. Reference : Leon speroff 7 th /ed, pg no: 415-425.

547.q: A 24 years old female reports in the casualty with history of amenorrhoea for two and half months and abdominal pain and bleeding per vaginum for one day. On examination, vital parameters and other systems are normal. On speculum examination, bleeding is found to come from Os. On bimanual examination, the uterus is of 10 weeks size, soft and Os admits one finger. The most likely diagnosis is
547.e: Clinical features and diagnosis of different types of Abortions In the question, os is open, size of uterus corresponds to period of amenorrhea and product of conception cannot be seen coming out from os.Thus, it indicates inevitable abortion. Reference: Dutta Obs 7/e, p 161, 162

547.q: A Patient at 24 weeks gestation is diagnosed as having IUD which occurred at 17 weeks but did not have a miscarriage. This patient is at increased risk for:
547.e: Dead fetuses, if retained for more than 4 to 5 weeks, release thromboplastin which leads to DIC (consumptive coagulopathy). In the question, the fetus has been dead and has been retained for five weeks so there are increased chances of DIC. Reference: : Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 325

547.q: All of the following are known causes of recurrent abortion except:
547.e: As discussed in previous question TORCH infection do not lead to recurrent abortion. SLE is an established cause for recurrent abortion SLE is associated with antiphospholipid syndrome (anti-cardiolipin antibodies) and is known to cause recurrent abortions. RH incompatibility is a known cause for spontaneous abortion and may lead to recurrent abortions if it remains unrecognized. Syphillis also does not lead to recurrent abortions but if you have to rule out one option between TORCH infection and syphilis go for TORCH infection. Reference: 'Pre-test' Obstetrics and Gynaecology 11/e, p 68.

548.q: A 30-year-old female patient is admitted to the Emergency Department with dyspnea, tachycardia, confusion, and other signs of hypoxia. The following laboratory data were obtained while the patient was breathing room air. PaO2 = 67 mmHg PaCO2 = 60 mmHg pH = 7.27 [HCO3-] = 26 mEq/L [Hb] = 15 g% SaO2 = 90% PvO2 = 30 mmHg SvO2 = 55% VO2 = 350 mL/min CaO2-CvO2 = 7 mL O2/100 mL Which of the following is the most appropriate classification of the patient's hypoxia?
548.e: Alveolar hypoventilation (as evidenced by the higher than normal value of Paco2) is a type of hypoxic hypoxia or hypoxemia (as evidenced by the decreased PaO2). Anemic hypoxia is characterized by a decreased concentration of hemoglobin (anemia) or a reduction in the saturation of hemoglobin with oxygen (SaO2) expected for a given Pao2, as would occur in carbon monoxide poisoning or methemoglobinemia. Stagnant hypoxia is characterized by a decreased cardiac output; in this patient, cardiac output, calculated as (VO2/CaO2 - CvO2), is 5 L/min, which is normal.
