In histotoxic hypoxia, oxygen extraction is impaired, and thus CaO2 - CvO2 would be less than normal and Svo2 would be greater than normal. Reference: Ganong, pp 683-691. Levitzky, pp 180-183.

548.q: Treatment of genuine stress incontinence are all except:
548.e: Pelvic floor exercises Sling operation Colposuspension (Burch) is all done for management of SUI. As far as anterior colporrhaphy is concerned - Kelly’s application is anterior colporrhaphy along with bladder neck repair, so I have included it in the correct option also. Reference: Shaw 14 th /ed p 174; Dutta gynae 5 th /ed p 387-9

548.q: Regimen used for expectant management of placenta previa is:
548.e: Expectant treatment had been advocated by Mcafee and Johnson, in an attempt to improve the fetal salvage without increasing undue maternal hazards. The aim is to continue pregnancy for fetal maturity without compromising the maternal health. Reference:-D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 19

548.q: A primigravida at 37 weeks of gestation reported to the labour room with central placenta previa with heavy bleeding per vaginum. The fetal heart rate was normal at the time of examination. The best management option for her is
548.e: The patient in the question: Has gestational age = 37 weeks i.e. fetus has attained maturity so immediate termination of pregnancy is recommended. Has central placenta previa Type IV i.e. vaginal delivery is contraindicated, cesarean section has to be done. Patient is having heavy bleeding. According to Fernando Arias 3/e, p 337 "In patients with heavy bleeding an efficient management plan including life support measures and immediate operative intervention is the only way to avoid a maternal death." It further says – on p 339 "Patients with placenta previa and severe bleeding should be delivered by cesarean section irrespective of the type of placenta previa." Reference: Dutta Obs 7/e, p 249, 250; Fernando Arias 3/e, p 337, 339

548.q: Abruptio placentae occurs in all except:
548.e: Abruptio placenta is premature separation of normally situated placenta resulting in hemorrhage Risk factors: Increased maternal age Pre-eclampsia Preterm ruptured membranes pregnancy Cigarette smoking Cocaine abuse External trauma Uterine leiomyoma Increased parity Chronic hypertension Sudden uterine decompression as in hydramnios and twin Thrombophilia Previous abruption Folic acid deficiency Reference: Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 252, 253; Williams Obs. 22/e, p 813, 814, 23/e, p 763-765

About one-third cases of antepartum hemorrhage belong to placenta previa. The incidence of placenta previa is 1 in 200 pregnancies (0.5%). In 80% cases, it is found in multiparous women. The incidence is increased beyond the age of 35 years, with high birth order pregnancies and in multiple pregnancy Reference: D C Dutta's textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 19

548.q: All of the following are high risk factors for placenta previa except:
548.e: Risk factors for placenta previa Multiparity Advanced age (>35 years) Smoking Prior caesarean delivery Multifetal gestation Placental abnormality Prior curettage History of ART (assisted reproductive technology) Reference:-Williams obstetrics 26 th edition, chapter 43

548.q: Which of the following is classified as mild degree of placenta previa?
548.e: There are four types of placenta previa depending upon the degree of extension of placenta to the lower segment. For clinical purpose, the types are graded into mild degree (Type-I and II anterior) and major degree (Type-II posterior, III and IV). Reference:-D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 19

549.q: Riskofuterine rupture in case ofuterine scar. 1317. Methergin is given for prophylaxis of ?
549.e: Ans, A. Anaemia Methergin (methyl-ergo-novine) is a semisynthetic ergot derivative derived from lysergic acid. Indications

549.q: Which of the following arteries is not ligated during stepwise devascularization for PPH?
549.e: Stepwise pelvic devascularization Uterine artery Tubal branch of ovarian artery (utero-ovarian artery) Anterior branch of internal iliac artery Reference:D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 28

549.q: A G2P1 had an uneventful vaginal delivery of a 3.4 kg baby girl. Placenta was completely expulsed soon after delivery. After delivery of placenta there was excessive vaginal bleeding uterus was hard and contracted. Most likely cause of bleeding would be:
549.e: Cervical tear is the commonest cause of traumatic postpartum haemorrhage. Clinical feature: Excessive vaginal bleeding immediately following delivery in presence of a hard and contracted uterus. Repair should be done under general anesthesia, in lithotomy position with a good light. Reference: D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 29

549.q: In case of severe PPH blood loss is more than:
549.e: The average blood loss is vaginal delivery: 500 ml, caesarean delivery: 1000 ml and caesarean hysterectomy:1500 ml. Depending upon the amount of blood loss, PPH can be Minor ( Major (> 1L) or Severe (> 2L). Reference:D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 28

549.q: Pathogenicity of PPH presented by four T's include all of the following except:
549.e: Four basic pathologies are expressed as the four Ts’ (RCOG): Tone (atonicity), Tissue (retained bits, blood clots), Trauma (genital tract injury) and Thrombin (coagulopathy). Reference:D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 28

549.q: When does expectant management in case of secondary PPH is not tried?
o: When minimal placental tissue is present
When patient is delivered by caesarean section
549.e: Conservative management (done for 24 hr): If the bleeding is slight and No apparent cause is detected, Monitoring facility available in the hospital. Reference:D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 28

549.q: All of the following conditions can lead to PPH except:
549.e: Haemorrhage in early pregnancy: abortion, ectopic pregnancy, hydatidiform mole and implantation bleeding. PPH: bleeding after 3 rd stage of labor (after delivery) Reference:D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 16

549.q: Likely size of uterus at 8 weeks postpartum is:
549.e: Weight of uterus : Immediately after delivery - 1000 gm At the end of 1 week - 500 gm At the end of 2 weeks - 300 gm At the end of 4 weeks it weighs - 100 gm (Pre-pregnant state). Also Know : Immediately following delivery, the fundus is just below the umbilicus (13.5 cm above the symphysis pubis/ 20 weeks gestational age size.) Involution of the uterus After 24 hours of delivery, height of uterus decreases by 1.25 cm/day. Uterus is a pelvic to organ. by the end of 2 weeks. Uterus returns almost to its normal size (pre pregnant size) by the end of 8 weeks. The process by which the postpartum uterus returns to its pre pregnant state is called Involution . Involution is achieved by decrease in the size of muscle fibres (and not in the number). Reference : Dutta Obs. 7/e, pg 145; Williams Obs. 24/e, pg 669

550.q: Which of the following statements is true about the fetal fibronectin (fFN) test?
o: In this test fFN is measured from maternal serum
Positive test in first trimester increases risk of abortion
Negative test means delivery will not occur in next 7 days
550.e: Fibronectin is a glycoprotein that binds the fetal membranes to the decidua. Normally it is found in the cervicovaginal discharge before 22 weeks and again after 37 weeks of pregnancy. Presence of fibronectin in the cervicovaginal discharge between 24 weeks and 34 weeks is a predictor of preterm labor. When the test is negative it reassures that delivery will not occur within the next 7 days . Reference : D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 22

550.q: Which of the following is not a contraindication to tocolysis:
550.e: Contraindications to tocolysis Intrauterine fetal demise Lethal fetal anomaly Nonreassuring fetal status Severe preeclampsia or eclampsia Maternal bleeding with hemodynamic instability Chorioamnionitis Preterm prelabor rupture of membranes Reference : laxmi sheshadri principles of obstetric, 1 st edition, chapter-35

550.q: Pain in early labor is limited to dermatomes:
550.e: In the early stages of labour pain is mainly uterine in origin because of painful uterine contraction "The pain of uterine contractions is distributed along the cutaneous nerve distribution of T 10 to L 1 In later stages pain is due to dilatation of the cervix. "The pain of cervical dilatation and stretching is referred to the back through sacral plexus." Reference : Dutta Obs 7/e, pg 117

550.q: Which of the following statements is not true regarding obstructive uterine rupture?
o: Occurs in cases of obstructed labor
Margins of rupture are ragged and necrosed
FHS is absent in all cases
550.e: Obstructive rupture-This is the end result of an obstructed labor. The rupture involves the anterior lower segment and usually extends through one lateral side of the uterus to the upper segment. The margins are ragged and necrosed. Nonobstructive rupture-Grand multipara are usually affected and rupture usually occurs in early labor. Weakening of the walls due to repeated previous births as mentioned earlier may be the responsible factor. The rupture usually involves the fundal area and is complete. Reference: D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 29

550.q: The following statements are related to the management of obstructed labour except:
o: There is no place of wait and watch policy
Dehydration and ketoacidosis should be promptly corrected
Oxytocin has got a definite place in the management
550.e: Management of obstructed labor: Prompt Management of dehydration and ketoacidosis—by giving IV fluids Antibiotics are given to prevent infection Most important step is to relieve obstruction by either instrumental delivery or by doingLSCS. LSCS may even have to be done, if the baby is dead to relieve the obstruction otherwise uterine rupture can occur. The two main principles in the management of obstructed labor are: Never wait and watch Never use oxytocin Reference : Dutta Obs 7/e, p 59

550.q: Which layer of myometrium is described as 'living ligature' of uterus
550.e: 3 layers of uterus Endometrium Myometrium Perimetrium/serosal Layers of myometrium Outer longitudinal Middle interlacing Inner circular The middle layer is the thickest of the three and consists of bundles of muscle separated by connective tissue. There is a tendency for the muscle bundles to interlace, and as the blood vessels which supply the uterus are distributed in the connective tissues, the caliber of the vessels is in part controlled by the contraction of the muscle cells. The purpose of this layer is therefore in part hemostatic. This layer is described as living ligatures of the uterus , and is responsible for control of bleeding in the third stage of labor. Reference: Shaw’s textbook of gynecology, 16th edition, chapter 1

550.q: Causes of uterine rupture include all of the following except?
550.e: GRAND MULTIPARA ARE AT RISK OF UTERINE RUPTURE. RISK FACTORS OF UTERINE RUPTURE INCLUDE: PREVIOUS CS (CLASSICAL > LSCS ) OBSTRUCTED LABOR( NON SCARRED ) GRAND MULTIPARA MISOPROSTOL : It is contraindicated for IOL in previous CS Pts. OXYTOCIN. KEYWORDS: M/C sign: non reassuring FHR Most specific: loss of station Generalised pain Hypotension Loss of uterine contour Fetal parts superficially palpable Reference: D C Dutta's textbook of obstetrics 8th edition, chapter 29

550.q: A 22-year-old primigravida patient came to hospital at 35 weeks of gestation complaining of abdominal pain. She denied having any vaginal discharge. She had regular uterine contraction and her cervical length was 2 cm in TVS. Obstetrician performed fFN test which was positive. What would be the most probable diagnosis for such a patient?
550.e: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (2020e) defines preterm labor to be regular contractions accompanied by a change in cervical dilation, effacement, or both or to be regular contractions and cervical dilation of at least 2 cm at initial presentation. fFN: Detected in cervicovaginal secretions in women who have normal pregnancies with intact membranes at term, fFN appears to reflect stromal remodeling of the cervix before labor . Reference : Williams obstetrics 26 th edition, chapter 45

551.q: How does a hydatidiform mole occur?
o: Hyperplastic proliferation of trophoblast within the uterine wall
551.e: Hydatidiform mole is a rare mass that rapidly grows within the uterus. It results from hyperplastic proliferation of trophoblast within the uterine wall. It has a high potential to become choriocarcinoma. Reference - Textbook of Langman's, 12th Edition, General Embryology Page number - 43

551.q: What malignant tumor arises from trophoblastic cells?
551.e: Choriocarcinoma is a malignant tumor that arises from trophoblastic cells that may occur following normal pregnancy, abortions, or hydatidiform mole. Reference - Textbook of Langman's, 12th Edition, General Embryology Page number - 43

551.q: Theca lutein cyst is not seen in:
551.e: Theca lutein cysts are bilateral cysts seen in ovaries associated with markedly elevated levels of hCG. Conditions of pregnancy where theca lutein cysts are seen: Molar pregnancy Diabetes D alloimmunization Multifetal gestation Chronic renal failure – decreased clearance of hCG Hyperthyroidism (hCG and TSH–anatomically similar) Reference: Williams Obs 24/e, p 50

551.q: A case of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia is detected to have lung metastasis. She should be staged as:
551.e: Staging of Gestational trophoblastic disease: Stage-I Disease confined to the uterus. Stage-II Disease extends outside of the uterus but is limited to the genital structures (adnexa, vagina, broad ligaments). Stage-III Disease extending to the lungs, with or without known genital tract involvement. Stage-IV Disease at other metastatic sites viz brain, liver, kidney or gastrointestinal tract. Reference: COGDT 10/e, p 893

551.q: A case of Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia belongs to high risk group, if disease develops after:
551.e: FIGO in 2000 devised a staging system for categorisation of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia into good prognostic (low risk) and bad prognostic (high risk) disease. Also if we have a look at the WHO prognostic scoring system: GTN following a term pregnancy comes under high risk. Reference: COGDT 10/e, p 892, 893; Novak 14/e, p 1593, 1594

551.q: All are the complications of anemia except:
551.e: Complications of Anemia Preeclampsia Infection Heart failure at 30-32 weeks PPH Shock Subinvolution Pulmonary embolism during puerperium Fetal: Low birthweight Intrauterine death Reference: Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 266

551.q: Malignant germ cell tumours of ovary includes:
551.e: Germ cell Tumors of ovary: Mnemonic: YES PCT Y - Yolk sac Tumor (Endodermal sinus Tm) E - Embryonal carcinoma S Seminoma ≈ Dysgerminoma P - Polyembryoma C - Choriocarcinoma T - Teratoma ≈ Dermoid In contrast to slow growing epithelial ovarian tumors, germ cell malignancies grow rapidly and are characterised by subacute pelvic pain. Most common germ cell Tumor – Mature teratoma or Dermoid cyst (Benign in nature). Most common malignant GCT – Dysgerminoma. Second most common malignant GCT – Endodermal sinus Tumor. (Yolk Sac tumor) Most common benign Tumor of ovary – Dermoid cyst Reference : Novak 14 th /ed pg 1506; 15 th /ed pg 1394; Williams Gynae 1 st /ed pg 741

551.q: The following primary tumors are common in the vulva except:
551.e: Histological types of vulval cancers Squamous cell carcinoma-90% Melanoma 5% Adenocarcinoma (Bartholin's gland) Basal cell carcinoma Sarcoma Reference: Dutta Gynae 6 th /ed pg 334

552.q: The lab for your pregnant patient indicates microcytic anemia. Optimal treatment of normocytic or mild microcytic anemia associated with pregnancy uses which of the following?
552.e: Iron deficiency microcytic anemia is the anemia that is most commonly associated with In this condition, oral iron supplementation is indicated. Reference: Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, Fourteenth Edition By Bertram G. Katzung Pg no. 834-37

552.q: All of the following are fetal complications of prolonged pregnancy except:
552.e: Fetal complications during pregnancy—There is diminished placental function, oligohydramnios and meconium stained liquor. These lead to fetal hypoxia and fetal distress. Reference: D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 22

552.q: Which of the following is a non-surgical method for replacement of uterine inversion?
552.e: Hydrostatic(O’Sullivan’s) method: The inverted uterus is replaced into the vagina. Warm sterile fluid (up to 5 liters) is gradually instilled into the vagina through a douche nozzle. The vaginal orifice is blocked by the operator's palms supplemented by labial apposition around the palm by an assistant. Alternatively, a silicon cup (vacuum extraction cup) is placed into the vagina. The douche can be placed at a height of about 3 feet above the uterus. The water distends the vagina and the consequent increased intravaginal pressure leads to replacement of the uterus. Reference: D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 28

552.q: Neonatal complications of prolonged pregnancy include:
552.e: Neonatal complications Chemical pneumonitis, atelectasis and pulmonary hypertension are due to meconium aspiration; Hypoxia (low Apgar scores) and respiratory failure; Hypoglycemia and polycythemia and Increased NICU admissions. Reference: D C Dutta’s textbook of obstetrics 8 th edition, chapter 22

552.q: 30 years old lady with failed medical treatment of uterine polyp, the surgical treatment of uterine polyp can be:
552.e: Endometrial polyp -- Hysteroscopy and resection (best) Removal by ovum forcep Incase of recurrence and, if family completed— uterine curettage hysterectomy Cervical polyp -- Twisting of the pedicle Big fibroid in vagina -- Removal of polyp by morcellation If associated with inversion enucleate Ref. Dutta Gynae 6th/ed p 287, 288

552.q: In pregnancy, which type of anemia is not common in India?
552.e: In countries like India, anemia due to iron and folic acid deficiency commonly occur during pregnancy. Only Vitamin B 12 deficiency as a cause of anemia is rare. 'Megaloblastic anemia caused by lack of vitamin B 12 , that is cyanocobalamin, during pregnancy is exceedingly rare' - Williams Obs. 22/e, p 1147, 23/e, p 1082 Reference: Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 268; Williams Obs. 22/e, p 1147, 23/e, p 1082; Fernando Arias 3/e, p 469

552.q: Dose of folic acid per day for treating megaloblastic anemia in pregnancy:
552.e: DOSE OF FOLIC ACID IN PREGNANCY: PER DAY: To prevent neural tube defect: 400 micro grams In pregnant females with previous h/o ntd: 4mg To treat megaloblastic anaemia: 1mg In patients with sickle cell disease: 4mg Reference: High Risk Pregnancy, Arias 4/e, p 237

552.q: Fourteen weeks pregnancy with third degree prolapse. Best management will be:
552.e: Other indications of Ring pessary: In puerperium – to facilitate involution. Patient unfit or unwilling for surgery. Women who have undergone at least one previous attempt at surgical intervention without relief. Diagnostic – It may be placed diagnostically to identify which women are at risk for urinary incontinence after prolapse correction surgery. Note: Pessaries are of two varieties : Supportive pessary eg–Ring pessary Space occupying pessary eg–Gellhorn pessary Reference: Dutta Obs 6th/ed p 312-3; Shaw 15th/ed p 337-8; Williams Gynae 1st/ed p 545-7

553.q: A female of 36 weeks gestation presents with hypertension, blurring of vision and headache. Her blood pressure reading was 180/120 mm Hg and 174/110 mm Hg after 20 minutes. How will you manage the patient?
o: Admit the patient, start antihypertensives and continue pregnancy till term.
Admit the patient, start antihypertensives, MgSO4 and terminate the pregnancy
Admit oral antihypertensives and follow up in out-patient department
553.e: In the question, patient is presenting with Headache, Blurring of vision, B/P = 180/120 mm of Hg (later 174/110 mm of Hg) i.e. she is a case of severe pregnancy induced hypertension. First step in the management of this case would be to prevent seizures i.e. give MgSO4. Her B/P should be controlled with antihypertensive and since pregnancy is >34 weeks, therefore terminate pregnancy (which is the definitive management). Reference : Fernando Arias Practical Guide to High Risk Pregnancy and Delivery 3/e, pg 417, 420, 424

553.q: Preconceptional intake of which of the following results in decrease in incidence of neural tube defect?
553.e: "Folic acid has been shown to effectively reduce the risk of neural tube defects (NTDs). A daily 4 mg dose is recommended for patients who have had a previous pregnancy affected by neural tube defects. It should be started at least 1 month (ideally 3 months) prior to pregnancy and continued through the first 6-12 weeks of pregnancy." -COGDT 10/e, p 197 Remember: Therapeutic dose of folic acid (to be given in females with a previous history of baby with NTD) - 4 mg. Prophylactic dose of folic acid = 0.4 mg i.e., 400 mg Duration: It should be started 1 month before conception and continued till 3 months of pregnancy. Note: Women with insulin dependent diabetes mellitus and those with seizure disorders treated by valproic acid and carbamazepine are also at greater risk for NTD's and should be given therapeutic dose of folic acid i.e 4 mg. Reference: Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 409; COGDT 10/e, p 197

553.q: A second gravida patient with a history of pre eclampsia comes to OPD at 5 months of amenorrhea. Which test would you like to perform for prediction of pre eclampsia in this pregnancy?
553.e: Doppler ultrasound Presence of diastolic notch between 22-24 weeks by Doppler velocimetry in the uterine artery predicts the development of preeclampsia. It is probably the best available test. Reference : Arias 5 th edition pg no 192

553.q: Dose of aspirin for prevention of pre eclampsia is
553.e: The action of low-dose aspirin in the prevention of preeclampsia involves its effects on blood clotting and vascular function: Antiplatelet Effect:Aspirin inhibits platelet aggregation by blocking the enzyme cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1), which reduces the production of thromboxane A2. This helps to prevent excessive blood clotting and improves blood flow. Vascular Protection: By inhibiting thromboxane A2, aspirin also helps to reduce endothelial cell activation and vasoconstriction, which can lower the risk of placental insufficiency and the development of preeclampsia. Overall, these effects contribute to improved placental blood flow and reduced risk of the complications associated with preeclampsia. As per ASPREE trial, 150 mg of aspirin is given from 12-36 weeks of pregnancy in patients with high risk of developing preeclampsia for prevention. Reference : Arias 5 th edition pg no 181

553.q: All are the laboratory investigations done in cases of pre eclampsia except
553.e: In preeclampsia, the focus is on monitoring renal function (A), liver function (B), and urine analysis (C) to assess the severity of the condition and its impact on the body. Anticardiolipin antibodies (D) are not typically part of the routine evaluation for preeclampsia; they are more relevant in the context of antiphospholipid syndrome. Investigations to be done in case of pre eclampsia are hemogram, platelet count, hematocrit, RFT, LFT, coagulation profile, electrolytes, serum uric acid, ECG, echocardiogram Reference : Arias 5 th edition pg no 180

553.q: 30 year old primi with 36 weeks of pregnancy with blood pressure 160/110 and urinary albumin is 3+ & platelet count 80000/mm3. What will be the management?
553.e: In the Question patient has - Blood pressure = 160/110 mm Hg Platelet count = 80, 000/cubic mm} indicating severe Preeclampsia The gestational age is 36 weeks Management of severe preeclampsia in Gestational age > 34 weeks is delivery As far as mode of delivery is concerned, vaginal delivery is preferred. If the cervix is not ripe prostaglandins are used to refer to the cause. If it fails then cesarean is done. Betamethasone to hasten lung maturity is not required at 36 weeks as lungs are already mature by this time. 'Termination of pregnancy is the only cure for preeclampsia. Severe preeclampsia demands anti convulsant and usually antihypertensive therapy followed by delivery'. Reference: Williams obs 23 rd edition pg 729

553.q: All are the indications for termination of pregnancy in a woman with preeclampsia except
553.e: Indications for termination of pregnancy irrespective of the weeks of gestation in case of preeclampsia are: Severe preeclampsia, with impending eclampsia Eclampsia (give MgSO4 first, followed by induction of labor) HELLP syndrome. Pulmonary edema Significant renal dysfunction, coagulopathy Abruption Previable fetus Fetal compromise A woman with a past history of eclampsia is at increased risk for developing eclampsia again in subsequent pregnancies. However, this is not considered an indication for termination of pregnancy in and of itself. Reference : Arias 5th edition pg no 197

553.q: Which is the most common medical complication of pregnancy?
553.e: Hypertensive disorders complicate 7-15% of all gestations and account for a quarter of all antenatal admissions. Reference : Arias 5 th edition pg no 172

554.q: A 42-year-old man presents with headaches, excessive sweating, galactorrhoea, polyuria and polydipsia. Visual field examination reveals bitemporal hemianopia. His blood pressure is 160/110 mmHg. Blood tests: fasting glucose 150 mg/dl, prolactin 1200 mU/l (<360).What is the most probable diagnosis?
554.e: Prolactinoma: (>200) Clinical features: Amenorrhoea Galactorrhoea Infertility Compressive symptoms: B/L TEMPORAL HEMIANOPIA. DOC: CABERGOLINE - FOR ALL CASES BROMOCRIPTINE- IF PREGNANCY IS DESIRED. Reference : Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 21 st edition Page 2912

554.q: A 50-year-old male patient presents with polyuria and polydipsia of 2 months duration. He has been on a chronic medication for last 15 years. The urine is hypoosmolar. His blood sugars are normal. Which could be the drug?
554.e: Polyuria, polydipsia with large volume of hypoosmolar urine suggest the diagnosis of Diabetes insipidus. Among the following, Lithium therapy causes nephrogenic diabetes. Other drugs causing Diabetes Insipidus: Lithium, Demeclocycline, Methoxyflurane, Amphotericin B, Aminoglycosides, Cisplatin, Rifampin, Foscarnet. Lithium causes DI by entering the Collecting Duct via the ENaC, where it down regulates the Aquaporin channels. Lithium also causes Chronic Tubulointerstitial Disease. Amiloride can be used to prevent and treat Lithium induced Diabetes Insipidus. Reference: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, Ch: 316, Pg: 2363.

554.q: As per IAS DP the proposed single step testing with a 75 gram oral glucose for gestational diabetes, the fasting glucose cut off is
554.e: It is recommended that an FPG( Fasting plasma glucose) value in early pregnancy ≥5.1 mmol/l (92 mg/dl) should also be classified as Gestational Diabetes Mellitus. International Association of Diabetes and Pregnancy Study Groups Consensus Panel; Metzger BE, Gabbe SG, Persson B, Buchanan TA, Catalano PA, Damm P, Dyer AR, Leiva Ad, Hod M, Kitzmiller JL, Lowe LP, McIntyre HD, Oats JJ, Omori Y, Schmidt MI. International association of diabetes and pregnancy study groups recommendations on the diagnosis and classification of hyperglycemia in pregnancy.

554.q: A 29-year-old woman came to the diabetes clinic with her two children. This is her third pregnancy and although not normally diabetic, she was diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus. Recent fasting plasma glucose levels have been in the range of 80-90 mg/dl and she is taking BD mixed insulins. Later that evening she collapses while shopping and is brought to the Emergency Department with blood glucose of 56 mg/dl. Which of the following represents the most appropriate management in this patient?
o: Reduce her dose of BD mixed insulin by 50%
Reduce her dose of BD mixed insulin by 20%
Check a random cortisol to rule out Addison's disease
Change her to a basal bolus regime
554.e: This lady's fasting plasma glucose levels are appropriate, but taking a BD mixed insulin regime is probably not appropriate to her lifestyle where her mealtimes and portion sizes may be slightly irregular given the fact that she has two other children to manage. A basal bolus regime would give her more flexibility in varying insulin dose. The coexistence of Addison's is unlikely and increasing the size of her meals would only promote more excess weight gain and worsening insulin resistance. Reference: ADA Standards of Diabetes Care - 2023

554.q: Which of the following blood glucose readings is diagnostic of gestational diabetes according to IADPSG criteria?
554.e: The screening for Diabetes mellitus should be performed in women at the first prenatal visit First trimester screening is performed for high risk women according to ADA while ACOG advocates universal screening for all women The diagnosis of Gestational Diabetes mellitus is made if either one of the following is satisfied: Fasting blood glucose > 92 mg/dl 1 hr post OGTT > 180 mg/dl 2 hr post OGTT > 153 mg/dl If fasting blood glucose is more than 126 mg/dl or 2-hour post glucose load value is > 200 mg/dl, the diagnosis of overt diabetes mellitus is made Reference: ADA Standards of Medical Care in Diabetes 2023

554.q: A 54 year old dark skinned man presents with lethargy, polyuria, polydipsia and stiffness of the hands. He has evidence of an arthropathy affecting the 2nd & 3rd metacarpophalangeal joints of both hands. Xray confirms evidence of degenerative disease at these sites. Which of the following the likely diagnosis?
554.e: Clues pointing towards hemochromatosis: Dark skinned-> bronzing of skin Polyuria, polydipsia-> Diabetes mellitus Destructive arthropathy in typical location The characteristic feature of haemochromatotic arthropathy is involvement of the second and third metacarpals. The arthropathy can lead to extensive joint destruction. These patients may have episodes of acute, inflammatory pseudogout from such deposition. Arthropathy and hypogonadism do not respond to Iron lowering therapy. Reference: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 21 st edition Ch: 374, Pg: 2871

554.q: In a nondiabetic high risk pregnancy, the ideal time for non-stress test monitoring is:
554.e: Intervals between NST testing The interval between tests is arbitrarily set at 7 days. According to ACOG, more frequent testing is advocated for women with post term pregnancy, type I diabetes mellitus, IUGR or gestational hypertension. In these circumstances some investigators recommend twice weekly (i.e. after 72 hours) with additional testing performed for maternal or fetal deterioration regardless of the time elapsed since the last test. Generally daily NST is recommended with severe preeclampsia remote from term. Reference: Williams Obs. 23/e, p 339

554.q: All are risk factors for vaginal candidiasis except:
554.e: Risk factors for Candida (Monilla) Vaginitis Promiscuity Immunosuppression (like HIV) Pregnancy Steroid therapy Following long-term broad spectrum antibiotic therapy Oral contraceptive pills Diabetes mellitus Poor personal hygiene Obesity Reference: Shaw 15th/ed p 146.

555.q: Indication of methotrexate in molar pregnancy:
555.e: Protocol for management of H. mole Prophylactic chemotherapy: Routine prophylactic chemotherapy is not advocated now at all. Earlier in the following conditions chemotherapy was given. Conditions: Initial high levels of b-hCG (> 100,000 mIU/ml) Elevation of serum hCG at 4–6 weeks or hCG values fail to come back to normal by stipulated truth (10-12 weeks). Evidence of metastasis irrespective of hCG levels. Age of patient > 35 years. Theca lutein cyst 6 cm Post evacuation hemorrhage. Drug used : Methotrexate/Actinomycin D is given for 5 days. Reference: Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 200, 196; COGDT 10/e, p 890; Shaw 14/e, p 231

555.q: A pregnant female develops an embolism just after delivery. What medical management should she take?
555.e: Venous thromboembolism in pregnancy Venous thromboembolism is the leading cause of maternal deaths in developed countries. Investigations Recommended method during pregnancy: Doppler ultrasound Gold standard (in conditions other than pregnancy): Venography Though objective evidence is ideal, treatment should be started on clinical grounds, if confirmatory tests are not available. Management For postpartum venous thrombosis, treatment with i/v heparin and warfarin are started simultaneously 6-8 hours after vaginal delivery and 24 hours after cesarean section and once INR is between 2 and 3, heparin is discontinued and warfarin is continued for 6 weeks. Note: Warfarin is absolutely safe in lactation. Reference : Williams 23/e, pg 1028, 29, Table 47.6

555.q: Patients with organic heart disease in pregnancy most commonly die during:
555.e: This is another way of asking, cardiac failure occurs most commonly at what time as the M/C cause of death in pregnant females with heart disease is congestive heart failure. Reference: Dutta Obs 7/e, p 225

555.q: The following statements are related to clear cell carcinoma of the vagina except:
o: Common to those whose mothers were given diethylstilbestrol during early pregnancy
Vaginal adenosis may progress to this conditions
The middle one-third is the commonest site
May be multicentric and may involve even the cervix as well
555.e: Clear cell adenocarcinoma of vagina- Primary vaginal adenocarcinoma is rare. This is found in adolescent girls who have had history of intrauterine exposure to diethylstilbestrol in the first trimester of pregnancy. The approximate risk of an offspring to develop the clear cell adenocarcinoma of the vagina following DES exposure is 1 in 1000 or less. These patients are more likely to develop vaginal adenosis but rarely clear cell adenocarcinoma. The lesion usually involves the upper-third of the anterior vaginal wall. The cervix may also be involved. Treatment: Radical hysterectomy, vaginectomy with pelvic lymphadenectomy is the treatment of choice. Radiotherapy is reserved for advanced cases. Reference : Dutta Gynae 6 th /ed pg 339

556.e: Anti D prophylaxis should be given after all types of abortions (threatened, medical, MTP) molar pregnancy, ectopic pregnancy, delivery (+manual removal of placenta), procedures performed antenatally (Amniocentesis, Chorionic villous sampling, External cephalic version) and in cases of antepartum hemorrhage (Vaginal bleeding in this case). Reference : Dutta Obs. 7/e, pg 344 "key points"; Shiela Balakrishnan, pg 369

556.q: Which type of Hb is not affected by Rh isoimmuni- sation:
556.e: The correct answer is (C): Anti Lewis. Anti Lewis antibodies are not affected by Rh isoimmunization, while Anti D, Anti C, and Anti E are all associated with Rh blood group antigens.Anti C and Anti E antibodies can also be produced in response to blood group incompatibilities, but their effects are generally less severe than those of Anti D The Lewis antigens do not cause erythroblastosis fetalis and differ from all of the other red cell antigens in that they are not synthesized in the red cell membrane but are absorbed into it." Reference: Fernando Arias 2/e, p 116

557.q: A 26-year-old woman comes with irregular vaginal bleeding and lower abdominal pain over the past 4 days. Physical examination shows a friable cervix, and cervical and adnexal tenderness. You prescribe doxycycline and a second medication. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of action of the most appropriate second drug used to treat this infection?
o: Binding at the D-ala-D-ala muramyl pentapeptide to prevent transglycosylation reactions
Binds to microtubules and causes mitotic arrest in metaphase
Inhibits DNA synthesis in virally infected cells
Inhibits peptidoglycan synthesis through the blockade of transpeptidation enzymes
557.e: This patient has signs of pelvic inflammatory disease, and since distinguishing diagnostic clues are not provided here, the answer should pertain to the most common causes, which include Chlamydia and gonococcal infection. Infections of the cervix may present as an erythematous, edematous, and friable cervix, but most often are without obvious signs or symptoms. Early signs and symptoms of a chlamydial infection in women tend to be mild and include pain during urination, frequent urination, and low-grade fever. Later symptoms can be more intense and include nausea, fatigue, and abnormal discharge from the vagina. Other symptoms include abdominal pain, lower back pain, irregular menstrual bleeding or spotting, and pain during sex. Reference: Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, Fourteenth Edition By Bertram G. Katzung Pg no. 816

557.q: At what gestational age should pregnancy with cholestasis of pregnancy be terminated.
557.e: Also know Management of Intrahepatic Cholestasis – Medical Management The most troublesome feature of intrahepatic cholestasis is pruritus (and pruritus is due to bile acid in blood): Pruritus can be managed temporarily with antihistamines and topical emollients Ursodeoxycholic acid (10-15 mg/kg/d in 2 divided doses) relieves pruritus decreasing in the concentration of bile acid in blood and it also improves biochemical abnormalities. In patients of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy – there is increased perinatal mortality. Hence fetal surveillance is done with biweekly NST. Conventional antepartum testing, does not predict fetal mortality as there is sudden death in choletasis due to acute hypoxia, hence delivery is recommended at 37-38 weeks. Reference : COGDT 10/e, pg 382; Williams Obs 24/e, pg 1085 Mgt of High Risk Pregnancy - S S Trivedi Manju Puri, pg 358

557.q: Earliest manifestation of end organ damage in chronic hypertension is
557.e: The earliest manifestation of end-organ damage in chronic hypertension is typically (B): Renal impairment. Chronic hypertension can lead to changes in kidney function and structure over time. These changes may be detectable through alterations in renal function tests, such as elevated serum creatinine levels or proteinuria. This early renal impairment often precedes other manifestations of end-organ damage such as hepatic, visual, or pulmonary complications Reference : Arias 5 th edition pg no 179

558.q: A 48-year-old woman presents with heavy menstrual bleeding. Which of the following hormones is most commonly associated with shedding of the endometrium during menstruation?
558.e: Involution of the corpus luteum results in a decrease in progesterone and estradiol secretion. This occurs around day 24 of a 28-day menstrual cycle. The loss of hormonal support causes endometrial shedding. LH, FSH, GnRH and estrogen are not involved in this process. Estradiol is primarily responsible for endometrial proliferation during the earlier phases of menstrual cycle. Reference : Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 21 st edition Page 3035

558.q: A girl with primary amenorrhea with normal ovaries, absent internal genitalia with normal external genitalia. Probable diagnosis?
558.e: The question says that the girl has normal ovaries which rules out. Turners syndrome where streak gonads are seen Noonan's syndrome Androgen insensitivity syndrome gonads are testis. So by exclusion our answer is Mayer-Rokitansky Kuster-Hauser Syndrome. Mullerian agenesis or mayer-okintansky-Kuster-hauser syndrome is a congenital malformation characterized by a failure of the Mullerian ducts to develop, resulting in absent uterus and variable malformations of the vagina, while both ovaries are intact and functioning. Ovaries are present and function normally so secondary sexual characteristics are normal. External genitalia are also normal as testosterone is absent. Reference : Speroff 7th/ed p 420-421.

558.q: Primary amenorrhea with absent uterus, normal breasts and scanty pubic hair is seen in:
558.e: The patient is presenting with primary amenorrhea along with well developed breast and scanty pubic hair and axillary hair -leave no doubt regarding Testicular feminisation syndrome as the diagnosis, which c/k/a AIS (Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome) Reference : Novak 14 th /ed, pg no: 1037-1038

558.q: A 16 year old child with primary amenorrhea with negative progesterone challenge test but positive combined progesterone and estrogen test. Diagnosis may be:
558.e: This child is presenting with primary amenorrhea with: Negative progesterone challenge test - which rules out PCOD (which may sometimes manifest as primary amenorrhea) When next step was done i.e., estrogen, progesterone combined test - lt comes out to be positive i.e., compartment I system (uterus, endometrium and outflow tract) is normal if properly stimulated by estrogen which rules out mullerian agenesis and Ashermann's syndrome. Positive estrogen progesterone combined test means the defect is in the production of estrogen i.e., either ovaries, pituitary, or hypothalamus. So from the given options we have to look for a cause which involves either of the above sites, which in this case is prolactinoma. Reference : Dutta Gynae 6 th /ed pg no: 467.

Kallmann’s syndrome is due to hypothalamic dysfunction characterised by a deficiency of gonadotropin releasing hormone (GnRH) causing a hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. This is associated with anosmia. It can occasionally be associated with optic problems, such as color blindness or optic atrophy, nerve deafness, cleft palate, cryptorchidism, renal agenesis, and mirror movement disorder. MRKH syndrome, also known as Mullerian agenesis, is due to anatomical absence of the uterus. This is the second most common cause of primary amenorrhea Turner’s syndrome is a type of gonadal dysgenesis and is overall the most common cause of primary amenorrhea Sheehan’s syndrome is postpartum pituitary necrosis. It leads to secondary amenorrhea and not primary amenorrhea. Reference: Shaw 15 th /ed, Page no:96-97

558.q: Pubertal events in girls which are not estrogen dependent?
558.e: The main hormone responsible for secondary sexual characteristics in females is estrogen. Estrogen leads to Breast development Growth spurt, i.e. height attained Production of cervical mucus Cornification of vaginal cells Menstruation (menstruation occurs due to withdrawal of progesterone in an oestrogen primed uterus). As far as hair growth is concerned – in females also the hormone responsible is Androgens (produced by adrenals and ovary) Reference: Williams Gynae 1st/ed p 315; Novak 14th/ed p 992, 15th/ed p 993

558.q: All are used in treating spasmodic dysmenorrhea except:
558.e: Spasmodic dysmenorrhoea is another name for primary dysmenorrhoea. The etiology of primary dysmenorrhea includes excessive amount of prostanoids secreted from the endometrium during menstruation. The prostanoids result in increased uterine contractions with a dysrhythmic pattern, increased basal tone, and increased active pressure. Pain is spasmodic in nature Pain of primary dysmenorrhea usually begins a few hours before or just after the onset of a menstrual period and may last 48 to 72 hours. Characteristics of spasmodic dysmenorrhoea Seen in adolescent girls Pain begins few hours before a rest of menstruation and lasts for 12–24 hours, but never 48 hours more than Management: NSAIDs, OCP’s can be used for management. Reference: Berek & Novak's gynecology 16th ed, p571

558.q: 17-year-old girl with height of 58 inches present with primary amenorrhea and rising FSH. The histological finding most consistent with her conditions is:
558.e: A height of 58 inches corresponds to approximately 147 cm. Which is short stature for a female of 16 years. Her FSH levels are rising, i.e., estrogen production is low i.e. there is an ovarian cause for 1° amenorrhea. Primary amenorrhea with short stature is seen in Turners syndrome. Turner syndrome (45 X) is the most common chromosomal abnormality causing gonadal failure, hence on histological examination their ovary should low oocyte count. These patients present with short stature. (Height They typically have many of the associated stigmata including lymph edema and sometimes large cystic hygromas of neck, webbed neck, coarctation of aorta, horseshoe kidneys. Reference: Novak's gynecology p 1038.

559.q: Most important structure preventing uterine prolapse is:
559.e: Supports of uterus have been discussed in detail earlier. Broad ligament (fold of peritoneum) and round ligaments are secondary supports of uterus and their role as support is doubtful. "Main support which prevents descent of the uterus is transverse cervical ligament (cardinal ligament) and its posterior extension the uterosacral ligament." Reference: Jeffcoate 7th/ed p 46

559.q: Gartner's cyst can be differentiated from cystocele by all except:
o: Presence of rugosities of overlying vaginal mucosa
559.e: Gartner’s cyst – are cysts of the remnants of Wolffian duct. M/C location = Anterolateral aspect of vagina and hence are often confused with cystocele. Features of Gartner’s cyst are: Upper three-fifths above the hymen develop from the fused uterovaginal canal of the Müllerian ducts. Rugosities of the overlying vaginal mucosa are lost. Vaginal mucosa over it becomes tense and shiny. Margins are well defined. Not reducible. No impulse on coughing Reference: Dutta Gynae 6th/ed p 210.

559.q: Most common complication of purandare's sling surgery?
559.e: The M/C complication of Purandare cervicopexy is deepening of pouch of douglas leading to enterocele formation. Enterocele can be prevented after purandare sling surgery by obliterating pouch of Douglas at the time of operation called Moscowitz repair. Reference : J B Sharma, Textbook of Gynecology 1 st edition p470

559.q: Shirodkar sling operation may be associated with all complications except:
559.e: As discussed in preceding text enterocele is a long term complication of purandare sling surgery and not of shirodkar's. Drawbacks of shirodhkar's sling surgery: Injury to sigmoid colon Intestinal obstruction Injury to ureter Hemorrhage from mesenteric vessels Injury to genitofemoral nerve present in psoas muscle Reference: J B Sharma, Textbook of Gynecology 1 st edition p470

559.q: A 65-year-old P3+0 female complains of procidentia. She has a past history significant of MI and is diabetic and hypertensive. Ideal management of prolapse in the patient is:
559.e: In females more than 60 years of age, who have medical complications like, in this patient previous H/O MI, hypertension and diabetes, Vaginal hysterectomy is not possible as the anesthetist will not agree to give anesthesia. In such patients procidentia/3° degree prolapse can be managed by Le fort's colpocleisis: In Le fort's repair/colpocleisis: The vaginal epithelium is removed followed by suturing of the anterior and posterior walls of denuded vagina therapy completely obliterating the vagina. The procedure is done under local anesthesia. Before performing this procedure, PAP smear and pelvic USG should be done to rule out cancers and pelvic pathology. Reference: Dutta Gynae. 5th/ed p 197-205; Shaw 15th/ed p

559.q: A 30 years old multipara has uterine prolapse, the management of choice is:
559.e: Fothergill's operation (Manchester Repair) is done in women below 40 years, who want to retain their menstrual function. The patient is less than 40 years and multiparous, so Fothergill's repair is the ideal management for them. Fothergill’s repair causes complications of pregnancy like incompetent os, habitual abortion and cervical dystocia therefore in a multipara who have completed their family we can do tubal ligation to prevent pregnancy. "If the family is completed, vaginal sterlization is to be done." Reference: Shaw 15th/ed p 339; Jeffocate 7th/ed p 289

559.q: A 30 years old multigravida presented with transverse lie with hand prolapse in IInd stage of labour with dead fetus. The treatment is:
559.e: Patient is presenting with a transverse lie with hand prolapse, i.e. the baby is dead so it should be managed as a dead baby with a transverse lie. Management in case of a dead baby with transverse lies – Cesarean section even in such cases, is much safer in the hands of those who are not conversant with destructive operations. Note: If this question is go for option a, i.e. LSCS, because in present day obstetrics there is no role of destructive procedures. Reference : Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 397, 585-587, Munrokerr 100/e, p 134, 135

559.q: Baldy webster operation is done in case of:
559.e: Surgeries for Retroversion Baldy webster operation Modified Gilliam’s operation Laparoscopic ventrosuspension Since round ligament helps to keep the uterus in an anteverted position in all these surgeries, round ligaments are tightened. Reference: Jeffcoates 8/e, page 274.

560.q: ECV is absolutely contraindicated in all except:
560.e: Absolute Contraindications for ECV: Placenta previa Uterine abnormalities (e.g., fibroids or structural anomalies) Contracted Pelvis, CPD Maternal medical conditions (e.g., severe hypertension, cardiac disease) Fetal distress or non-reassuring fetal heart rate patterns IUGR Multiple pregnancies Rupture of membranes, Oligohydramnios ECV is performed with caution and without force in patients with lower uterine scar. Its a relative contraindication Reference : Fernando Arias 4/e, p 374

560.q: Not true about red degeneration of myomas is:
o: Due to interference with blood supply
560.e: Let us see each option one by one. Red degeneration of fibroid commonly occurs during pregnancy. (Option “a” is correct) The pathogenesis of fibroid is obscure but the initial change appears to be one of subacute necrosis which is presumably due to an interference with its blood supply. Some say that arterial or venous thrombosis is the basis of this and the lesion is the result of infarction. (Option “c” is thus correct). Red degeneration should be managed conservatively with bed rest and analgesics to relieve the pain. (option “d” is thus correct) There is no need for surgical intervention. Reference: Shaw 15th/ed p 355.

560.q: A 24 years old female came with 2 years of infertility and sub mucosal fibroids. She was scheduled for a myomectomy. All of the following measures reduce bleeding during myomectomy except:
560.e: Measures to control blood loss during myomectomy Preoperative GnRH analogs Moderate degree of edelberg position to enhance venous return Timing the surgery in the immediate postmenstrual phase. Hypotensive anaesthesia (using sodium nitro pruside) Use of vasoconstrictive agents mainly vasopressin intraoperatively Use of victor Bonney’s myomectomy clamp around blood vessels and round ligament Use of tourniquets around blood vessels Uterine artery embolisation (UAE) Reference: Dutta Gynae 6th/ed p 604.

560.q: Regarding imaging of uterine fibroids all are correct except:
o: Ultrasound is ideal to confirm the diagnosis
Saline Infusion Sonography (SIS) is more sensitive to detect any submucous fibroid
MRI is superior to USG to identify the exact location of myoma
CT scanning is an alternative to MRI
560.e: The M/C investigation done to diagnose/detect fibroids is USG Three-dimensional ultrasonography can locate fibroids accurately. Although MRI is better (more accurate) than USG but is not routinely used as it is expensive and not widely available. -CT scan has a limited contrast resolution than MRI. For submucous fibroid hysteroscopy on saline infusion semiography can be done. Reference: Dutta Gynae 6th/ed p 278-279.

560.q: Treatment of red degeneration of fibroid in pregnancy:
560.e: Management of Red degeneration of fibroid. Patient is managed conservatively Patient is put to bed rest and given analgesics (to relieve the pain), sedatives and, if required antibiotics If because of mistaken diagnosis laparotomy is done, abdomen is closed without doing anything Myomectomy should never be contemplated during caesarean section as vascularity of fibroid is increased during pregnancy (due to increased estrogen) leading to increased blood loss during cesarean section. Reference : Shaw 14/e, pg 326; Dutta Obs. 6/e, pg 309; Jeffcoate 7/e, pg 502

560.q: Calcareous degeneration occurs most commonly in which type of fibroids:
560.e: "Calcareous degeneration usually involves the subserous fibroids with small peduncle or myomas of postmenopausal women. It is usually preceded by fatty degeneration. There is precipitation of calcium carbonate or calcium phosphate within the tumor, when whole of the tumor is converted into a calcified mass it is termed as 'womb stone' " Complications : Torsion Hemorrhage Infection Ascites; pseudo-Meigs syndrome (Produced by pedunculated subserous fibroid) Malignant change (rarest) Degenerations: Atrophy Red degeneration Hyaline degeneration (MC) Fatty degeneration or calcification Myxomatous degeneration Cystic degeneration Reference: Dutta Gynae 5th/ed p 265.

560.q: Submucosal fibroid is detected by all except:
560.e: Laparoscopy is not the best method for detecting submucosal fibroids as it is primarily used for other types of fibroids and other pelvic issues. Hysteroscopy -This method directly visualizes the uterine cavity and is very effective for detecting and treating submucosal fibroids. Hysterosalpingography -This radiologic technique can reveal filling defects in the uterine cavity caused by submucosal fibroids. USG (Transabdominal) -While it is less specific for detecting submucosal fibroids compared to other methods, it can still help in identifying fibroids and their locations. Laparoscopy (D)-This method is useful for detecting subserous fibroids or differentiating pedunculated fibroids from other pelvic masses but is not ideal for detecting submucosal fibroids directly. Reference : William's Gynae 1st/ed p 203; Dutta Gynae 6th/ed p 278.

560.q: Which of the following is a risk factor for inversion of uterus?
560.e: Placental implantation at the fundus, Uterine atony, Cord traction applied before placental separation, Abnormally adherent placentation seen with placenta accreta spectrum disorders Other risk factors are a short cord, uterine wall weakening at the implantation site, uterine tumors, and excessive fundal pressure. Reference: Williams obstetrics 26 th edition, chapter 42

561.q: A 19-year-old woman gives a history of sharp pain in the lower abdomen for 2 days every month approximately 2 weeks before the menses. The most probable etiology for her pain is:
561.e: A female giving a history of sharp pain in lower abdomen, every month, 2 weeks before the menstruation suggests mittelschmerz as the diagnosis. Mittelschmerz is synonymous to painful ovulation. Pain is associated with rupture of ovarian follicle at the time of ovulation Ref. Dutta Gynae 4th/ed p 172, 5th/ed p 178

Ans, D. Hysterectomy Hysterectomy is the treatment of choice. Local resection can be tried in younger women in whom it is localized. Medical treatment oPtions are NSAIDS & hormonal therapy, though not much effective GnRH, danazole, Mirena IUCD for menorrhagea & pain.

561.q: Cause of secondary dysmenorrhea in a young female are all except:
561.e: Causes of secondary dysmenorrhea: PID Endometriosis Adenomyosis IUCD Uterine fibroid Polyps Cervical stenosis Congenital malformation of uterus like bicornuate uterus Management : Treatment of the underlying cause. Reference: Berek & Novak's gynecology 16th ed, p580

o: Characterised by growth of endometrium outside uterus
Presents with menorrhagia, dysmenorrhea, and an enlarged uterus
561.e: (B) Adenomyosis is a condition where there is ingrowth of endometrium (both gland + stroma) directly into the myometrium. Earlier it was called Endometriosis interna It is more common in Multiparous females(i.e.option a is correct). (A) Adenomyosis is more common in women who have had children, so it is not most common in nulliparous women. (C) Adenomyosis commonly presents with symptoms such as menorrhagia (heavy menstrual bleeding), dysmenorrhea (painful periods), and an enlarged uterus. 60 (D) Adenomyosis is more common in women who are in their 40-50years , so it is not typically associated with younger women. Reference: Shaw 15th/ed pp 474-5; Novak 15th/ed pp 484-5.

Endometriosis sometimes occurs in abdominal wall scars following operations on uterus or tubes and is known as scar endometriosis. Operations most likely to be followed by scar endometriosis : Hysterotomy Classical cesarean section Myomectomy Ventrofixation Following operations for section of fallopian tube Following operations for removal of pelvic endometriosis Episiotomy Ref. Jeffcoate 7th/ed p 371

“Deep penetrating endometriosis is a form of the disease which was described by Koninck’s group. These lesions can extend 10 mm or more down from the peritoneal surface and the deeper lesions appear to have a closer association with pain than infertility, whereas less deep lesions have a closer association with infertility than pain.” Reference: Williams Gynae 1st/ed p 230 Reference: Novak 14th/ed p 1144, 15th/ed p 512

561.q: All are true regarding endometriosis, except:
o: Ovary is the most common site
561.e: Endometriosis is occurence of functioning endometrial tissue (glands + stroma) outside the uterine cavity. Whatever the initial genesis of endometriosis, its further development depends mainly on estrogen (Option “a”). It can occur anywhere in the body, Most common site being ovary (Option “d”). Can also involve lungs and pleura (Option “b”). In endometriosis the ovary contains tarry dark brown fluid (due to presence of blood pigments like hemosiderin) and cul de sac has yellow brown fluid. Clear fluid is not seen anywhere, So, Option “c” is incorrect. Reference: Shaw 15th/ed p 466.

561.q: All are used in treatment of endometriosis except:
561.e: Drugs used in the management of endometriosis Mnemonic - Proctor and Gamble Always Offer Good Deals Proctor –Progesterone -First line management → Injectable progestin-DMPA and → LNG-IUS → Oral progestins- continuous administration Gamble –GnRH analogue Always –Antiprogesterone-mifepristone Offer –OCP Good –Gestrinone Deals –Danazol Superficial peritoneal and ovarian implants may respond well to medical management but large endometriomas and extra pelvic endometriosis are unlikely to respond and will ultimately require surgical excision. Reference: Shaw 15th/ed pp 472-3; Novak 14th/ed pp 1164-9.

562.q: Which of the following is recommended for a newborn born to a mother suffering from acute viral hepatitis B infection?
562.e: HBIG is indicated for newborn infants of HBsAg-positive mothers, with initiation of the vaccine series at the same time, both within 12 hours of birth (administered at different injection sites). Infection at birth is associated with clinically silent acute infection but a 90% chance of chronic infection , whereas infection in young adulthood in immunocompetent persons is typically associated with clinically apparent acute hepatitis but a risk of chronicity of only ~1% Tenofovir is indicated in the management of chronic hepatitis B infection Reference : Harrison's Principles of internal medicine 21st ed chap 341 pg. 2592

562.q: As regard the PCOS and hyperinsulinemia:
o: Hyperinsulinemia is observed in about 40% to 80% of women with PCOS
Hyperinsulinemia stimulates hepatic synthesis of SHBG
Metformin has many other health benefits
562.e: Insulin resistance and compensatory hyperinsulinaemia is observed in about 40% of women with normal weight and 80% obese women with PCOS. Hyperinsulinemia results in decreased hepatic synthesis of SHBG and increased ovarian androgen biosynthesis. Metformin reduces weight, BMI fasting insulin levels, blood pressure and LDL cholesterol. Metformin does not cause hypoglycemia neither in normoglycaemic patients nor with diabetic individuals. Reference: Dutta Gynae 6 th /ed p 461-2, 470

562.q: Which of the following findings are seen in PCOS
562.e: There is no doubt that PCOS causes oligomenorrhea/amenorrhea, due to anovulation i.e.option a and b are correct. Pathologically - Ovaries are enlarged (2-5 times the normal size). Tunica albuginea is thickened. There is Theca cell hypertrophy (stromal hyperthecosis) and multiple follicular cysts are localized along the surface of the ovary (i.e.options 'c' is correct). Sonographic findings in case of PCOS include : ROTTERDAM CRITERIA >12 small cysts (2 to 9 mm in diameter) Increased ovarian volume (> 10 ml). Increased amount of stroma relative to the number of follicles. Only one ovary with these findings is sufficient to define PCOS. Other findings like Pearl necklace appear in which follicles are distributed underneath the capsule in a row. Reference: Shaw 15th/ed, pg 369-371

562.q: Which of the following are masculinizing tumors of the ovary?
562.e: Masculinizing Tumors develop from Sex cord of Embryonic gonad and include Arrhenoblastoma/Androblastoma Hilus cell Tm Adrenal cortical Tm/Lipoid cell Tm of ovary Gynandroblastoma Reference: Shaw 15 th /ed p 380-381

562.q: Which of the following chemotherapeutic regimens is among the most frequently used for treating germ cell tumors of the ovary?
o: POMB-ACE (Vincristine, Methotrexate, Bleomycin, Cisplatin, Etoposide, Actinomycin D, Cyclophosphamide)
562.e: The most frequently used chemotherapeutic regimens for germ cell tumors of the ovary are: BEP (Bleomycin, Etoposide, Cisplatin) EP (Etoposide, Cisplatin) EC (Etoposide, Carboplatin) These combinations are preferred due to their high efficacy and established use in clinical practice. BEP regimen details : Bleomycin : 30,000 IU on days 1, 8, and 15 every 3 weeks Etoposide : 100 mg/m2/day for 5 days every 3 weeks Cisplatin : 20 mg/m2/day for 5 days or 100 mg/m2 on day 1 every 3 weeks Explanation Of Other Options: VBP (Vinblastine, Bleomycin, Cisplatin) (Option B) & VAC (Vincristine, Actinomycin D, Cyclophosphamide) (Option C): While effective, VBP & VAC is less frequently used as first-line therapy compared to BEP and not considered a primary regimen in most guidelines. POMB-ACE (Option D): This is a complex multi-drug regimen used in refractory cases but not the most commonly used.

562.q: Which of the following is true about coeliac plexus block?
o: Located retroperitoneally at the level of L3
Useful for the painful conditions of lower abdomen
Most common side effect is diarrhea and hypotension
562.e: Answer- D (Most common side effect is diarrhea and hypotension) Celiac Plexus Block: Located retroperitoneally at the level of Ll Usually done bilaterallv Useful for the painful conditions of upper abdomen Most common side effect is diarrhea and hvpotension 89. Ovarian fossa is formed by all except? a) Obliterated umbilical artery b) Internal iliac artery c) Ureter d) Round ligament of ovary Correct Answer - D Each ovary lies in ovarian fossa on lateral pelvic wall which is bounded :?

562.q: All of the following are true about Kroonenberg's tumor except:
562.e: Krukenberg tumor: Krukenberg tumor by definition represents carcinoma of stomach metastasis to ovary . But the eponym is commonly used to denote any gastric cancer metastatic to ovary Tumor arises by retrograde lymphatic spread e. carcinoma cells pass from the stomach to the superior gastric lymph node which also receives lymphatics from the ovary. Characteristics of Krukenberg Tumour: Always bilateral Have smooth surface No tendency to form adhesions Freely mobile No infiltration through the capsule. Histologically the tumour has signet ring cells in the background of myxomatous stroma. They retain the shape of a normal ovary. Have waxy consistency. Reference : Shaw 15 th /ed pg 425-6; CGDT 10 th /ed pg 877

562.q: True regarding neoplasms of the ovary are:
o: Stromal invasion is commonly present in ovarian tumours of borderline malignancy
Lymphocytic infiltration is characteristic to dysgerminoma
Presence of ascites and pleural effusion in Brenner tumour indicates poor prognosis
562.e: Stromal invasion is absent. The epithelium shows multilayering, cellular atypia, pleomorphism and mitotic activity. Brenner tumour may present with the features of Meigs' syndrome and treatment prognosis is satisfactory. 20% of ovarian endometrioid carcinoma is associated with endometrial carcinoma. In postmenopausal women with unilocular cyst measuring 8–7 or less with normal several CA125 levels, expectant management is acceptable. Reference : Dutta Gynae 6 th /ed pg 384

563.q: The progesterone component of OCP acts by:
o: Bringing about alterations in cervical mucus
563.e: Actions of the progesterone component of combined oral contraceptives: Suppresses ovulation by its inhibitory action on the pituitary and the hypothalamus. This is predominantly achieved by estrogens but even by progesterone. Causes atrophic changes in the endometrium and prevents nidation even if fertilization occurs. Acts on the cervical mucus, making it thick and tenacious and impenetrable by sperms. The third-generation progestogens have a higher affinity for progesterone receptor and have a role in inhibiting ovulation. The main function of progestogens in combined pills is to counteract the undesirable effects of estrogen such as endometrial hyperplasia and heavy withdrawal bleeding. Reference: SK Chaudhary 7 th /ed pp 125-126, 14.

563.q: Maximum success after reversal of tubal ligation?
563.e: Ans, C. Clip method The Falope sialistic ring destroys 2-3 cm fallopian tube. The Hulka& Filshie clips destroya smaller segment (3-4mm)' thus preserving the potential of successful reversal of surgery. The failure rate varies between .2 and 15%"

563.q: Oral contraceptive pills decrease incidence of all of the following conditions except:
563.e: Cancers/cysts Uterine cancer Ovarian cancers Fibroid uterus (Progesterone only pills) Ovarian cysts Benign breast diseases Benign disease of genital tract Endometriosis (if used continuously) PID (here Salpingitis) Ectopic pregnancy (as it decreases incidence of PID) They decrease ovulation thus, are helpful in Dysmenorrhea, premenstrual tension and Mittelschmerz syndrome. By decreasing blood loss they are helpful in menorrhagia and polymenorrhea. Acne and hirsutism (especially those containing desogestrel) OCPs are also beneficial in: DUB Hormone therapy for hypothalamic amenorrhea Prevention of menstrual porphyria. Reference: Shaw 15 th /ed pp 231-232; Dutta Obs 6 th /ed p 545; Harrison 17 th /ed p 563

563.q: 34 years old lady using OCP since 5months presents with amenorrhea since 6 weeks. Which of the following is best to calculate gestational age in this case?
563.e: Naegeles formula is not used to calculate EDD but USG is done and CRL is used in cases of: Previous history of use of OCP prior to conception. Irregular cycles Patient doesn't remember her LMP Patient was breast feeding The best parameter to measure gestational age is Crown Rump Length(CRL).It is measured in the first trimester. 1 st trimester: CRL 2 nd trimester: Biparietal diameter(BPD)>Head circumference 3 rd Trimester: Femoral length

563.q: Lutein cysts are associated with all except:
563.e: Lutein cysts are usually bilateral and caused by excessive chorionic gonadotropin secreted in cases of gestational trophoblastic tumors. -These may also be formed with administration of gonadotropins or even clomiphene to induce ovulation. These are usually lined either by theca lutein cells called theca lutein cyst or by granulosa lutein cells, called granulosa lutein cyst. Spontaneous regression is expected within a few weeks following effective therapy of the tumors with the gonadotropin level returning back to normal. Reference : Dutta Gynae 6 th /ed pg 290

563.q: OCP's intake causes psychiatric symptoms, and abdominal pain. Diagnosis is:
563.e: Patients taking OCP's and presenting with abdominal pain and psychiatric problems, diagnosis is undoubtedly acute intermittent porphyria as OCP's can precipitate porphyria. Reference: Harrison 17 th /ed p 2439

563.q: All of the following are LARC methods except:
563.e: LARC method of contraception are Long acting Reversible contraceptive methods: LARC methods include: LARC Infection: DMPA/NET-en Implants-Implanon, Norplant IUCD: CuT, LNG IUCD. Transdermal patches Vaginal ring Reference: Leon Speroff 7 th /ed p 842; 8 th /ed p 926

563.q: Definite use for PGE2 is all except ?
563.e: Ans. A. Contraception om 1316. All of the following occurs because of prostaglandin use except? a) Excess water retention b) Flushes c) Increased motility of bowel d) Nausea Correct Answer - A Ans, A. Excess water retention Disadvantages & side effects of prostaglandins

o: It does not increase the risk of HIV
Treatment of male partners reduces recurrence.
Pregnant women should be routinely screened for bacterial vaginosis.
Atopobium vagina is associated with recurrence.
564.e: Associated with increased risk of acquiring HIV, C. trachomatis, and N. gonorrhoeae. Treatment of male partners with metronidazole does not prevent recurrence of bacterial vaginosis. Recurrence: Metronidazole gel twice weekly for >3 months Recommendation is against routine screening of pregnant women for bacterial vaginosis. Reference: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 21 st ed, Ch: 136, Pg: 1083

564.q: A 46-year-old female suffering from severe menorrhagia underwent hysterectomy 6 years back. She wishes to take hormone replacement therapy. I/V/O hot flushes and atrophic vaginitis.The treatment of choice is:
564.e: Both estrogen alone or estrogen + progesterone can be used for treating menopausal symptoms. The choice depends on whether the uterus is present or not. "For women with a uterus, a progestin should be combined with an estrogen, to lower the risk of endometrial cancer." All women who have intact uterus should receive combined estrogen - progesterone therapy. Reference: Williams Gynae 1st/ed pp 495, 499-500

564.q: A young lady presents to your office with a complaint of copious vaginal discharge, but there is no cervical discharge on per speculum examination. Which of the following should be given for the management?
564.e: Syndromic management of sexually transmitted infections (WHO 1991) Principle: Treatment of STDs should be initiated at the patient's first visit to a clinic. At the same time the couple is counseled about the importance of condom use and prevention of STD transmission. Syndromic managements are based on epidemiological studies all over the world. Syndromic diagnosis and laboratory assisted diagnosis have been found similar in terms of accuracy. Method: Management is done by criteria for syndromic diagnosis of PID. These include detection of vaginal discharge abdominal pain, cervical motion tenderness, bilateral adnexal providers are trained up to follow a standardized protocol (flow chart) to treat such a patient. This is particularly suitable in a health care setting of developing countries. Reference: Dutta Gynae 6 th /ed p 176; Internet search-www. naconlinr.org/upload/publication/ste

564.q: Which of the below infections of vagina occurs in acidic pH
564.e: Candida is M/C vaginitis in: – Pregnancy, diabetes – Immunocompromised – OCP users, steroid users, antibiotic users Symptoms: intense pruritus Curdy white vaginal discharge Signs: yeasty curdy white vaginal discharge Cervix normal Diagnosis: sabouraud's media Fungal hyphae in 10% KOH preparation pH Reference : J B Sharma, Textbook of Gynecology 1st edition p340

564.q: Amsel's criteria of bacterial vaginosis includes all except
o: White, milky, nonviscous, adherent vaginal discharge
564.e: Bacterial vaginosis occurs due to alteration of vaginal flora; lactobacilli decrease whereas coccobacilli and Gardnerella increase. Amsel’s criteria includes: White milky, non viscous, adherent vaginal discharge Vaginal pH more than 4.5 Positive whiff test: amine odour with 10% KOH Presence of clue cells Increase in number of gardnerella vaginalis and reduced number of lactobacilli Treatment: tab. Metronidazole 2 g single dose or tinidazole or clindamycin 300 mg BD for 7 days Reference: J B Sharma, Textbook of Gynecology 1 st edition p333

564.q: Regarding bacterial vaginosis, all are true except:
o: Homogeneous vaginal discharge with pH 5.0 to 6.0
Positive clue cells in 100% of cases
It is due to Gardnerella vaginalis
564.e: Clue cells are diagnostic but about 40% patients may not have clue cells. Reference: Dutta Gynae 6th/ed p 152

564.q: All are benign lesions of vagina except:
564.e: Benign lesions of vagina: Congenital malformations Infections Ulcers Scarring Stenosis DES induced lesions Granulation tissue Cysts Reference: JB Sharma textbook of Gynecology e1 p 497

564.q: Most common gynecological problem in prepubertal girls is
564.e: Vulvovaginitis occurs due to lack of estrogen. Most commonly seen in children. Causes Foreign body Worm infestation Tuberculosis Infections such as candida Symptoms are intense pruritus and offensive vaginal discharge. Estrogen cream and treatment of infections are done for its management. Reference: J B Sharma, Textbook of Gynecology 1 st edition p332

566.q: A 16-year-old boy is being treated with desmopressin for diabetes insipidus. His plasma glucose level (fasting) is 108 mg/dl, sodium 139 mmol/l (137-144), potassium 4.5 mmol/l (3.5-4.9) and calcium 10.9 mg/dl. He still has complaints of polyuria, polydipsia and nocturia. What could be the most probable cause?
566.e: This boy most probably has nephrogenic diabetes insipidus due to hypercalcemia. In this condition, renal tubules are resistant to antidiuretic hormone (ADH), which is due to a receptor defect of vasopressin-2 receptor or a post-receptor defect in an ADH-sensitive water channel called aquaporin-2. Central DI (ADH deficiency) show good response to desmopressin (V2 agonist) administration. The findings do not suggest diabetes mellitus, which is also associated with these symptoms. In patients with the syndrome of inappropriate secretion of ADH (SIADH), low sodium levels are the hallmark. Metabolic causes of Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus: Chronic Hypokalemia Chronic Hypercalcemia Reference : Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 21 st edition Page 2920

566.q: Kalindi 25 years female admitted as a case of septic abortion with tricuspid valve endocarditis. Vegetation from the valve likely to affect is:
566.e: "Right sided endocarditis which usually involves the tricuspid valve causes septic pulmonary emboli occasionally with infarction and lung abscesses." Reference: CMDT '07, p 1447

566.q: The preferred site for obtaining cultures in a patient with acute PID during laparotomy is,
566.e: For identification of organisms in PID the materials are collected from the following available sources: Discharge from urethra or Bartholin’s gland Cervical canal Collected pus from the fallopian tubes during laparoscopy or laparotomy. The material collected is subjected to Gram’s stain and culture (aerobic/anaerobic). The findings of Gram-negative diplococci is suggestive of gonococcal infection. Reference: Dutta Gynae 6th/ed pg 130

566.q: During laparoscopy, the preferred site for obtaining cultures in a patient with acute PID is:
566.e: According to: For identification of organisms in PID the materials are collected from the following available sources: Discharge from urethra or Bartholin’s gland Cervical canal Collected pus from the fallopian tubes during laparoscopy or laparotomy. The material collected is subjected to Gram’s stain and culture (aerobic/anaerobic). The findings of Gram-negative diplococci is very much suggestive of gonococcal infection. Reference : Telinde Operative Gynae 9th/ed pg 678, 679; Reference : Dutta Gynecology 6th/ed pg 126

After birth-related epithelial trauma and healing, fragments of stratified epithelium occasionally is embedded beneath the vaginal surface. Similar to its native tissue, this buried epithelium continues to shed degenerated cells . As a result, epidermal inclusion cysts are formed, which are filled with debris . Reference: williams obstetrics 26th edition chapter 2

566.q: All are the sequelae of PID except
566.e: A): Ectopic pregnancy - This is correct. PID can lead to scarring and damage to the fallopian tubes, increasing the risk of ectopic pregnancy. (B): Chronic pelvic pain - This is correct. PID can cause inflammation and scarring in the pelvic organs, leading to persistent pain. (C): Multiple pregnancy - This is incorrect. Multiple pregnancy is not a recognized sequelae of PID. (D): Dyspareunia - This is correct. Dyspareunia, or painful sexual intercourse, can result from the pelvic inflammation and scarring associated with PID Reference: J B Sharma, Textbook of Gynecology 1st edition p353

566.q: In a pregnant woman with heart disease, all of the following are to be done except:
566.e: Methergine after delivery. Methyl ergometrine is contraindicated in patients with heart disease. Reference: Dutta Obs. 7/e, p 278

566.q: Hormone replacement therapy, absolute contraindication is:
566.e: Contraindications are: A = A ctive liver disease B = Undiagnosed vaginal B leeding C = C ancers → endometrial/breast D = D VT Ref. Novak 15th/ed p 1245.

567.q: Most common malignancy of fallopian tube
Which of the following pelvic structures is not developed from urogenital sinus?
567.e: The cloaca (endodermal) is divided by formation of the urorectal septum by the seventh week (7 th ) and is separated to create the rectum and the urogenital sinus. Urogenital sinus has 3 parts The cephalad or vesicle portion → urinary bladder The middle or pelvic portion → female urethra The caudal or phallic part → distal 1/3 of vagina (sinovaginal bulb) and the greater vestibular (Bartholin), urethral, and paraurethral (Skene) glands Reference : William's Obstetrics 25th Edition, chapter 7, page no. 121

567.q: Which one of the following congenital malformations of the fetus can be diagnosed in the first trimester by ultrasound?
567.e: As discussed in chapter on fetal malformation, anencephaly can be diagnosed as early as 8-10 weeks/first trimester in experienced hands. Microcephaly: - USG in Obs and Gynae Callen 4/e, p 298, 299 It has decreased head size. In these patients both brain mass and total cell number are reduced. There is a disproportion in size between the skull and face. It is difficult to recognize this anomaly by ultrasound - A head circumference below 2 SD from the mean is used as a diagnostic criteria in midtrimester scan. Holoprosencephaly is the presence of a single centrally placed cerebral ventricle and may be associated with midline abnormalities of the face. With the use of a vaginal probe it can be recognised in the beginning of midtrimester. Reference: Williams Obs. 21/e, p 1120; USG in Obs. and Gynae by Callen 4/e, p 284, Fernando Arias 3/e, p 64, 66, 69

567.q: A pregnant mother is treated with oral anticoagulant. The likely congenital malformation that may result in the fetus is:
567.e: Warfarin is an anticoagulant drug. Action : Interferes with the synthesis of the vitamin K dependent factors like II, VII, IX and X. Side effects: Hemorrhage It leads to: – Contradi’s syndrome : skeletal and facial anomalies in the fetus Chondrodysplasia punctata in the fetus. Miscarriage, IUGR and stillbirths accentuates neonatal hypothrombinemia. Reference : Dutta Obs. 7/e, pg 511

567.q: Most common menstrual complaint in patients of genital TB is
