Club foot can be primary or secondary Primary Idiopathic (MC) Secondary Neurological disorders Spina bifida Meningomyelocele Myelodysplasia Poliomyelitis Syndromes Arthrogryposis Multiplex Congenita Larsen's syndrome Reference: Miler's 8th Edition of Review of Orthopaedics, page no. 600

According to Ponseti technique cavus is corrected first. The order of correction is given by the mnemonic - CAVE- Cavus followed by Adductus and varus and equinus is corrected as the last step Treatment is started within 1st week of life. The cavus aspect of the deformity is corrected first, followed by the adduction, then varus and lastly equinus. After every manipulation, an above-knee POP cast is applied, which is changed every 5-7 days. It is usually possible to correct all components of the deformity within 6 weeks. The equinus deformity often remains undercorrected, and can be treated by percutaneous tenotomy of tendoachilles. The cut tendoachilles regenerates spontaneous Reference: Essential orthopedics by Maheshwari 7 th edition page no 210.

675.q: A child is born with CTEV (Congenital Talipes Equinus Varus). All of the following can be the causes except
675.e: Primary (Congenital clubfoot ) : Cases where clubfoot may be present since birth include: Idiopathic (most common type) Neurogenic-Spina bifida Dysplastic-Arthrogryposis multiplex congenital (AMC). Secondary (Acquired clubfoot) : In some diseases a muscle imbalance may result, causing contracture of the posteromedial foot structures leading to a secondary CTEV anytime during life. Paralytic (Poliomyelitis) Post-traumatic-contracted scar on posteromedial aspect Post infective. Spastic (Cerebral palsy). Reference- MAHESHWARI ORTHO 5 TH EDITION PAGE NO 212.

676.e: Parsonage Turner syndrome is brachial plexus neuritis. It is an uncommon disorder characterized by severe shoulder pain followed by patchy muscle paralysis and sensory loss involving the shoulder girdle and upper extremity. Reference: Miler's 8th Edition of Review of Orthopaedics, page no. 1513

676.q: Most common cause of osteomyelitis in sickle cell disease is
676.e: Bacterial causes of acute hematogenous and direct osteomyelitis include the following: Most common organism causing acute osteomyelitis: Staph. Aureus MCC of osteomyelitis in sickle cell anemia patient: SALMONELLA MCC of osteomyelitis in IV drug abuser: PSEUDOMONAS MC organism causing osteomyelitis in open foot injury: PSEUDOMONAS MC organism causing osteomyelitis in HIV patient: Staph. Aureus MC organism causing osteomyelitis in case of animal bite: Pasteurella Multiocida MC organism causing osteomyelitis in case of human bite: Eikenella Corrodens Reference: Maheshwari Essential Orthopedics, 5th ed, Pg: 168.

676.q: All are risk factors of DDH except
676.e: Twin pregnancy is not a risk factor for DDH Risk factors of DDH are First born child Female child Fetal malposition - Breech (MC) Family history of DDH Oligohydramnios Reference: Miler's 8th Edition of Review of Orthopaedics, page no. 558

676.q: All of the following can cause painful limp in a child except
676.e: The only 2 conditions that produce painless limping in a child are: Congenital coxa vara Early stage of Perthe's disease. In later stages, Perthe's disease will also become painful.

676.q: Which of the following is not seen in Marie - Strumpell disease?
676.e: Marie Strumpell disease is just another name for ankylosing spondylosis. The extra articular manifestations of ankylosing spondylosis are Atlantoaxial subluxation Anterior uveitis Apical fibrosis Aortic regurgitation AV conduction block Ig A nephropathy Amyloidosis Achilles enthesitis Reference: J. Maheshwari's 5th Edition of Essential Orthopaedics page no. 290

676.q: Which of the following is not a poor prognostic sign of Perthe's disease
676.e: The poor prognostic signs of Perthe's disease are called Head at risk signs. Head at risk signs are Gage sign - V shaped radiolucency in the lateral aspect of the physis. Calcification lateral to epiphysis Horizontal physis Lateral subluxation of the femoral head Metaphyseal cysts Separation of physis is a feature of SCFE and no Perthe's disease. Reference: Tachdjian's Pediatric Orthopaedics 5th edition page no. 605

677.q: A 16-year-old child presented with rickets and deformities. Doctors are planning the surgical correction of these deformities. When can surgery be done?
o: After white line is visible on X-ray
677.e: The methods to evaluate recovery in rickets are X ray There will be an appearance of a white line in the metaphysis. This is called the 'White line of Frankel' Blood tests first change to be seen - increase in phosphate levels End point - normal ALP Surgery should be done only after the rickets have been completely cured and bone healing has completely taken place. This is indicated by normal ALP. Reference: Miler's 8th Edition of Review of Orthopaedics, page no. 81

677.q: Stoss regimen is used in the treatment of which condition?
677.e: Stoss regimen is a vitamin D supplementation method used for the treatment of rickets. Here a single dose of vitamin D - 3L to 6L IU is given as an oral dose or as an IM injection. Reference: J. Maheshwari's 5th Edition of Essential Orthopaedics page no. 311

677.q: All are true regarding osteopetrosis except
677.e: Fracture healing is normal in osteopetrosis. Osteopetrosis is also called Marble bone disease/Albers Schonberg disease It is a congenital condition characterized by defective osteoclastic resorption of immature bone resulting in its accumulation through out the skeleton, causing increased frequency of long bone fractures, cranial nerve palsies, pancytopenia and low back pain. Clinical feature include Low back pain Pathological fractures Progressive anemia Severe infections : Mandible osteomyelitis Easy bruising Failure to thrive Cranial N 2, 7, 8 palsy leading to blindness and deafness Reference: Miler's 8th Edition of Review of Orthopaedics, page no. 688

677.q: A 4 year old child presented with progressive anemia, hepatomegaly and osteomyelitis of jaw. X ray shows diffuse sclerosis of bone . What could be the diagnosis?
677.e: Osteomyelitis of jaw in a child is the classical feature of osteopetrosis. Osteopetrosis is also called Marble bone disease/Albers Schonberg disease It is a congenital condition characterized by defective osteoclastic resorption of immature bone, resulting in its accumulation throughout the skeleton, causing increased frequency of long bone fractures, cranial nerve palsies, pancytopenia and low back pain. Clinical feature include: Low back pain Pathological fractures Progressive anemia Severe infections : Mandible osteomyelitis Easy bruising Failure to thrive Cranial N 2, 7, 8 palsy leading to blindness and deafness Reference: J. Maheshwari's 5th Edition of Essential Orthopaedics page no. 317

677.q: Which of the following is not seen in rickets?
677.e: Phosphate levels will be reduced in rickets. The biochemical changes in rickets are: Calcium - ↓ / N PTH - ↑ Serum PO4 - ↓ Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP) - ↑ Serum Vit D - ↓ Reference: J. Maheshwari's 5th Edition of Essential Orthopaedics page no. 311

677.q: A 6-year-old child presented with bleeding gums and rosary-like thickening of the costochondral junctions, which are angular and painful. What is the diagnosis?
677.e: There are 2 conditions that can produce rosary in the chest wall - rickets and scurvy. In rickets, the rosary is painless and rounded. However, in scurvy, they are painful and angular. This child has painful angular rosary and there is gum bleeding, both point towards scurvy. Reference: J. Maheshwari's 5th Edition of Essential Orthopaedics page no. 315

677.q: A 7 month old child is brought to the OPD with signs, symptoms and biochemical changes of rickets. Which of the following findings is unlikely to be found in this child?
677.e: Long bones of legs get deformed only after the child starts weight bearing, so a 7 month old child will never develop deformities of lower limb. Clinical features of rickets: Craniotabes(earliest sign) Frontal bossing Rachitic rosary Harrison's groove Pectus carinatum(pigeon chest) Broadening of the ends of long bones, most prominently around wrists and knees. It is seen around 6-9 months of age. Delayed teeth eruption is noticed in infants. Muscular hypotonic: The child's abdomen becomes protuberant(pot belly) because of marked muscular hypotonia. Visceroptosis and lumbar lordosis can occur. Deformities: Deformities of the long bones develop, once the child starts walking. The most common deformity is bilateral genu varum, also called bow legs. Reference: Maheshwari Ortho, 5 th edition, Page no. 311.

677.q: Most common childhood tumor metastasizing to the bones is
677.e: Common primary sites for bone metastasis In males: Prostate followed by lung In females: Breast followed by lung In children: Neuroblastoma Overall: Breast followed by prostate and then lung Reference: Maheshwari Essential ortho, 5 th edition, Page no. 236.

678.q: The commonest cause of pathological fracture worldwide is?
678.e: Most common cause of pathological fracture is osteoporosis . In India, however the most common cause is Nutritional deficiencies. Reference- Rockwood and green’s adult fracture 8ᵗʰ edition, page-671

678.q: In comparison of two patient. Patient-1 is 34yr old female with pathological fracture of shaft of femur due to metastasis of breast cancer and patient-2 is 64year old female with pathological fracture of shaft femur due to osteoporosis. Which of the following is true?
o: Patient -1 will have delayed union compared to patient-2
Patient -2 will have delayed union compared to patient-1
Both fractures will unite in the same time
678.e: Osteoporotic pathological fracture has good prognosis because it follows natural process of bone healing but with some delay. But pathological fracture of malignant lesion has very poor potential for healing and usually ends up in nonunion. Reference- Rockwood and green’s adult fracture 8ᵗʰ edition, page-678

678.q: A lady with osteoporosis is on prolonged bisphosphonates. She develops pain in her right hip. Next investigation is?
678.e: In this case, we have to get an x-ray to rule out an atypical fracture. One of the complications of prolonged bisphosphonate therapy is the development of atypical fractures. Atypical fractures occurs after drug usage of more than 5-7 year It occurs due to the defective remodeling of bones, resulting from osteoclast suppression by bisphosphonates. These fractures are commonly seen in the sub-trochanteric region of the femur. These are called atypical fractures because they involve the lateral cortex and not the medial cortex of bone as is typically seen. Reference: Koval's Handbook of fracture's 5th edition, page no. 375

678.q: FRAX score is related to which condition?
678.e: FRAX score is related to osteoporosis FRAX is Fracture Risk Assessment Score It was a questionnaire based scoring system developed by WHO to calculate the 10-year risk of major fractures in patients with osteoporosis. Reference: Miler's 8th Edition of Review of Orthopaedics, page no. 2016

Phosphate levels will be reduced in osteomalacia. The biochemical changes in osteomalacia are: Calcium - ↓ / N PTH - ↑ Serum PO 4 - ↓ Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP) - ↑ Serum Vit D - ↓ Reference: J. Maheshwari's 5th Edition of Essential Orthopaedics page no. 312

678.q: Most common cause of pathological fracture is
678.e: Pathological fractures occurs in a bone which is already weakened by an underlying pathology MC cause worldwide: Osteoporosis MC cause in India : Nutritional causes MC local cause: Malignancy MC bone involved: Thoracic vertebra Reference: J. Maheshwari's 5th Edition of Essential Orthopaedics page no. 4

678.q: When treating osteoporosis with alendronate, what is the most common side effect?
678.e: Alendronate is generally given orally in a dose of 70 mg/week. Patient is advised to take 6–8 oz of water and not to lie down for at least half an hour as these can cause gastritis and esophagitis. Reference: Manish Kumar Varshney, 1 st edition, Page no. 84.

678.q: What bone disease would result from a loss of osteoprotegrin(OPG) protein?
678.e: Osteoprotegerin(OPG) is a member of the TNF receptor family but it is secreted and acts like a cytokine. OPG has bone protective properties by inhibiting osteoclast development and activation. Osteoprotegerin is a decoy receptor which binds and thereby opposes RANK ligand. RANK ligand is the primary agent that activates osteoclasts and causes bone resorption. Hence, the loss of OPG will result in excessive bone resorption by osteoclasts causing osteoporosis. Reference: Manish kumar varshney, 1 st edition, Page no. 67.

679.q: Woven bone is found in all of the following except
o: Around the growth plate in children
Cancellous bone of femur in adults
679.e: Woven bone is immature bone seen during embryonal development. Woven bone is week and is slowly replaced by stronger lamellar bone during development. Woven bone is almost completely replaced by 2 years of age. However, there are conditions where, woven bone can be seen even after 2 years of age. Eg Around the growth plates in growing children During fracture healing Pathologies of bone Paget's disease Fibrous dysplasia Osteogenic tumors - osteogenic sarcoma, osteoblastoma etc. Reference: Miler's 8th Edition of Review of Orthopaedics, page no. 20. Reference: Kulkarni's 3rd edition of Textbook of Orthopaedics and Trauma page no. 161

679.q: Blade of grass lesion is seen in which of the following conditions?
679.e: Blade of grass lesion is an elongated V shaped lytic area in the diaphysis of long bones, seen in Paget's disease. Paget's disease is a disorder of abnormal bone turnover. It is a chronic disease of bone remodeling characterized by abnormal osteoclastic activity(and later by increased osteoblastic activity) resulting in replacement of normal bone with excessive, weak and hyper-vascular bone. X-ray findings depend on the phase of Paget's disease Lytic phase Flame shaped/Blade of grass appearance Osteoporosis circimscripta Mixed phase Picture frame vertebra Ivory vertebra Cotton wool skull Blastic phase Tam O shanter skull Reference: Manish kumar varshney, 1 st edition, Page no.86.

679.q: Which is the drug of choice in Paget's disease?
679.e: Drug of choice in Paget's disease are bisphosphonates which reduce bone turnover and increase lamellar bone formation. The only bisphosphonate in the options is Alendronate. Calcitonin is very useful in relieving the pain in Paget's disease and decreasing bone resorption but the effect is only temporary. Calcium and vitamin D should also be supplemented. Pathological fractures usually require surgery and internal fixation. Reference: Fundamentals of Orthopaedics Mohindra and Jain, Page no. 338.

679.q: What laboratory findings would you expect to find in a patient newly diagnosed with renal osteodystrophy?
o: Decreased PTH secretion, hypophosphatemia and hypocalcemia
Increased PTH secretion, hyperphosphatemia and hypocalcemia
Decreased PTH secretion, hypophosphatemia and hypercalcemia
Increased PTH secretion, hyperphosphatemia and hypercalcemia
679.e: Decreased calcium, increased serum phosphate, increased alkaline phosphatase and increased parathyroid hormone are all characteristic of renal osteodystrophy Renal osteodystrophy is characterized by bone mineralization deficiency due to the electrolyte and endocrine abnormalities associated with chronic kidney disease. The pathogenesis of renal osteodystrophy is multifactorial. Hypocalcemia occurs due to the inability of the damaged kidney to convert vitamin D3 into its active form, calcitriol and because there is loss of calcium through urine. There will also be phosphate retention as the failed kidneys cannot excrete phosphates. The hypocalcemia and lack of phosphate excretion by the damaged kidney causes hyperparathyroidism and secondary hyperphosphatemia. Reference: Manish Kumar Varshney, page no, 33, 1 st edition.

679.q: What is Von Recklinghausen disease of bone?
679.e: 'Von Recklinghausen disease of bone' is another name for the destructive bone changes seen in hyperparathyroidism. 'Von Recklinghausen disease' is neurofibromatosis type I. Reference: J. Maheshwari's 5th Edition of Essential Orthopaedics page no. 317

Deafness in Paget's disease is both conductive and sensorineural. Conductive because of the narrowing of the external auditory meatus and sclerosis of the ear ossicles. Sensorineural because of the narrowing of the cranial nerve foramina, resulting in the compression of the vestibulocochlear nerve. Reference: Miler's 8th Edition of Review of Orthopaedics, page no. 1904

680.q: Which of the following pairs of structures are antagonist to each other around the ankle joint?
680.e: PL&TA are antagonist to each other as PL plantar flexes and TA dorsiflexes ankle joint. PB & PT are antagonist to each other as PB everts the foot and PT inverts the ankle joint. Reference - Manish Kumar Varshney 1 st edition page no 1242

680.q: A 35-year-old man presents to the emergency department with pain and swelling of the right knee for the past three days. Also, for the past two days, he has felt feverish. The patient is able to ambulate, but walking exacerbates the pain in his knee. Temperature is 39.3°C (102.7°F). On physical examination, the right knee is red, warm to touch, and tender. A large effusion is noted. Which of the following diagnostic studies of the knee is the most appropriate initial step?
680.e: The clinical presentation described, is characteristic of septic arthritis of knee joint. The best method for confirming the diagnosis is to aspirate the knee joint to look for pus. The process of joint aspiration is also called arthrocentesis. Option B- Arthroscopy, is incorrect because this study is not the initial step in diagnosis. Option C- Bone scan, is incorrect because this study is appropriate to nonspecifically localize areas of inflammation but cannot be used to distinguish infectious from sterile processes. Option D- CT scan, and Option (E), MRI, are incorrect because these studies are more sensitive for diagnosing osteomyelitis and periarticular abscesses. Reference- Maheshwari Ortho 5th edition, page no 170.

680.q: Which deformity of tibia is seen in the triple deformity of the knee?
680.e: Triple deformity of knee consists of posterior subluxation of tibia, external rotation of tibia and flexion. The mnemonic ‘P ER F’ can be used to remember this. Triple deformity is classically seen in late stages of TB of knee joint. Rarely rheumatoid arthritis can also produce similar deformity. Reference: Apley’s System of Orthopaedics and Fractures, 8th Edition, Page Number-42.

680.q: Which joint is more commonly involved in pseudo gout?
680.e: The most common joint involved in various pathologies. Septic arthritis- Knee joint Gout- MP joint of great toe Pseudo gout- Knee joint Rheumatoid arthritis- Metacarpophalangeal joint Ankylosing spondylitis- Sacroiliac joint Osteoarthritis- Knee joint> Hip joint Senile osteoporosis- Vertebrae Paget’s disease- Pelvic bone > Femur > Vertebrae Osteochondritis dissecans Knee joint Reference- Essential Orthopedics Maheshwari 5 th edition page no 293

680.q: Which joint is more commonly involved in GOUT?
680.e: Septic arthritis- Knee joint Gout- MTP joint of great toe Pseudo gout- Knee joint Rheumatoid arthritis- Metacarpophalangeal joint Ankylosing spondylitis- Sacroiliac joint Osteoarthritis- Knee joint> Hip joint Senile osteoporosis- Vertebrae Paget’s disease- Pelvic bone > Femur > Vertebrae Osteochondritis dessicans- Knee joint Reference- Essential Orthopedics Maheshwari 5 th edition page no 293

680.q: A 4 year old child presents with mild fever, right hip pain and decreased appetite for 3 days. O/E she has fullness in Scarpa's triangle, hip is flexed, abducted and externally rotated and mild restriction of movements in the hip. What is the diagnosis ?
680.e: When a child presents with hip pain and FABER deformity of the hip, there are 2 DDs - transient synovitis or septic arthritis. In this case, there is mild fever and only mild restriction of movements, so the diagnosis is transient synovitis of hip. In septic arthritis, there will be high grade fever and severe restriction of hip movements. Reference: J. Maheshwari's 5th Edition of Essential Orthopaedics page no. 181

680.q: Which of the following is not seen in coxa vara?
680.e: Telescoping of hip is seen in unstable hip and not in coxa vara. Causes of telescopy can be DDH, Tom Smith arthritis, surgical excision of femoral head etc. Coxa vara is the condition characterized by a reduction in the neck shaft angle. Clinical features of coxa vara are Adduction, External rotation deformity Limitation of Abduction and Internal rotation Shortening Trendelenburg sign + Axis deviation Reference :Tachdjian's Pediatric Orthopaedics 5th edition page no. 667

680.q: HONG KONG operation is done for?
680.e: Hong Kong procedure(Radical anterior decompression and spinal fusion): It is a radical anterior debridement of spine followed by removal of diseased vertebral body and bone grafting in the area of the removed body. It helps in early healing of the disease and prevents also a deformity in better way, but needs appropriate facilities. It is usually done in cervical spine TB. Reference: Maheshwari Essential Orthopedics, 7 th edition, Page no. 200.

681.q: A 25-year-old football player sustains a blow to the arm during a match. He develops temporary weakness and tingling, but recovers completely within 6 weeks without surgical intervention. Which of the following best describes neuropraxia?
681.e: Explanation: Neuropraxia is the mildest form of peripheral nerve injury , as described in Seddon's classification . In this condition, the axon remains intact, but there is focal demyelination or damage to the myelin sheath due to compression or ischemia. Conduction block occurs across the site of injury, leading to weakness or sensory loss. Since the axon and endoneurial tubes are preserved, full recovery occurs within weeks to months without Wallerian degeneration. Explanation of other options: Damaged axon, intact nerve sheath (Option B): Describes axonotmesis , where axons are damaged but connective tissue sheaths remain intact. Damaged axon and nerve sheath (Option C): Describes neurotmesis , the most severe form of injury, with a poor prognosis.

681.q: A man slept with head over forearm, next morning he complains of tingling, numbness over forearm. It is caused by ?
681.e: Ans.C . Sensitivity to hypoxia is C>B>A Type C fibers (Type IV Lloyd & Hunt) are least susceptible to hypoxia'

681.q: Which of the following is not an indication of external fixator?
o: Closed fracture of upper tibia with compartment syndrome and blisters over skin
Closed fracture shaft humerus with Radial nerve palsy
Fracture with burns wound over fracture site
681.e: Indications of external fixator Open fracture (grade 3b-3c- absolute indication, grade-2-3a-relative indication) Vascular injury Severe soft tissue injury Damage control orthopedics Nerve injury is not an indication of external fixation Reference- AO manual of principle of fracture management

681.q: Carpal Tunnel syndrome is seen in all except
681.e: CTS is associated with Colles fracture and not Smith's fracture. Most of the CTS is idiopathic, however there are several risk factors such as: Hypothyroidism Diabetes Acromegaly Rheumatoid arthritis Pregnancy Gout Alcoholism Amyloidosis Sarcoidosis Malunited Colles fracture Reference: J. Maheshwari's 5th Edition of Essential Orthopaedics page no. 114

681.q: Carpal tunnel syndrome is caused by all EXCEPT
681.e: Carpal tunnel syndrome is produced by entrapment of median nerve beneath the flexor retinaculum. Associated conditions that can leads to carpal tunnel syndrome are: Idiopathic(most common) Pregnancy Endocrine disorders - Hypothyroidism, Diabetes mellitus, Myxedema, Acromegaly, Hyperparathyroidism Deposition disorders - Rheumatoid disorder, Gout, Rheumatic disorder, Amyloidosis, Sarcoidosis, Leukemia, Chronic renal failure Reference: Apley's system of orthopedics & fracture, 8th edition, Page: 247-248.

681.q: All of the following are predictive findings for correctly diagnosing carpal tunnel syndrome EXCEPT:
o: Abnormal Semmes-Weinstein testing in wrist-neutral position
Positive median nerve compression test(Durkan's sign)
Loss of small digit adduction(Wartenberg sign)
681.e: Wartenberg sign is persistent abduction and extension of the small digit when a patient is asked to adduct the digits and is seen in cubital tunnel syndrome, but not carpal tunnel syndrome. Reference: Maheshwari Essential Orthopedics, 5 th edition, Page no. 303.

Most commonly injured knee ligament is the MCL followed by the ACL. ACL is the most commonly operated knee ligament as most of the MCL injuries are managed conservatively. Reference - Manish Kumar Varshney 1 st edition page no 878

681.q: Investigation of choice for ligament injuries of the knee is?
681.e: Investigation of choice for knee ligament injury is MRI as it will clearly show injuries of both the cruciates (intra articular) and the collaterals (extra articular) However, the investigation of choice for intra articular knee structures such as, ACL, PCL, menisci and cartilage is diagnostic arthroscopy. This is because, when we put an arthroscope in the knee joint, we can visualize the intra articular structures in 5 to 10 times magnification. Reference - Maheshwari, Essential Orthopedics 5 th edition page no 151.

682.e: Answer- A. Osteoid osteoma Dense, homogenous mineralization (calcification) is typical of osteoid matrix, formed by benign and malignant bone forming lesions. 1265. Which of the following is true about Giant cell tumor a) Usually presents as a lytic lesion with sclerotic rim b) Always beingn c) Epiphyseal origin d) Seen in age less than 15 years Correct Answer - C Answer- C. Epiphyseal origin GCT is an osteolytic tumor arising from the epiphysis and is common between the age of 20-40 years. The commonest sites are lower end of femur and upper end of tibia. Other common sites are lower end radius and upper end of humerus. It may also occur in the spine and sacrum. The radiological features are : -

682.q: Which is not a cause of pain in osteochondroma?
682.e: Malignant change can cause pain in osteochondroma. However the malignancy that arises in osteochondroma is chondrosarcoma and not osteosarcoma. The causes of pain in osteochondroma are Bursitis (most common cause) Fracture of the pedicle Compression of an adjacent nerve Malignant change - chondrosarcoma. Reference: Miler's 8th Edition of Review of Orthopaedics, page no. 1881

682.q: Which of the following is also called the Codman's tumor?
682.e: Codman's tumor is another name for Chondroblastoma. It should not be confused with Codman's triangle which is a type of periosteal reaction, most commonly seen in osteosarcoma. Reference: Tachdjian's Pediatric Orthopaedics 5th edition page no. 1109

682.q: Which of the following is not true about osteoid osteoma?
o: Generally affect diaphysis of long bones
The commonest bone affected is the femur
682.e: Osteoid Osteoma: Benign bone forming lesion considered to be the most common true benign tumor of the bone Age group: 2 nd -3 rd decades Male: Female 3:1 Lower extremity, long bones, Posterior elements spine, Diaphyseal/metaphyseal Pain: worse at night XRAY - Cortical radiolucent nidus High levels of cyclooxygenases and prostaglandins in the lesion Frequently responds to NSAIDs HISTOLOGY - Trabeculae surrounded by loose fibrovascular tissue TREATMENT - NSAIDs, Burr down technique, Radiofrequency ablation. Reference: Maheshwari, Essential Ortho, 5 th edition, Page no. 236.

682.q: A 26 years male with epiphysial bone tumor shows lytic lesion with chicken-wire calcification.
682.e: Chondroblastoma This is a cartilaginous tumor containing characteristic multiple calcium deposits. It occurs in young adults and is located around the epiphyseal plate . Bones around the knee are commonly affected. Radiologically, there is a well-defined lytic lesion surrounded by a zone of sclerosis. Areas of calcification within the tumor substance give rise to a mottled appearance . Treatment is by curettage and bone grafting. Chondroblastoma(Codman tumors): Microscopically they are composed of chondroblasts, chondroid matrix, cartilage with occasional giant multinucleated cells(which may lead to the incorrect diagnosis of giant cell tumor). Calcium deposition surrounding the chondroblasts, which are typically polyhedral shape, results in typical ' chicken-wire calcification '(pathognomonic) Reference: Maheshwari Essentials Ortho, 5 th edition, Page no. 236.

682.q: Most frequent benign bone tumor of hand is -
682.e: Important facts Commonest bone malignancies Secondaries(metastases) Commonest primary malignant tumor → Multiple myeloma Commonest primary malignant tumor of long bones → Osteosarcoma Commonest benign tumor of bonne → Osteochondroma(Osteochondroma is not true neoplasm since its growth stops with cessation of growth at the epiphyseal plate) Commonest true benign tumor of bone → Osteroid osteoma Commonest benign tumor of hand → Enchondroma Reference: Apley's, 9th edition, Pg: 197.

682.q: A 15y old boy presented with back pain. CT showed an expansile lytic lesion in transverse process of vertebra. What is the likely diagnosis?
682.e: Osteosarcoma never involves the vertebra. Metastasis can occur rarely in this age group, but it usually involves the vertebral body and the pedicles. Tumors that can commonly involve the transverse process are ABC and Osteoblastoma. Osteoblastoma will have a large nidus and surrounding sclerosis, hence it is not a lytic lesion The classical expansile lytic lesion of the transverse process is aneurysmal bone cyst (ABC). Reference: J. Maheshwari's 5th Edition of Essential Orthopaedics page no. 237

682.q: Chondrosarcoma can develop in which of the following conditions?
682.e: Chondrosarcoma can arise from other benign cartilage tumors especially enchondromas. In the given options, the only syndrome that presents with enchondromas is Maffucci syndrome. Maffucci syndrome has a 100% risk of malignant change. Maffucci syndrome Multiple enchodromas Soft tissue angiomas Phleboliths Jaffe campanacci syndrome Muliple Non ossifying fibromas Mazabraud syndrome Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia Myxomas McCune Albright syndrome Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia Cafe au lait spots Precocious puberty Reference: J. Maheshwari's 5th Edition of Essential Orthopaedics page no. 248

683.q: Commonest site of occurrence of chondrosarcoma is
683.e: Chondrosarcoma A chondrosarcoma is a malignant tumor derived from cartilage cells and it tends to maintain its cartilaginous character throughout its evolution. Highest incidence is in the fourth and fifth decades and men are affected more often than women. Most commonly involved bones are pelvis(most common), femur(2 nd most common), humerus, ribs and shoulder girdles. It may be at metaphysis or diaphysis. This tumor is slow growing but can metastasise to distant site The usual presentation is dull ache or gradually enlarging mass. Radiological features Expansile, radiolucent lesion in the medullary cavity(concentric) Endosteal scalloping. Punctate comma shaped or popcorn calcification. Treatment Surgery is the treatment of choice Reference: Campbell, 12 th edition, Page no. 914.

683.q: T 10 protocol for the treatment of osteosarcoma includes all except?
683.e: The drugs used in T 10 protocol include High dose Methotrexate Bleomycin Dactinomycin Doxorubicin Cyclophosphamide Reference: Miler's 8th Edition of Review of Orthopaedics, page no. 1854

683.q: A 45 year old male presented with an expansile lesion in the distal femoral metaphysis. The lesion shows endosteal scalloping and punctate calcification. Diagnosis?
683.e: The diagnosis is chondrosarcoma. The points in favor are The age of the patient is 45 years. The common age for chondrosarcoma is between 40 to 60 years. The site of origin is the metaphysis. The x ray finding of endosteal scalloping and punctate calcification is seen in chondrosarcoma. Osteosarcoma and Chondroblastoma are commonly seen in the 2nd decade of life Metastasis does not produce endosteal scalloping and punctate calcification Reference: Miler's 8th Edition of Review of Orthopaedics, page no. 1885

683.q: Increased LDH levels are a bad prognostic factor in which tumor?
683.e: Poor prognostic factors for Ewing's sarcoma Distant metastases Advanced and extensive disease with fulminant course. Large tumor size(> 8cm) Proximal location Older age(> 17 years) Male gender Genetic aberrant P-53 expression Relapse Early(within Poor response to chemotherapy Elevated ESR, WBC, LDH value indicates more extensive disease and poor prognosis. Ewing sarcoma is the most chemosensitive and most radiosensitive malignant bone tumor. Ewing sarcoma(> osteosarcoma) is the most common tumor showing bone to bone metastasis, hence mandating a bone scan to detect the metastasis. Reference: Maheshwari Essential Ortho, 5 th edition, Page no. 243.

683.q: What is the most common primary malignancy of the skeleton?
683.e: Metastasis is the most common malignancy of the skeleton, but multiple myeloma is the most common primary malignancy of the skeleton. Osteochondroma is the most common benign tumor of the skeleton. Reference: Maheshwari Essential Ortho, 5 th edition, Page no. 247.

683.q: Which is the most common radiation induced tumour?
683.e: The most common radiation induced tumour is osteosarcoma. Such tumors are called secondary osteosarcoma. They have a very poor prognosis. The most common radiation induced benign tumour is osteochondroma. Reference: J. Maheshwari's 5th Edition of Essential Orthopaedics page no. 242

683.q: Which of the following is bone forming malignant tumour?
683.e: Bone-forming tumours are a sub-set of bone tumours that are characterised by their propensity to form excess osteoid. They can be further subdivided into benign and malignant tumours. Benign tumours Osteoid osteoma Osteoblastoma Bone island(enostosis) Osteopoikilosis Osteoma Malignant tumours Malignant bone-forming tumours are all osteosarcomas. Osteosarcoma(conventional) Telangiectatic osteosarcoma Low-grade central osteosarcom Reference: Adam's Outline of orthopedics, 14th edition, Pg: 113.

683.q: Most common site of Admantinoma is
683.e: Adamantinoma is a low grade malignant tumor most commonly affecting the tibia. It is a diaphyseal tumor. Tibia (85% cases) followed by fibula is the most common site for adamantinoma of long bones. It occurs between 20 to 40 years of age. The swelling is associated with only minimal pain and it increases in size gradually. Typically, it appears as a honeycomb-like, loculated lesion on X-ray. Metastasis is not common. Treatment is by resection. Reference: Maheshwari Essential Ortho, 5 th edition, Page no. 237.

684.q: A 50-year-old woman has pins and needles sensation that worsens at night and is relieved when she shakes her hand. She also has episodic left knee pain throughout the day. She takes medications for constipation. Her BMI is 35 kg/m2. Her pulse is 57/min and blood pressure is 120/75 mm Hg. Sensation is decreased to light touch in the thumb and index finger. DTR = 1+ and there is mild edema in the legs. Which of the following treatments is most likely to benefit the patient?
684.e: This obese patient has neuropathic pain along the distribution of the median nerve that is consistent with carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS). The patient presents with classic signs of hypothyroidism: constipation, fatigue, bradycardia, hyporeflexia, and lower limb edema (which is usually myxedematous and non-pitting, but pitting edema can also occur due to excessive albumin in extracellular spaces). While the precise etiopathology is uncertain, it is assumed that the excess deposition of glycosaminoglycans, hyaluronic acid, and mucopolysaccharides in hypothyroidism causes myxedema. These characteristic depositions can subsequently cause compression of the carpal tunnel. With thyroid hormone replacement and return to a euthyroid state, symptoms should improve within weeks to months. Reference: Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, Fourteenth Edition By Bertram G. Katzung Pg no. 699

684.q: A professional tennis player presents with shoulder pains especially whilst serving the ball. He has limited passive and active shoulder abduction to less than 60°. His temperature is 36.5°C and he has a normal white cell count. There is tenderness around the anterior portion of the shoulder joint. Which diagnosis is likely?
684.e: Pain during abduction with limitation of movement is suggestive of supraspinatous tendonitis. Palpation or compression around the greater tubercle of the humerus is particularly tender. Glenohumeral joint OA is very rare. Though Rotator cuff tendinitis is often accompanied by a sub acromial bursitis, the more likely answer here is supraspinatus tendinitis, considering the recurrent overhead abduction as in a tennis player. Tennis elbow causes pain the elbow. Reference: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 21 st Ed, Ch: 375, Pg: 2878

684.q: A 35-year-old female presents to the emergency room after a motor vehicle collision where her leg was pinned under the car for over 30 minutes. On arrival at the casualty, her BP was 80 systolic. Which of the following is the most accurate way to diagnose compartment syndrome in this patient?
o: Diastolic blood pressure minus intra-compartmental pressure is less than 30 mmHg
Diastolic blood pressure minus intra-compartmental pressure is greater than 30 mmHg
684.e: The classical definition of compartment syndrome is an intracompartmental pressure of 30mm of Hg or above. However, this is not true for hypotensive patients. The best way to diagnose compartment syndrome in a hypotensive patient is to calculate the delta P value. Diastolic blood pressure minus intracompartmental pressure is called delta p, If delta p is less than 30 mm hg patient requires immediate fasciotomy for compartment syndrome Reference- Maheshwari ortho 5th edition, page number 47

684.q: A 3 year old boy is brought with the history that he had a fight with his older sister, who pulled his hand forcefully to get her favorite toy from him. After this, the boy started crying with pain on the elbow. O/E the boy is keeping his forearm pronated. X ray did not show any fractures. The next step is
o: MRI to rule out occult fractures
Manipulate the elbow into supination and flexion
Apply crepe bandage and repeat x ray after 1 week
Apply a plaster cast and repeat x ray after 1 week
684.e: This is a case of pulled elbow also called the nursemaid’s elbow. It is a subluxation of radial head caused due to an axial pull distal to the elbow. Seen in children Clinical features Minimal inflammation Pronated forearm X ray - normal Treatment - flexion and supination of the forearm will reduce the radial head and correct the subluxation. Reference: J. Maheshwari's 5th Edition of Essential Orthopaedics page no. 105

684.q: The anterior approach to total hip arthroplasty requires dissection between which of the following muscle planes?
684.e: DISCUSSION: The anterior approach to the hip joint involves identifying the plane between the tensor fascia lata and the sartorius muscles. In the anterolateral approach to hip, we use the plane between TFL and Gluteus medius. Reference: Berry, D. J. (2001). PRIMARY TOTAL HIP ARTHROPLASTY. In M. W. Chapman (Ed.), Chapman's Orthopaedic Surgery (3rd ed., pp. 2749–2759). Lippincott Williams & Wilkins

684.q: In Anterolateral approach for hip surgery, intermuscular plane is made between tensor fascia lata and which other muscle?
684.e: The plane of dissection in anterolateral approach to hip is between TFL and gluteus medius Incision: Curvilinear incision centered over the greater trochanter running posteriorly along the shaft of the femur with hip in 30–40° of flexion starting 2–3 cm behind the ASIS. Soft tissue dissection: Plane is developed between the TFL and the gluteus medius (protects the inferior branch of the superior gluteal nerve). TFL is then retracted medial and anterior, and the gluteus medius retracted posterior and lateral exposing gluteus minimus posteriorly and rectus anteriorly. Reference: Manish kumar varshney 1st edition page no 1094.

684.q: A healthy 72-year-old woman is seen 14 days after cemented total knee arthroplasty. She reports increasing pain and swelling for the last 4 days accompanied by 4 days of wound drainage. Examination reveals that she is afebrile, and has erythema and moderate serosanguinous drainage from the wound. The knee is moderately swollen. Aspiration of the knee reveals no organisms on Gram stain. Culture results are expected back in 48 hours. Optimal management should consist of?
o: Initiation of a first-generation cephalosporin while awaiting culture results.
Initiation of broad-spectrum antibiotics while awaiting culture results.
Ultrasound to evaluate for fluid collection around the knee.
Surgical debridement of the knee before culture results are available.
684.e: DISCUSSION: Increased pain, swelling, erythema, and drainage 2 weeks removed from the primary arthroplasty are all signs of a probable infection. Erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein may not be helpful as they are elevated postoperatively even in the absence of infection. Even in the absence of infection, persistent wound drainage is an indication for surgical debridement to prevent subsequent infection. When a postoperative infection is easily recognized by clinical examination, there is no need to wait for a positive culture before proceeding with debridement. Reference: Burke, D. W., & O'Flynn, H. (2001). PRIMARY TOTAL KNEE ARTHROPLASTY. In M. W. Chapman (Ed.), Chapman's Orthopaedic Surgery (3rd ed., pp. 2869–2896). Lippincott Williams & Wilkins.

684.q: A 16 year old child, who is a known case of hemophilia presented with painful swelling of right knee after a trivial fall. What should not be done?
o: X ray of the right Knee
684.e: In most instances of hemarthrosis, the first line of management is aspiration of joint, which will relieve the pressure within the joint and provide pain relief to the patient. However, this is contraindicated in hemophilia, as even if we aspirate a joint and remove all the blood, it will re-accumulate within few hours. This is because, the deficiency of clotting factor 8 will not allow clot formation and there will be continued bleeding into the joint. Reference: Miler's 8th Edition of Review of Orthopaedics, page no. 699

685.q: All are causes of recurrent dislocation of shoulder except
685.e: Rotator cuff tear is not a cause of recurrent dislocation of shoulder. The Common injuries causing recurrent dislocation of the shoulder are Bankart lesion Bony Bankart lesion Hill Sach's lesion Reference: J. Maheshwari's 5th Edition of Essential Orthopaedics page no. 90

685.q: A young cricket player comes to you with knee pain and inability to extend it fully. He gives a history of twisting injury to his right knee when he collided another player while fielding. His MRI shows a double PCL sign. What is the appropriate management?
o: Application of above knee cast for 6 weeks
Icing, rest, compression and elevation for 2 weeks and then isometric and knee bending exercises
Icing, rest, compression and elevation for 2 weeks and then gradual return to sports
685.e: Double PCL sign on MRI is classically seen in bucket handle tear of a meniscus. The inability to fully extend the knee suggest a locked knee, again pointing towards a bucket handle meniscal tear. The best treatment of acute bucket handle meniscal tear in young athletes is arthroscopic repair. However if the meniscus injury is in the white- white zone, then a partial meniscectomy is done as the meniscus will not heal even if we do a repair because of the poor blood supply at the white -white zone. Reference - Manish Kumar Varshney 1 st edition page no 894.

685.q: Patient with history of knee injury 3 months back presents with knee pain. O/E knee was unstable with knee in flexion but stable in extension. What structure is injured?
685.e: ACL is made up of 2 bundles Anteromedial - which becomes tight in flexion Posterolateral - which becomes tight in extension In this patient, the knee is unstable in flexion but stable in extension. This means that the anteromedial fibres of the ACL are torn but the posteromedial fibers are intact. Reference: Miler's 8th Edition of Review of Orthopaedics, page no. 728

685.q: A 23 year old female slipped from stairs, causing her right foot to go into excessive inversion. She has pain and swelling around the ankle. Which structure is most likely injured?
685.e: The most common ligament injured in inversion injuries of the ankle is the ATFL (anterior talofibular ligament) In fact, it is the most commonly injured ligament in the body. It is said that, every human will get an ATLF strain at least once in their lifetime. Reference: Koval's Handbook of fracture's 5th edition, page no. 452

685.q: Patient presents to the OPD with pain and feeling of buckling of right knee. He gives history of injury during playing hockey 3 months back. On examination, the knee was unstable anteriorly in extension but was stable in 90 degrees of flexion. Probably injury involves:
685.e: The ACL ligament is the primary restraint to anterior tibial displacement, accounting for approximately of the resistance to the anterior drawer test when the knee is at of flexion and neutral rotation. ACL has 2 bundles –anteomedial and posterolateral. The anteromedial band is tight in flexion, providing the primary restraint, whereas the posterolateral bulky portion of this ligament is tight in extension. The posterolateral bundle also provides the principal resistance against hyperextension. Therefore in ACL tears Complete ACL tear will produce instability in both flexion and extension. Anteromedial bundle tear will produce instability in flexion Posterolateral bundle tear will produce instability in extension. Reference - Manish Kumar Varshney 1 st edition page no 879.

685.q: Which of the following is not a feature of ACL injury?
o: Pop sound in the knee during the time of injury
Swelling of the knee immediately after the injury
Feeling of knee buckling while attempting to walk
685.e: In patients with ACL tears, there is difficulty in climbing down stairs and not in climbing up stairs. This is because while coming down stairs, the tibia will be pulled anteriorly by gravity and the tibia will translate anteriorly as there is no restraint from the ACL. This will result in a feeling of giving way and instability. Features of Acute ACL tear are Pop sound at the time of injury Immediate effusion of knee Pain Unable to weight bear Features of Chronic ACL tear are Feeling of instability Difficulty going down stairs Occasional pain Reference: Miler's 8th Edition of Review of Orthopaedics, page no. 733, 741

685.q: Inversion injury to ankle caused damage to which of the following structures?
685.e: Inversion injury to ankle involves damage to talofibular ligament (the lateral complex). INVERSION INJURY An inversion force with the foot in plantar flexion results in the sprain of the anterior talofibular ligament of the ankle. It is the most common ligament injury occurring in the body. Reference - Maheshwari Essential Orthopaedics, 4th ed., 135

685.q: In dancers, peroneal muscle weakness has been shown to be the cause of which of the following?
685.e: The most common acute skeletal injury in the dancer is the inversion sprain of the ankle and thought to be due to relative peroneal muscle weakness. Sprains may occur in any ligament in the foot or ankle, but most common ones involve the lateral ligament complex (anterior talofibular, calcaneal-fibular, and posterior talofibular ligaments); the anterior tibiofibular, the lateral talocalcaneal ligament; and, occasionally the medial (deltoid) ligament. Regardless of the method of treatment, adequate physical therapy and proper rehabilitation are necessary to restore normal use following injury. Restoration of full peroneal strength is essential to minimize risk of recurrent sprains. Reference - Manish Kumar Varshney 1 st edition page no 1262.

686.q: Clostridium perfringens toxin which causes myonecrosis is
686.e: The major toxins used for strain classification of clostridium perfringens are alpha toxin, beta toxin, epsilon toxin, and iota toxin. Alfa toxin is responsible for hemolysis, myonecrosis and gas gangrene in the infected tissue. Reference- Microbiology by Ananthanarayan and Paniker, 8th ed. pg. 251, 263, 634

686.q: Which of the following processes is involved in age-related intervertebral disc degeneration?
o: Increased cell number in the nucleus pulposus
686.e: PATHOPHYSIOLOGY OF DISK DEGENERATION: Loss of Proteoglycan - The aggrecan molecules become smaller and get leached from the tissue. This reduces glycosaminoglycans and water holding capacity and thus there is fall in the osmotic pressure of the disk matrix. Loss of Collagen Fibers - Type II collagen become more denatured and get replaced by type 1 collagen. Increase in Fibronectin - Fibronectin content increases with increasing degeneration and it becomes more fragmented. Enzymatic Activity - Increased fragmentation of the collagen, proteoglycan and fibronectin is mediated by increased enzymatic activity including cathepsins, MMPs and aggrecanases. Reference: Manish Kumar Varshney, 1 st edition, Page no. 1353.

686.q: The spinal cord terminates as the conus medullaris at what vertebral level in adults?
686.e: SPINAL CORD: The spinal cord extends from the level of foramen magnum to the level of the intervertebral disc between 1st and 2nd lumbar vertebra. The spinal cord is 40-50 cm long and 1-1.5 cm in diameter. By weight the spinal cord contributes only 2% of the central nervous system. All the three meninges namely the pia, arachnoid and dura mater cover the spinal cord. It is attached to the dura mater by a series of lateral denticulate ligaments emanating from the pial folds. Reference: Manish Kumar Varshney, 1 st edition, Page no. 1331.

686.q: Perivascular lymphocytes & microglial nodules are seen in -
686.e: Ans. is 'b' i.e., HIV encephalitis o Perivascular infiltrate of lymphocytes (and macrophages) with microglial nodules is seen in HIV encephalitis. o Perivascular infiltrate of lymphocytes (and monocytes) is also seen in multiple sclerosis. But, microglial nodules are characteristic of HIV encephalitis.

687.q: All of the following have contributed to defining and developing defense mechanisms except:
687.e: Sigmund Freud focused primarily on repression as the central defense mechanism . Anna Freud greatly elaborated on individual defense mechanisms, including Reaction formation Regression Undoing Introjection Identification Projection Turning against the self Reversal Sublimation. George Valiant classified defence mechanisms into Narcissistic Immature Neurotic Mature levels Victor Frankl however, has no contribution to describing defense mechanisms. (Option D) Reference : Kaplan and Sadock’s Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11 th edition, Chapter 4 Theories of Personality and Psychopathology, Page number 177.

687.q: A 26-year-old male CT1 psychiatric trainee was put down badly by his consultant in a ward round and the consultant shouted at him. After work, he went to see his mother and started to present childish behavior such as playing with his old toy cars. Which is the most likely defense mechanism?
687.e: Regression is the defence that refers to the reversion to the early stage of ego functioning . Each and every person has defences to deal with stress. Some of them are mature defences → altruism, sublimation, suppression and humour. Some are immature and neurotic defences → displacement, isolation regression and projection. Isolation : thoughts, emotions or behaviour is isolated to break the link with other thoughts or memories ( Option B ) Projection : unacceptable thoughts, emotions and feelings are projected on to some other person ( Option C ) In displacement , emotions or wishes are transferred from the original object or person to a more suitable substitute ( Option A ) Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, eleventh edition, chapter 4, page no. 161

687.q: Which of the following statement is false about Topographical model of mind proposed by Sigmund Freud?
o: Consists of Unconscious, Preconscious and Conscious
Preconscious serves as a censor mechanism
All defense mechanisms operate at unconscious level except suppression
Id, Ego and Superego all operate at unconscious level only
687.e: Id largely operates at unconscious However, ego and superego operate at all three levels of conscious, preconscious and unconscious. Reference : Kaplan and Sadock’s Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11 th edition, Chapter 4 Theories of Personality and Psychopathology, Page number 154.

687.q: Which of the following is false about Structural model of mind proposed by Sigmund Freud?
o: Consists of Id, Ego and Superego
Id works on morality principle and guides a person what not to do
Defense mechanisms are a function of ego to maintain balance between id and superego
687.e: The structural model of mind proposed by Sigmund Freud consists of Id, Ego and Superego. Id works on pleasure principle . Freud used the term id to refer to a reservoir of unorganized instinctual drives . The id lacks the capacity to delay or modify the instinctual drives with which an infant is born. (Option B is FALSE) Ego works on reality principle . It works as a balance between ego and superego. Superego works on morality principle and guides a person what not to do. Reference : Kaplan and Sadock’s Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11 th edition, Chapter 4 Theories of Personality and Psychopathology, Page number 159.

687.q: Age of responsibility refers to the age at which an individual can:
o: Make the decision to consent to sexual relationship
Earn money and open a bank account
Be held accountable for their criminal actions
687.e: The age of criminal responsibility is the age below which a child is deemed incapable of having committed a criminal offence. In legal terms, it is referred to as a defence of infancy , which is a form of defense known as an excuse so that defendants falling within the definition of an "infant" are excluded from criminal liability for their actions , if at the relevant time, they had not reached an age of criminal responsibility. Nothing is an offence which is done by a child under Indian Penal Code the age of seven years . The age of criminal responsibility is raised to 12 years if the child is found to have not attained the ability of understanding the nature and consequences of his act. Reference : https://www.unicef-irc.org/portfolios/documents/394_india.htm

687.q: A 55-year-old male lawyer wished for his child to be a lawyer too, but unfortunately the child died in a car accident. Since the child's death, the lawyer has started to offer free legal advice to students. Which is the most likely defense mechanism?
687.e: Altruism is a type of higher or mature defence mechanism . (Option B) In this, a person deals with inner conflict or any stress by helping others or fulfilling the needs of others. Reaction formation is seen in the patients with obsessive–compulsive disorder ; here the attitude is opposed to the oppressed wish and constitutes the opposite reaction. ( Option D ) Humour is also a mature defence in which a person deals with stress by giving it a humorous form or takes things lightly in a jovial way ( Option C ) Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, eleventh edition, chapter 4, page no. 161

688.q: All the following conditions result due to problems with basal ganglia except:
688.e: There are four main conditions to be aware of that result from problems with the basal ganglia: Huntington's chorea (caudate nucleus) Wilson's disease (copper deposition in the basal ganglia) Parkinson's disease (substantia nigra) Hemiballismus (sub thalamic nucleus) Multiple sclerosis is a demyelinating disease of CNS. Reference: Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11 th Edition, Page Number-8.

688.q: Information about emotion passes through all of the following structures of brain except:
688.e: The Papez circuit consists of the hippocampus → fornix → mammillary bodies → mammillothalamic tract → anterior thalamic nucleus → genu of the internal capsule → cingulate gyrus → Para hippocampal gyrus → entorhinal cortex → perforant pathway → back to hippocampus The boundaries of the limbic system were subsequently expanded outside of the Papez circuit to include the amygdala, septum, basal forebrain, nucleus accumbens, and orbitofrontal cortex. The limbic system is thought to be involved in various functions such as mediation of emotional responses (through amygdala), influencing neuroendocrine responses (via hypothalamus) and reward system regulation (via nucleus accumbens). Reference: Kaplan and Sadock’s Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11 th edition, Chapter 1.2 Functional Neuroanatomy, Page number 13.

688.q: In a patient presenting with headache, all of the following features typically suggest tension-type headache except:
o: Not aggravated by noise or light
Not associated with nausea or vomiting
688.e: Criteria for Tension type headache: At least 10 episodes of headache occurring on 1-14 days per month on average for >3 months and, 1 attack lasting from 30 mins-7 days. 2/4 of following b/l, non-pulsatile (non-throbbing quality), mild to moderate, not aggravated by routine activities None of following Nausea or vomiting, either photo or phono-phobia. Reference: Kaplan and Sadock’s Comprehensive Textbook of Psychiatry, 10 th edition, Chapter 2.11 Neuropsychiatric aspects of headache, Page number 1647.

688.q: A 24-year-old married housewife attempted to slash her wrist after a fight with her husband over his drinking habit. The cut was made superficially on the wrist with a knife. On asking her, she later replied that she had no intent to die, but felt very angry after the fight. This is termed as:
688.e: Deliberate self-harm means willful self-inflicting of painful, destructive, or injurious acts without intent to die ( OPTION A ) Parasuicide is a term used to describe patients who injure themselves by self-mutilation (e.g., cutting the skin), but who usually do not wish to die. ( OPTION B ) Hence, in the above clinical scenario, since intention to die is absent, the self-harming behavior by cutting skin superficially is suggestive of deliberate self-harm/ Para-suicide. ( CORRECT OPTION D ) Reference : Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11th edition, Chapter 23.1 Suicide, Page number 763.

688.q: Which of the following is associated with suicidal behavior ?
688.e: Tryptophan hydroxylase (TPH) is an enzyme involved in the biosynthesis of serotonin. A polymorphism in the human TPH gene has been identified, with two alleles -U and L. Because low concentrations of 5-HIAA ( OPTION A ) in CSF are associated with suicidal behavior, it was hypothesized that such individuals may have alterations in genes controlling serotonin synthesis and metabolism. It was found that the presence of the L allele (OPTION C) was associated with an increased risk of suicide attempts . The presence of one TPH*L allele may indicate a reduced capacity to hydroxylate tryptophan to 5-hydroxytryptophan in the synthesis of serotonin, producing low central serotonin turnover and, thus, a low concentration of 5-HIAA in CSF. Reference : Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11th edition, Chapter 23 Emergency Psychiatric Medicine, Page number 767.

688.q: A 52-year-old divorced male patient, currently unemployed, belonging to low socio-economic status and living alone, died by committing suicide by hanging in the afternoon. Which demographic factor is least indicative of risk of suicide in him ?
688.e: Advanced age, marital status (divorced), Occupation status (unemployed), Socio-economic status (Low socio-economic status), living alone are all important predictors of suicide. ( OPTION A, B, D ) However, time of the day has least clinical correlation to suicide ( CORRECT ANSWER -C) Reference : Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11th edition, Chapter 23.1 Suicide, Page number 763.

688.q: psychiatrist has supposedly crossed and violated the boundaries of doctor-patient relationship in which of the following:
o: If he has had sexual relations with the patient
If he has had business relations with patients
688.e: Boundaries of doctor-patient relationship are violated if the physician has sexual or business relations with the patient. Breaching of confidentiality is allowed in some situations like when the patient is a minor , when the patient is homicidal or suicidal or in legal matters. Reference : Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11th edition, Chapter 36.2 Ethics in Psychiatry, Page number 1393.

688.q: Which drug should be prescribed with caution in conjunction with fluvoxamine?
688.e: Fluvoxamine, when used with naproxen, increases the risk of bleeding. ( CORRECT OPTION D) In addition, it should be used with caution when given together with lithium(or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs[NSAIDs]), St John's wort, tryptophan or warfarin. Fluvoxamine inhibits the cytochrome P450 CYPIA2/2CG/3A4. Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 29th, Page no. 1021.

689.q: A 16-year-old girl is brought to a physician by her mother, who states that her daughter has been losing weight steadily. The adolescent denies there is a problem and states that she is in no way underweight. The physician determines that the girl is 5 ft 6 in tall and weighs 90 lbs. Which of the following would be the next best step to work this patient up?
o: Complete blood count and differential white blood cell count
Calculation and assessment of patient BMI
689.e: The BMI of a patient is calculated using the patient weight, height and age (in those younger than 18) to create a ratio. BMIs of less than 19 may be the first indication of ANOREXIA NERVOSA. It is an easy, non-invasive calculation that is done in the office quickly so should be done prior to more invasive, expensive, and time-consuming laboratory studies. Reference: Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 15.4, Obesity and Metabolic Syndrome, Page no. 523.

689.q: Maximum score in MMSE is given to which of the following cognitive functions?
689.e: MMSE assesses the following five cognitive functions and gives them different weightage. Orientation - 10 points Registration - 3 points Attention and concentration - 5 points Recall - 3 points Language - 9 points Max score = 30 ≤24/30 = indicative of cognitive impairment Reference: Mini Mental Status Examination

689.q: A 22-year-old woman is referred for assessment by the obstetric team. She is reported to be feeling depressed following the birth of her first baby three days ago. She has no history of depressive disorder. The baby is healthy, although the woman required a caesarean delivery. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
o: Major depressive episode with post-partum onset
689.e: Baby blues typically occur 3-6 days following the birth of the baby in 50-60% of mothers. Post-partum depression occurs in approximately 10% of women after parturition . It usually occurs within 6-8 weeks of birth , most often beginning between days 3 and 14 after parturition Adjustment disorder is usually diagnosed within six months of the occurrence of a significant stressor, and usually resolves within six months of the resolution of the stressful situation ( Option B ) An adjustment reaction is a short-lived anxiety response to a stressful situation. ( Option C ) Given the time frame of this presentation, the birth and the prevalence’s, the most likely diagnosis is baby blues. Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 27, page no. 839

689.q: All of the following scales are used for assessment of intelligence except:
689.e: Scales for intelligence assessment are Weschler Intelligence scale Bhatia Battery test Binet Kamat Scale Montreal Cognitive Assessment scale is used for assessing cognition and not intelligence. Reference: Kaplan and Saddocks Synopsis of Psychiaitry, 11th Edition, Chapter 31, Page No.: 1115-1116

690.q: A severely depressed patient, having undergone six sessions of Electroconvulsive therapy, complains of memory loss following the procedure. Which of the following is false about ECT-induced amnesia in this patient?
o: Both retrograde and anterograde amnesia may occur
690.e: The greatest concern about ECT is the association between ECT and memory loss. About 75 percent of all patients given ECT say that the memory impairment is the worst adverse effect. Although memory impairment during a course of treatment is almost the rule, follow-up data indicate that almost all patients are back to their cognitive baselines after 6 months . (Option A is FALSE) Despite the memory impairment, which usually resolves, no evidence indicates brain damage caused by ECT. Reference : Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11 th edition, Chapter 30th, Brain Stimulation methods, Page number 1071.

690.q: After the complete management for wernickes encephalopathy, which of the following conditions can remain despite the treatment?
690.e: Wernicke's may reversed completely with treatment, residual ataxia and horizontal nystagmus remains there. Reference: Kaplan and Saddocks Synopsis of Psychiaitry, 11th Edition, Chapter 20, Page No.: 632

690.q: A 44-year-old smoker male patient, taking treatment for hypertension, COPD, and Xerophthalmia, starts feeling depressed and suicidal. Which of the following agents included in his treatment regimen, is least likely to cause depression and suicidal ideations in him?
690.e: Antihypertensives like reserpine, propranolol, Corticosteroids, Montelukast have all been associated with causing depression and pose a risk for suicide ( OPTIONS A, B, D ) However, topical application of methylcellulose eye drops has not been associated with depression. ( CORRECT ANSWER C ) Reference : Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11th edition, Chapter 23.1 Suicide, Page number 764.

690.q: Which of the following antidepressants is considered first-line treatment for depression in cancer patients?
690.e: Explanation: SSRIs are the first-line antidepressants for cancer patients due to their effectiveness, minimal sedative and autonomic side effects, and fewer drug interactions. Psychostimulants can help with fatigue and appetite. They are well-tolerated and suitable for patients with cancer-related depression. ECT (Electroconvulsive Therapy) can be considered in select cases. It is safe and effective for cancer patients, even with brain tumours.

690.q: A prospective mother is concerned about the risk of teratogenicity if she gets pregnant while on lithium. Which of the following best describes the risk of Ebstein's anomaly associated with lithium treatment in pregnancy?
690.e: Ebstein's anomaly comprises of dislodgement of the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle. The risk is increased with the use of lithium in the first trimester of pregnancy. Foetal ultrasound and echocardiography are indicated at 16-18 weeks. The risk is 1:1000 Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 29th, Page no. 986.

690.q: Regarding treatment of unipolar depressive disorder in adults, which one of the following statements is least true?
o: Approximately two-thirds of patients with depressive disorder are treated successfully with antidepressant medication alone
Combined treatment with antidepressant medication and cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) confers an additional treatment effect of approximately 30% over treatment with each treatment alone
Relapse rates following treatment discontinuation are higher in those taking medication compared with those who have received CBT
CBT is just as effective in the treatment of severe depressive disorder as antidepressant medication
690.e: CBT has been found to be slightly less effective than antidepressant therapy in the treatment of unipolar major depressive disorder and is recommended as equally efficacious in the treatment of mild-to-moderate unipolar depressive disorder. Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 8, page no. 376

Cerletti and Bini conducted the first electrical induction of seizures in a patient with catatonia in 1938. Before this, the seizures were introduced chemically. ( OPTION A ) Meduna (1934) used camphor to produce seizures in 1934. ( OPTION C ) In 1940, electroconvulsive therapy was introduced in the USA. Sakel introduced ‘insulin coma treatment’ for schizophrenia in 1933. ( OPTION D ) Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, eleventh edition, chapter 30, page no. 1066

690.q: All of the following can be used in treatment of tics except:
690.e: Medications used in treatment of tics are: Atypical and typical antipsychotics Noradrenergic agents like clonidine and guanfacine Alternative agents like Tetrabenazine, Topiramate and Tetrahydrocannabinol. Reference: Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11 th edition, Chapter 31.8c, Tourette's disorder, Page number 1204.

691.q: The most characteristic neuropsychiatric manifestations of systemic lupus erythematosus include?
691.e: Neuropsychiatric lupus commonly presents with seizures, psychosis, cognitive dysfunction, mood disorders and stroke, through autoantibody-mediated injury and thrombotic mechanisms. It is a diagnosis of exclusion requiring other causes to be ruled out.

691.q: A patient with untreated hypothyroidism is most likely to present psychiatrically with?
691.e: Hypothyroidism classically causes depression, fatigue, psychomotor slowing and cognitive impairment, occasionally severe enough to be called myxoedema madness. Hyperthyroidism, by contrast, tends toward anxiety, agitation and tremor.

691.q: A young adult with personality change, depression, dysarthria and Kayser-Fleischer rings most likely has?
691.e: Wilson disease is caused by ATP7B mutation with copper accumulation in liver, brain and cornea. Psychiatric symptoms such as personality change and depression often accompany movement disorder and dysarthria; Kayser-Fleischer rings and low ceruloplasmin support the diagnosis.

691.q: Psychiatric symptoms in Huntington disease most often appear in relation to chorea as follows?
691.e: Depression, irritability and apathy frequently precede chorea by years in Huntington disease, an autosomal dominant disorder caused by CAG expansion in the HTT gene. Psychiatric symptoms are a major cause of disability in the disease.

691.q: The most common psychiatric manifestation of multiple sclerosis is?
691.e: Depression affects around half of multiple sclerosis patients over the disease course, driven by lesion burden, inflammation and psychosocial factors. Euphoria (euphoria sclerotica) is a recognised but much less common feature.

691.q: The most common psychiatric feature of Cushing syndrome is?
691.e: Hypercortisolism most often causes depression, with irritability, insomnia and cognitive slowing. Mania or psychosis can also occur, particularly with higher cortisol levels, and usually improve when cortisol is normalised.

691.q: Acute intermittent porphyria characteristically presents with abdominal pain plus which neuropsychiatric features?
691.e: Acute intermittent porphyria attacks combine severe abdominal pain, autonomic instability and neuropsychiatric symptoms including confusion, hallucinations, seizures and peripheral neuropathy, often precipitated by drugs, fasting or alcohol.

691.q: General paresis of the insane (neurosyphilis) classically presents with?
691.e: General paresis is a late parenchymatous form of neurosyphilis: progressive dementia with grandiose or megalomaniac delusions, dysarthria, tremor and Argyll Robertson pupils. It develops years after untreated syphilis infection.

692.q: Which of the following IV anaesthetic agents does not cause cardiac depression
692.e: Etomidate: It is another induction anaesthetic (0.2-0.5 mg/kg) which has a briefer duration of action (4-8 min) than thiopentone; produces little cardiovascular and respiratory depression, but motor restlessness and rigidity is more prominent as are pain on injection or nausea and vomiting on recovery. It is a poor analgesic and has not found much favour except for patients with compromised cardiovascular status. Options B,C,D: Propofol, Methohexitone and Thiopentone have cardiac side effects and hence not used in cardiac patients.

692.q: A young woman recently diagnosed as schizophrenic develops severe muscle cramps with torticollis a short time after drug therapy is initiated with haloperidol. The best course of action would be to
o: Add risperidone to the drug regimen
Discontinue haloperidol and observe the patient
692.e: Acute dystonic reactions are usually very painful and should be treated immediately with parenteral administration of a drug that blocks muscarinic receptors such as benztropine. Option A- Adding risperidone is not protective, and fluphenazine is as likely as haloperidol to cause acute dystonia. Option B- There is no role of observing the patient in acute dystonia. Option C- Oral administration of diphenhydramine is a possibility, but the patient may find it difficult to swallow and it would take a longer time to act. Reference: Basic & Clinical Pharmacology, Fourteenth Edition by Bertram G. Katzung Pg no. 542-543

692.q: A 76-year-old man with history of hypertension and cancer of the colon had colectomy under general anesthesia 24 hours ago. He is receiving an epidural infusion of fentanyl at the rate of 100 micrograms/h. Which of the following is least likely?
692.e: Epidural opioids can cause nausea, pruritus, and respiratory depression Biggest advantage of these agents over epidural administration of local anesthetics is the hemodynamic stability , as there is no inhibition of sympathetic system Hypotension is highly unlikely with epidural fentanyl administration Reference : https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8706199/

692.q: Opioid available for use as transdermal patch?
692.e: The opioid Fentanyl is available in a transdermal therapeutic system (TTS) Advantages of transdermal fentanyl include: Increased patient compliance and comfort Avoidance of hepatic first pass metabolism Consistent analgesia Fentanyl is as effective as oral morphine for relieving cancer pain Disadvantages: Respiratory depression was significant and other side effects of opioids like nausea, vomiting, constipation is still seen but less in comparison to oral morphine Sufentanil and buprenorphine could be suitable for transdermal delivery, but their safety and efficacy are yet to be tested (Option B) Morphine can be delivered trans-dermally only after application to the deepithelialized skin Reference: Stoelting's pharmacology and physiology in anaesthetic practice 5th edition

693.q: In depressions, there is deficiency of ?
693.e: Ans. A. 5-HT Depression = Decrease in serotonin and norepinephrine. Serotonin is the most imPortant neurotransmitter in depression. Mania= Increased of norepipherine.

693.q: Which of the following drugs acts as competitive antagonist in the 5-HT3 receptors?
693.e: Clozapine competitively inhibits 5-HT3-receptors .( CORRECT OPTION A) Other antipsychotics mentioned in the question inhibit this receptor in a non-competitive fashion. Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 29th, Page no. 1029.

693.q: Which of the following medications has the highest propensity to cause QT prolongation on ECG?
693.e: ECG abnormalities occur in approximately 25% of all patients on antipsychotics. The most commonly reported changes are the prolonged QT interval(suggestive of repolarization disturbances), depressed ST segments and abnormal T waves. Thioridazine, pimozide, quetiapine, sertindole and droperidol prolong QTC interval to a higher extent than other antipsychotics . This predisposes to a fatal form of arrhythmia called torsade de pointes (polymorphic ventricular arrhythmia) leading to sudden death . Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 29th, Page no. 1027.

693.q: Which of the following is thought to best describe the receptor binding of aripiprazole?
693.e: Aripiprazole is thought to differ from most other antipsychotics in that it is a partial agonist at dopamine D2 receptors rather than an antagonist. It is also thought to have 5HT2A antagonist and 5HT1A partial agonist. Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 29th, Page no. 1028.

693.q: Which of the following antipsychotic agents is least likely to prolong the QTc interval on ECG recording at therapeutic doses?
693.e: Aripiprazole has no effect on the QTc interval. Chlorpromazine and Quetiapine are associated with a moderate effect on QTc .(Option B & D) Pimozide, Haloperidol and sertindole are drugs for which extensive QTc prolongation has been noted. (Option C) Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 29th, Page no. 1028.

693.q: Which of the following antipsychotics is least likely to cause sedation?
693.e: In comparison with other antipsychotics, aripiprazole has a very low relative incidence of sedation. All of the other antipsychotics like Chlorpromazine, Clozapine and Promazine are associated with high relative incidences of sedation .(Option B, C & D) Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 29th, Page no. 1028.

693.q: Which of the following is a formal thought disorder?
693.e: A formal thought disorder is considered to be a schizophrenic language disorder It characterised by disordered speech, and results from disorganised thoughts. It is often a symptom of schizophrenia, mania, severe depression with psychosis and other psychotic disorders. Tangentiality is a formal thought disorder in which there is tangential association of ideas leading to disruption in the smooth continuity of speech. Thought insertion, thought broadcasting, thought withdrawal and thought block are Schneider’s first rank symptoms . (Option C & D) Delusion of persecution is a fixed belief in which patients believe that they are being followed, persecuted and spied on, and that the perceived persecutor will cause them harm. (Option A) Reference: PGNIP2, Cijo Alex, 2 nd Edition, Chapter 3, page no. 27

693.q: What is the recommended duration of antipsychotic maintenance treatment after a first episode of psychosis?
693.e: Explanation: For patients after their first psychotic episode, antipsychotic maintenance therapy is recommended for at least one year to reduce relapse risk, longer or indefinite treatment may be needed after more episodes.

694.q: A 70-year-old man admitted in an intensive care unit suddenly develops fluctuation in orientation to time, place and person along with sleeplessness, aggressive behaviour and visualisation of small insects and animals. All of the following terms can be used to describe his condition except:
694.e: The above-mentioned case scenario represents delirium. Various terms describing delirium are as follows: Acute confusional state Acute brain failure Encephalitis Encephalopathy Intensive care unit psychosis Toxic metabolic state Central nervous system toxicity Paraneoplastic limbic encephalitis Sundowning Cerebral insufficiency Organic brain syndrome Reference : Kaplan and Sadock’s Textbook of Psychiatry, 11 th edition, Chapter 21.2 Delirium, Page number 697.
