711.q: A 27-year-old male CT2 psychiatric trainee was put down by his consultant in a ward round and the consultant shouted at him. After work, he went to the gym and exercised for half an hour more than usual. What is the most likely phenomenon?
711.e: This is the transformation of our instinctual energy to a more socially acceptable one . So, in this case, rather than shouting back at the consultant, the trainee went to the gym and transformed his anger and frustration into exercising . This is a mature defence mechanism. Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, eleventh edition, chapter 4, page no. 162

711.q: Which of the following drugs is least likely to cause serotonin syndrome?
711.e: Olanzapine is not associated with serotonin syndrome . Other drugs like Venlafaxine, Ecstasy and Fluoxetine have all been implicated in serotonin syndrome.(Option A, B & C) Ecstasy has been associated with serotonin syndrome in combination with venlafaxine. Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 29th, Page no. 1020.

711.q: 24-year-old Miss D had come to the Psychiatric OPD with the c/o Unresponsive episodes characterized by clonic movements and weeping spells lasting for 1 hour followed by an interpersonal conflict with her boyfriend. Supportive counselling was provided and she was prescribed with few medications. Two months later, she began to develop galactorrhoea with irregular menstrual cycle. Which of the following medications is more likely to cause it?
711.e: Levosulpiride is an atypical antipsychotic that blocks D2 receptors commonly prescribed in Conversion Disorder Considering the clinical presentation of the patient, all of the above medications can be provided to the patient but Levosulpiride is more prone to cause hyperprolactinemia leading to side effects like amenorrhoea, galactorrhoea, anorgasmia Escitalopram and Sertraline are SSRIs (Selective Serotonin Reuptake inhibitors) which may also lead to Hyperprolactinaemia but in much lesser propensity while Clonazepam is a Benzodiazepine lacking such effect Reference: Kaplan and Sadock’s Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 29 Psychopharmacological Treatment, page no. 1014

711.q: 27-year-old patient presents to the Psychiatric OPD with the chief complains of low mood with weeping spells, disinterest in her routine activities, early morning awakening, reduced appetite and suicidal ideation since last 15 days followed by the death of her husband. Patient is 4 months pregnant and unwilling to get admitted. Which of the following anti-depressant medication should be avoided in this patient?
711.e: Amongst all the antidepressants mentioned, Paroxetine is Category D drug. Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors(SSRIs) are prone to cause teratogenicity in the form of - Heart defects like ASD, VSD in the first trimester Pulmonary Hypertension in the third trimester Should be cautiously used, avoiding Paroxetine altogether. Reference : Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 29th, Psychopharmacological treatment, Page no. 1016.

711.q: A 45-year-old man in the medical ward on linezolid antibiotics developed confusion, muscle rigidity and hyperthermia shortly after he was placed on citalopram for low mood. What is the most likely diagnosis?
711.e: Serotonin syndrome is a rare but serious condition characterised by excess serotonergic activity. Symptoms include confusion, muscle rigidity, hyperreflexia and GI upset . Other symptoms include hyperthermia and fluctuation of blood pressure. Linezolid is an antibiotic used in treatment of gram-positive bacteria. It is a weak monoamine oxidase inhibitor and interaction with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor has been documented. Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 29th, Page no. 1020.

711.q: There is high risk of development of which psychiatric illness along with OCD?
711.e: OCD is ego dystonic. There is high risk of development of depression. And both should be treated simultaneously. Reference: Kaplan and Saddocks Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11th Edition, Chapter 10, Page No.: 418

711.q: This syndrome presents with affected individuals being cortically blind but unaware of it and hence deny they have a problem. Patients start falling over furniture as they can't see. However, they believe they can still see and describe their environments in detail but are wrong in their description. Identify this syndrome.
711.e: Anton's syndrome (Anton-Babinski syndrome): Occurs following damage to the occipital lobe. Affected individuals are cortically blind but are unaware of this and deny they have a problem (Anosognosia). It often presents as the patient starts falling over furniture as they can't see. Affected individuals believe they can still see and describe their environments in detail but are wrong in their description (confabulation). Reference: Kaplan and Sadock’s Synopsis of Psychiatric, Chapter 1.2 Functional Neuroanatomy, Page number 6.

711.q: Which statement accurately reflects the psychiatric considerations in patients with epilepsy?
o: Psychosis is more commonly observed during the ictal phase of seizures than during the interictal phase.
Mood disorders, such as depression, are rarely seen in patients with epilepsy
Increased religiosity and personality changes are often noted in patients with temporal lobe epilepsy
Most patients with epilepsy do not require any psychological support
711.e: Explanation: Personality disorders, mood disorders, and psychotic symptoms may be more common in patients with epilepsy, particularly those with temporal lobe epilepsy. Psychotic symptoms are generally more prevalent during the interictal period rather than the ictal phase. Ictal symptoms are typically characterised by disorganised behaviour rather than psychosis (Option A) . Mood disorders, including depression and anxiety, are more common in patients with epilepsy than in the general population. This can significantly affect the patient's quality of life (Option B) . Many patients with epilepsy benefit from psychological support and counselling to address the psychosocial implications of their diagnosis, including coping with chronic illness and managing stigma (Option D) .

712.q: A patient is on treatment of depression, complaining of painful coitus/sexual dysfunction. Which drug will you switch him on to address his problem?
712.e: Bupropion is NDRI. Others can increase the level of serotonin, which can cause sexual side effects. Reference: Kaplan and Saddocks Synopsis of Psychiaitry, 11th Edition, Chapter 29, Page No.: 954

712.q: Which of the following is an adverse effect of an antidepressant drug, k/as a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor?
712.e: Sexual dysfunction is a well-documented adverse effect of SSRIs. These drugs can cause various sexual problems, such as decreased libido, delayed ejaculation or difficulty achieving orgasm. This adverse effect can significantly impact a patient's quality of life. Other options: B.Dry mouth - Dry mouth is a common side effect of many medications, including some antidepressants, but it is not specific to SSRIs. C.Blurring of vision - Blurred vision is not a commonly reported side effect of SSRIs. D.Constipation - Constipation is also not a common side effect of SSRIs. Key Takeaway: Sexual dysfunction is a common and well-documented adverse effect of SSRIs , which can impact adherence to treatment.

712.q: How to differentiate between psychological and organic erectile dysfunction ?
712.e: Ans. A. Nocturnal penile tumescence One of the important method to distinguish psychogenic impotence from organic imPotence is nocturnal penile tumsescence & early morning erection which are preserved in psychogenic impotence but not in organic cause of impotence.

713.q: Under hypnosis or during psychotherapy, a patient may recover a memory of a painful experience or conflict-particularly of sexual or physical abuse, that is etiologically significant. This is known as:
713.e: Under hypnosis or during psychotherapy , a patient may recover a memory of a painful experience or conflict-particularly of sexual or physical abuse - that is etiologically significant. When the repressed material is brought back to consciousness, the person not only may recall the experience but may relive it, accompanied by the appropriate affective response (a process called abreaction). If the event recalled never really happened but the person believes it to be true and reacts accordingly, it is known as false memory syndrome. (Option A) Reference: Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11th edition, Chapter 12, Dissociative disorders, Page number 463.

713.q: A 35-year-old businessman enjoys dressing up in his wife's clothes. He says he does so to experience what it feels like to be a woman and it does not cause him sexual arousal. He has no desire to be a woman and he is very much comfortable with his genital organs. What is the correct term to describe his behavior?
713.e: Dual-role transvestism: Patient wears the dress of opposite sex to enjoy the temporary feeling of belonging to other sex. Unlike trans sexualism, there is no desire of permanent sex change. There is no sexual arousal associated with cross dressing. Reference: Kaplan and Saddocks Synopsis of Psychiaitry, 11th Edition, Chapter 17, Page No.: 597

713.q: According to Freud, during psychosexual development a boy focuses his love on his mother. This can reach a stage where a boy becomes jealous of his father and wants to kill him. However, he cannot do this for fear of castration and so represses these urges as he moves to the next stage of development. Which of the following describes the boy's psychosocial development?
713.e: According to Freud there are five stages of psychosexual development. The approximate age range of the stages is characterised by: Oral phase : 1 year of fixation on mouth and lips – relation to sucking, biting and mouthing. Anal phase : 1–3 years of fixation on anal cavity – relation to toilet training. Phallic phase : 3–5/6 years of fixation and sensitivity to genitals. The Oedipus complex occurs only in this stage. Latency phase : 5/6 years of puberty – sexual preoccupations of earlier years repressed. Genital phase : puberty/maturity – new demands and sexual desires. This was described by Freud and occurs during the phallic stage of psychosexual development . The Oedipus complex derives its name from a classical Greek tragedy about Oedipus Rex who killed his father. Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, eleventh edition, chapter 4, page no. 157

713.q: An 8-month-old girl enjoyed picking up toys and bringing them to her mouth. She was often seen sucking them. What phase of Freud's psychosexual development is she going through?
713.e: According to Freud there are five stages of psychosexual development. The approximate age range of the stages is characterised by: Oral phase : 1 year of fixation on mouth and lips – relation to sucking, biting and mouthing. Anal phase : 1–3 years of fixation on anal cavity – relation to toilet training. Phallic phase : 3–5/6 years of fixation and sensitivity to genitals. The Oedipus complex occurs only in this stage. Latency phase : 5/6 years of puberty – sexual preoccupations of earlier years repressed. Genital phase : puberty/maturity – new demands and sexual desires. Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, eleventh edition, chapter 4, page no. 157

713.q: Drug-facilitated rape is a type of acquaintance sexual assault done by allegedly placing some drugs in the beverage of the victim surreptitiously. The sexual encounter is not remembered by the victim due to anterograde amnesia. Which drug out of the following is a 'date rape drug':
713.e: Gamma-Hydroxy-Butyrate, ketamine, and Rohypnol (Flunitrazepam) have been called 'date rape drugs' because they produce disorienting and sedating effects and often users cannot recall what occurred during all or part of an episode under the influence of the drug. Hence, it is alleged that these drugs might be surreptitiously placed in a beverage or a person might be convinced to take the drug and then not recall clearly what occurred after ingestion. Reference: Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11 th edition, Chapter number 20.9, Stimulant-related disorders, Page number 679.

713.q: Some children who have undergone physical or sexual abuse are unable to recall specific painful memories related to the abuse. They either repress/supress such painful memories. This kind of psychogenic amnesia is known as _____________.
713.e: Catathymic amnesia is the inability to recall specific painful memories , and is believed to occur due to the defence mechanism of repression However, it is unclear whether the repression is driven by a conscious motivation to forget, i.e., suppression, or whether it is unconscious, i.e., primary repression Under hypnosis or during psychotherapy , a patient may recover a memory of a painful experience or conflict-particularly of sexual or physical abuse-that is etiologically significant When the repressed material is brought back to consciousness, the person not only may recall the experience but may relive it , accompanied by the appropriate affective response This process is called abreaction Reference: Fish’s Clinical Psychopathology, third edition, Chapter 5 Disorders of Memory, Page no. 65

713.q: Which of the following is not a predictor of suicide?
713.e: Adolescent age is not a predictor of suicide. Reference: Kaplan and Saddocks Synopsis of Psychiaitry, 11th Edition, Chapter 23, Page No.: 768

713.q: A homosexual person feels that he is a woman trapped in man's body and has persistent discomfort with his sex. Most likely diagnosis is:
713.e: Person suffering from Trans-sexualism is not happy with his genital organs and always insist for sex change and to be treated like opposite sex. Reference: Kaplan and Saddocks Synopsis of Psychiaitry, 11th Edition, Chapter 18, Page No.: 600

714.q: Fetal alcohol syndrome is a known preventable cause of intellectual disability. Which of the following is true about alcohol use in pregnant women?
o: Any amount of alcohol use is not recommended during pregnancy
Up to 3 standard drinks per day in pregnancy is not causative for fetal alcohol syndrome
More than 7 standard drinks per week in pregnancy can lead to fetal alcohol syndrome
Occasional use of alcohol during pregnancy is not harmful
714.e: The National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism defines at-risk alcohol use for healthy nonpregnant women as > 3 drinks per occasion or > 7 drinks per week and any amount of drinking for women who are pregnant or at risk of pregnancy. Reference: Alcohol Use in Pregnancy (nih.gov)

714.q: Deciding to take an antacid before indulging in a spicy meal to avoid gastric distress is an example of which form of learning?
714.e: Negative reinforcement refers to giving a stimulus or event , which when its cessation or termination is contingent on a response, increases the likelihood that the response will occur again . Avoidance learning is seen in negative reinforcement , where to avoid an adverse event, the stimuli is avoided. For example, to avoid gastric distress, antacid is taken before eating a spicy meal. Reference : Morgan and King's Introduction to Psychology, 7th edition, Chapter 4 Principles of Learning, Page number 149.

714.q: A 25-year-old male, who once got trapped in an elevator, has now started avoiding all small enclosed spaces like other elevators, closed rooms, bathrooms, etc. for the fear that something embarrassing might happen to him there. The principle of Pavlovian conditioning which explains this is known as:
714.e: A person or animal tends to generalize the conditioned response to other stimuli that are somewhat similar to the original conditioned stimuli. The greater the similarity , the greater the generalisation among conditioned stimuli. Hence, in the above case scenario, where the person is phobic to all small enclosed spaces, which are like his original conditioned stimuli of being trapped in an elevator , is suggestive of stimulus generalisation. Reference : Morgan and King's Introduction to Psychology, 7th edition, Chapter 4 Principles of Learning, Page number 146.

714.q: Students are often encouraged to perform better by giving medals and trophies for their achievement in academics or other extracurricular activities. This form of learning which modulates behavior is known as:
714.e: Positive reinforcer is a stimulus or event , which, when it follows a response, increases the likelihood that the response will be made again. For example, receiving medals or trophies, praise from parents, etc. can act as positive reinforcers to enhance performance of students. Reference : Morgan and King's Introduction to Psychology, 7th edition, Chapter 4 Principles of Learning, Page number 149.

714.q: A 7-year-old boy with severe intellectual disability was evaluated when he transferred to a new private school. Observed in his classroom, when he was prompted to engage in tasks that required that he take his hands out of his pockets, he began hitting his head with his hands. If his hands were held by the teacher, he hit his head with his knees. He was adept in contorting himself, so that he could hit or kick himself in almost any position, even while walking. Such behaviour is least likely with:
714.e: Genetic syndromes associated with self-injurious behaviour are Lesch Nyhan syndrome, Rett syndrome, Prader-Willi syndrome, Smith-Magenis syndrome and Oculocerebral syndrome of Lowe. Reference: Self-injurious behaviour as part of genetic syndromes - PubMed(nih.gov)

714.q: A child with IQ 50, which of the following is true?
o: Can follow simple verbal commands and handle money
714.e: 50 - 69: Mild MR. Mild MR people can have an independent living, handle money, study till 6 th class. Reference: Kaplan and Saddocks Synopsis of Psychiaitry, 11th Edition, Chapter 31, Page No.: 1120

714.q: What is the age limit for a child as defined under the POCSO Act, 2012?
714.e: Explanation: Under the Protection of Children from sexual offences act (POSCO) of 2012, a child is defined as any person, regardless of gender, who is below 18 years of age. Reference: The Protection of Children from sexual offences act, 2012

714.q: Who developed the theory of learning known as operant conditioning?
714.e: BF Skinner: Operant conditioning JB Watson: Extinction Ivan Pavlov: Classic conditioning Albert Bandura: Social learning Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, eleventh edition, chapter 2, page no. 102

715.q: Which of the following is a technique used in treatment of tic disorders?
715.e: Habit reversal technique is used in management of tic disorders. It involves several components aimed at increasing tic awareness, developing competing responses to tics and building and sustaining motivation and compliance. Reference: Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11 th edition, Chapter 31.8c, Tourette's disorder, Page number 1202.

715.q: A 35-year-old married woman with a history of depressive disorder presents in the outpatient department complaining of loss of libido. Which antidepressant medication would be the most suitable to prescribe to address this side effect?
715.e: Mirtazapine has a lower incidence of sexual side effects than most other antidepressants at 24%. SSRIs may indirectly decrease libido through a direct inhibition of sexual arousal and orgasm.(Option A) Tricyclic antidepressants may decrease libido indirectly through sedation. Venlafaxine can inhibit arousal and orgasm.(Option D) Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 29th, Page no. 993.

715.q: You get a call from the duty obstetrician about a 32-year-old woman who was 15 week's pregnant and her bipolar affective disorder was stabilized on lithium. Which of the following statements about use of lithium in pregnancy is correct?
o: Lithium is not excreted in breast milk.
Lithium use does not affect the fetus in the second trimester.
Serum lithium levels increase in the third trimester of pregnancy.
Serum lithium levels increase in the immediate postpartum period.
715.e: Lithium is excreted in breast milk , so it should be explained clearly to the mother about the effect of lithium in newborn babies.( OPTION A IS FALSE ) Lithium can affect the baby during the second and third trimesters. It can have toxic effects if serum lithium levels are very high and can also cause cardiac dysfunction, diabetes insipidus and hypothyroidism in the fetus.( OPTION B IS FALSE ) Lithium levels fall during the third trimester of pregnancy.( OPTION C IS FALSE) However, immediately after delivery, the serum concentration starts to rise , so lithium levels should be closely monitored.( CORRECT OPTION D) Lithium use is usually associated with Ebstein's anomaly of the tricuspid valve. Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 29th, Page no. 987.

715.q: Which of the following most closely reflects the risk of bipolar affective disorder in a first degree relative of an affected proband?
715.e: Five to ten per cent. This contrasts with 5-10% in population controls. Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 8, page no. 365

715.q: Which of the following questionnaire systems is used for eating disorder:
715.e: SCOFF QUESTIONNAIRE: screening test for eating disorder S - Sick - Do you feel sick that you have eaten a lot? C - Control - Do you think you have lost control over amount of food you eat?≥ O - One stone - have you lost more than 6Kg in last 3-6 months? F - Fat - Do you believe that your are Fat when others are saying, you are thin? F - Food - do you think food dominates your life? If yes for ≥ 2 questions - Detailed examination needed Reference: The SCOFF questionnaire, Morgan JF, Reid F, Lacey JH. The SCOFF Questionnaire-A new screening tool for Eating Disorder. West J Med. 2000 Mar;172(3), Page No.: 164-165

715.q: A 45-year-old female, following a quarrel with her husband and children, presented with sudden loss of voice over for few hours. Though she would try to speak out hard, only whispering sounds would be heard. In this case, hysterical aphonia can be ruled out from other organic causes of aphonia by:
715.e: Hysterical aphonia ( Conversion disorder symptom ) is presented with sudden loss of voice which is usually precipitated by an acute psychological stressor In hysterical aphonia, though the patient can make only whispering sounds, however, on asking the patient to cough or laugh , he/ she can produce normal cough sound or laughter sound The structure of larynx is found to be the normal The movement of vocal cords may slightly be diminished Reference: Kaplan and Sadock’s Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 13.4, Functional Neurological Symptom Disorder (Conversion Disorder), Page 476

715.q: A 3-year-old girl child had normal development until 18 month's age, after which regression of achieved milestones, deceleration of head circumference, hand wringing movements and impairment in intellectual functions and communication skills was observed. Which is the mode of inheritance of genetic abnormality in this girl?
715.e: Rett syndrome, now diagnosed in the DSM-5 as a form of autism spectrum disorder, is believed to be caused by a dominant X-linked gene. It is degenerative and affects only females. Head circumference deceleration, deterioration in communications skills, motor behaviour and social functioning starts at about 1 year of age. Symptoms include ataxia, facial grimacing, teeth-grinding and loss of speech. Stereotypical hand movements, including hand-wringing, are typical. Reference: Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11 th edition, Chapter 31.3, Intellectual disability, Page number 1124.

715.q: A 7-year-old boy has presented with social communication difficulties and repeated stereotypical behaviours. Which of the following biomarkers could be identified in this boy? I. Elevated histamine II. Increased total brain volume III. Theory of mind deficits IV. Impaired occipital lobe processing V. Impaired frontal lobe processing VI. Dysfunction of mirror neuron system
715.e: Biomarkers in autism spectrum disorder: Elevated serotonin in platelets Increased total brain volume Disruption of sensitive or critical periods within brain's plasticity Theory of mind deficits Tendency to scan faces differently than controls Greater amygdala hyper-arousal Dysfunction of mirror neuron system Decreased activation of left frontal regions during memory and language-based tasks Reference: Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11 th edition, Chapter 31.5, Autism spectrum disorder, Page number 1154.

716.q: A child with untreated ADHD is most likely to develop which of the following disorders during adolescence?
o: Separation from parents leading to depression
716.e: Explanation: Untreated Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in childhood is associated with an increased risk of developing Conduct Disorder during adolescence. Children with ADHD often display impulsivity, aggression, and difficulty following rules, which may escalate into more severe behavioural problems, including violating the rights of others and engaging in antisocial behaviour . Explanation for other options: Binge eating (Option A) is not typically associated with untreated ADHD, although some individuals with ADHD may engage in emotional eating. Selective mutism (Option B) is more commonly associated with anxiety disorders and is not directly linked to ADHD. Separation from parent leading to depression (Option C) is not a common progression from ADHD, though emotional difficulties can arise, especially in children with comorbid conditions

716.q: A 50-year-old homeless male veteran is brought to the emergency department by the police for disruptive behaviour. On mental status examination, he has an elevated affect, but also has psychomotor agitation and paranoia; he says he "feels fantastic" but is wary of answering any questions, quickly becoming irritated. On physical examination, the patient exhibits a moderately elevated blood pressure and pulse rate. He is most likely intoxicated with which of the following substances?
716.e: Cocaine(or other stimulants such as amphetamine) intoxication can present with Euphoria Irritability Anxiety Psychotic symptoms such as paranoia Elevated vital signs Conversely, intoxication with alcohol, barbiturates, benzodiazepines and opiates generally causes depression, somnolence and depressed vital signs(OPTIONS A, B, & C). Reference: Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 20.9, Stimulant-related disorders, Page no. 675.

716.q: In a delirious patient, disturbances in attention increase towards the evening time due to sensory deprivation. This is known as:
716.e: In delirious state, the patient becomes more disturbed, disoriented, hyper vigilant towards the evening after sunset due to sensory deprivation. This is known as sun downing. Reference: Kaplan and Sadock’s Comprehensive Textbook of Psychiatry, 10 th edition, Chapter 10.2 Delirium, Page number 3062.

716.q: Which of the following is true regarding the clinical presentation of OCD?
716.e: Patients with obsessions usually harbour their difficulties for a long time (often 5 to10 years) before they present to a doctor . (Option A & B) The ego-dystonic nature of obsessions results in anxiety and reduces help seeking and sharing of their secret illness. OCD has its origin in adolescence or childhood . But most patients do not seek help until they are in their twenties or thirties . Often the onset of depression brings OCD to clinical attention. Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 10, page no. 423

716.q: All of the following Disruptive and Impulse control disorders are seen in adults except?
716.e: Intermittent Explosive disorder, Kleptomania and Pyromania are classified as Disruptive and Impulse Control disorders seen in adulthood. Whereas Oppositional defiant disorder and Conduct disorder are seen in childhoodor adolescence . Reference: Kaplan and Sadock’s Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11 th edition, Chapter 19 Disruptive, Impulse control, and Conduct disorders, Page number 608.

716.q: Which of the following is the most critical criterion for diagnosing gender dysphoria in children, according to the DSM-5?
o: Strong preference for clothing typical of another gender
Insistence on being another gender or desire to be another gender
Desire for primary or secondary sexual characteristics of the desired gender
716.e: Explanation: The DSM-5 emphasizes the child's self-perception and the desire or insistence that one is another gender as the most critical criterion for gender dysphoria in children. Other behaviours (like preference for opposite-gender clothing or playmates) are supportive but not primary diagnostic criteria. Gender Dysphoria In Children: Key Diagnostic Criterion: The most critical factor for diagnosing gender dysphoria in children is desire or insistence on being another gender. Behavioural Characteristics: Preference for clothing, toys, and games typically associated with the opposite gender. Desire to take on roles of the opposite gender during play. Rejection of same-gender stereotypes and preference for other-gender playmates. Dislike of their own sexual anatomy or a desire to have the sexual characteristics of the desired gender.

716.q: All of the following are sub-types of Oppositional Defiant disorder except:
716.e: DSM-5 has divided oppositional defiant disorder into three types: Angry/Irritable Mood Argumentative/ Defiant Behaviour Vindictiveness Crying is not a sub-type of Oppositional Defiant Disorder. Reference : Kaplan and Sadock’s Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11 th edition, Chapter 31.12 Oppositional Defiant Disorder, Page number 1244.

716.q: All of the following themes are usually present in children with conduct disorder except:
o: Lack of remorse/ guilt for their actions
716.e: Individuals with conduct disorder can exhibit a persistent interpersonal and emotional pattern that can be characterized by at least two of the following: Lack of remorse or guilt Callous lack of empathy Unconcerned about performance Shallow or deficient affect. Communication skills, however, are not lacking in those with conduct disorder. Reference : Kaplan and Sadock’s Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11 th edition, Chapter 31.12 Conduct disorder, Page number 1247.

717.q: A 25 year old female is presented to OPD with complaints of agitation, muttering to herself and sleep disturbances. She claims that her husband has stolen the baby from her womb. She has delivered a healthy child three weeks back, however has not taking care of the baby. What is the most probable diagnosis?
717.e: Nihilistic delusion is associated postpartum and duration is around 3 weeks. Diagnosis is Postpartum psychosis. Reference: Kaplan and Saddocks Synopsis of Psychiaitry, 11th Edition, Chapter 8, Page No.: 357

717.q: Which one of the following is NOT a poor prognostic factor in OCD?
717.e: It is observed that about 20–30% of those with OCD show a significant improvement, 40–50% have a moderate improvement, while the rest have a chronic or worsening course. Poor prognostic factors include yielding to compulsions, a childhood onset , male , bizarre content of compulsions, need for hospitalization , a coexisting major depressive disorder , the presence of overvalued ideas , and the presence of personality disorder (especially schizotypal). (Option A, B & C) A good prognosis is indicated by good premorbid adjustment, the presence of a precipitating event, and episodic nature. The content or theme of obsessions and family history do not relate to the prognosis . Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, Eleventh edition, Chapter 10, page no. 420

717.q: Which of the following is/are leading cause of death among 15-24 years old?
717.e: Unintentional injury and homicide were the leading causes of death among residents ages 15-24, each accounting for 34.2% and 32.9%, respectively, of all deaths. These were followed by suicide (9.9%) and cancer (5.8%). Accidents (unintentional injuries), homicide, suicide, cancer, and heart disease make up the five leading causes of death for teenagers Reference : https://cchealth.org/health-data/hospital-council/2010/pdf/11_lcd_by_age.pdf

717.q: The Mental Health Gap Action Programme (mhGAP) does not include which of the following disorders?
717.e: Explanation: The Mental Health Gap Action Programme (mhGAP) by the World Health Organization (WHO) aims to improve access to mental health care in low and middle-income countries. It focuses on priority conditions including: Depression (Option B) Schizophrenia (Option C) Bipolar disorder Epilepsy Dementia Self-harm Alcohol and substance use disorders Child and adolescent mental disorders (Option D) OCD is not listed as a core mhGAP target condition. References: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK310854/

717.q: Who has the right to make complaints about deficiencies in the provision of mental health services?
o: Only healthcare professionals can file complaints
The person with a mental illness or their nominated representative has the right to make complaints
The concerned Board can file complaints on behalf of the person with a mental illness
Only legal guardians can make complaints
717.e: Explanation: Under the Mental Healthcare Act (MHCA) 2017, a person with a mental illness (PMI) has the right to complain about any deficiencies in the provision of mental health services. If the person is unable to do so, their nominated representative (NR) can file a complaint on their behalf. Reference: The Mental Healthcare Act, 2017

717.q: What is the maximum duration of emergency treatment a person with mental illness can receive under the Mental Health Care Act, 2017?
717.e: Explanation: As per section 94 of the Mental Healthcare Act (MHCA) 2017, emergency treatment can be provided for up to 72 hours, with the consent of the nominated representative (if available). Any medical practitioner can provide emergency treatment as per the provisions of this section of the act. Reference: The Mental Healthcare Act, 2017

717.q: Which of the following is a common form of asynchronous communication used in telemedicine?
717.e: Explanation: Asynchronous communication refers to interactions that do not occur in real time. Asynchronous communication includes methods like email, where information can be sent at one time and reviewed later, unlike real-time communication, such as video conferencing (Option A), Telephonic consultations (Option C), and Live chat forums (Option D). Reference: Telemedicine Practice Guidelines, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, 2020

717.q: Which is the last stage of psychosocial development as described by Erikson?
717.e: Erikson, a student of Freud, accepted the basic theory of early psychosocial development but proposed that development continues across the lifespan, particularly in terms of the developing relationship between the individual and the social system within which they live. He underlined the social context for this final stage of growth. In Childhood and Society, he wrote, 'the style of integrity developed by his culture or civilisation thus becomes the "patrimony" of his soul In such final consolidation, death loses its sting When the attempt to attain integrity has failed, the individual may become deeply disgusted with external world and contemptuous of persons as well institutions Reference: Synopsis of Psychiatry, eleventh edition, chapter 4, page no. 169

718.q: A 12-year-old girl complains of feeling depressed frequently and having nightmares since last 4 months. On delving deeper, she revealed to the psychiatrist that she has been having these symptoms after one of her uncles molested her in an isolated place. She has not talked about this event to anyone (including her parents) due to shame and requests the psychiatrist too not to reveal it to anyone. What should be the role of psychiatrist in this case?
o: Confidentiality in this case can't be breached as the patient has denied revealing
Confidentiality should be breached as this is a matter of child sexual abuse
Confidentiality can be breached only after taking consent of the patient in this case
Confidentiality should only be breached if the matter involves legal court
718.e: If a child has been the victim of physical or sexual abuse, then psychiatrists are required to make an immediate report to an appropriate agency . ( Option B is CORRECT ) In this situation, confidentiality is decisively limited by legal statute on the grounds that potential or actual harm to vulnerable children outweighs the value of confidentiality in a psychiatric setting. Reference : Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11th edition, Chapter 36.1 Forensic Psychiatry, Page number 1383.

718.q: An expert psychiatrist has been called upon to assess testamentary capacity for a 65-year-old male contemplating on making a written will of his properties. Which of the following symptoms if present in this testator can suggest of testamentary incapacity?
o: Paranoid delusions regarding his family members
718.e: Symptoms of testamentary incapacity Difficulties in attention and information processing Language difficulties Memory difficulties Impairment of higher executive functions Persecutory delusions ( Option B ) Delusions of poverty( Option C ) Reference : https://www.lawyersclubindia.com/experts/files/61400_184055_article_on_wills.pdf

718.q: Which statements are correct with respect to Mental Healthcare Act 2017 ? 1. Suicidal act has been decriminalised 2. Advanced directive and Nominated representative are concepts newly introduced 3. ECT has been approved for use in minors 4. No restrictions on performing Psychosurgery 5. Chaining in any manner or form is prohibited 6. ECT can be used as a form of emergency treatment
718.e: According to Mental healthcare Act 2017, Section 309 suicide attempt is decriminalised , considering the fact that those attempting suicide undergo lot of stress ( Statement 1 is Correct ) Advanced directive which allows a person to modify one’s treatment options and Nominated representative can be appointed. ( Statement 2 is Correct ) Use of ECT in minors is restricted; if needed, permission from Mental Health Review Board is essential. Also, ECT cannot be used as emergency treatment. (Statement 3 & 6 are Wrong) Similarly, performing psychosurgeries like lobotomies or cingulotomy is restricted without permission from Mental Health Review Board. (Statement 4 is Wrong) Chaining (physical restraint) is prohibited procedure under this act. (Statement 5 is Correct) Reference : https://www.prsindia.org/uploads/media/Mental%20Health/Mental%20Healthcare%20Act,%202017.pdf

718.q: All of the following are indications for seclusion/restraint of a psychiatric patient except:
o: For punishment or convenience of staff
To prevent clear imminent harm to patient and others
As a part of behaviour therapy
718.e: Indications for seclusion and restraint: Prevent clear, imminent harm to the patient or others ( Option C ) Prevent significant disruption to treatment program or physical surroundings Assist in treatment as part of ongoing behaviour therapy ( Option D ) Decrease sensory overstimulation ( Option A ) Patient's voluntary reasonable request Contraindications for seclusion and restraint: Extremely unstable medical and psychiatric conditions Delirious or demented patients who are unable to tolerate decreased stimulation Overtly suicidal patients Patients with severe drug reactions or overdoses or who require close monitoring of drug dosages For punishment or convenience of staff ( Option B ) Reference : Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 11th edition, Chapter 36.1 Forensic Psychiatry, Page number 1387.

718.q: A patient diagnosed with Bipolar-I disorder; current episode Manic, severe has been admitted. After admission, he exhibits extremely violent behaviour, in form of destruction of hospital properties and trying to hit the medical staff as well as his relatives. Which of the following statement is false regarding his management (keeping in mind Mental Healthcare Act 2017)?
o: The patient can be secluded in a separate facility under proper observation and monitoring
The patient can be physically restrained using ropes and chains as he is at risk of harm to others
The patient can be chemically restrained using neuroleptics
718.e: Chaining in any form or manner is a prohibited using Mental Health Care Act 2017. Reference : https://www.prsindia.org/uploads/media/Mental%20Health/Mental%20Healthcare%20Act,%202017.pdf

718.q: What is the legal status of statements made during a narcoanalysis test in India?
o: Statements are fully admissible in court
Statements are admissible only if recorded under supervision
Statements can be used to convict the accused
718.e: Explanation: Narcoanalysis is primarily a deception detection technique, also known as the "truth serum" test. Initially used in military settings, it is now employed in forensic investigations. Uses barbiturates (e.g., Sodium Pentothal) to induce a semi-conscious state, lowering inhibitions and making it harder to lie. The Supreme Court of India (Selvi vs. The state of Karnataka, 2010) held that involuntary administration of Narcoanalysis Polygraph test Brain-mapping as unconstitutional and inadmissible as evidence in the court of law. Reference: Selvi vs. State of Karnataka

719.q: A patient presents with abrupt loss of reading ability despite being literate, however, when asked to write, he could write spontaneously. This can be caused due to:
719.e: Alexia without agraphia (patient can’t read, but can write) = Infarct to left Posterior cerebral artery. Reference: Alexia Without Agraphia: A Rare Entity (nih.gov)

719.q: Who received Nobel Prize for demonstrating role of dopamine as a neurotransmitter in the brain?
719.e: In 1957, Dr. Arvid Carlson showed that dopamine was a neurotransmitter in the brain and not just a precursor of norepinephrine. This was the prevailing view at that time. He also developed an assay to measure dopamine in the brain and found that the highest regional concentration existed in the basal ganglia. Reference: Arvid Carlson, and the story of dopamine (nih.gov)

719.q: All of the following are the products of cannabis except:
719.e: Heroine is opioid Reference: Kaplan and Saddocks Synopsis of Psychiaitry, 11th Edition, Chapter 20, Page No.: 644
Squeeze technique and Stop start technique are used for Premature ejaculation. Reference: Kaplan and Saddocks Synopsis of Psychiaitry, 11th Edition, Chapter 17, Page No.: 585

719.q: What is the age range of juveniles who may be tried as adults for heinous offences under the JJ Act 2015?
719.e: Explanation: Juveniles aged 16-18 years who commit heinous offences may be tried as adults under the Juvenile Justice Act of 2015, depending on the nature of the crime. Heinous offences are those punishable for a term of 7 years or more under the Indian Penal Code (IPC). Reference: The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015

719.q: Which of the following best describes capacity in the context of informed consent?
o: The participant's ability to freely make decisions without external interference
The participant's ability to understand the information provided and form a reasonable judgment
The participant's understanding of the risks and benefits of the research
The participant's willingness to participate in the research study
719.e: Explanation: Informed consent is an autonomous decision made by an individual regarding medical interventions or research participation. It ensures individual autonomy and rational decision-making. Types of Consent: Informed vs. Real Consent: Informed: Full understanding of diagnosis, risks, and prognosis. Real: In line with the "prudent person rule" (reasonable doctor's judgment). Implicit vs. Explicit Consent: Implicit: Implied through actions (e.g., showing up for examination). Explicit: Clearly expressed, either verbal or written.

719.q: Which of the following noradrenergic receptors is presynaptic?
719.e: All except one of the adrenergic receptors are postsynaptic. The only presynaptic adrenergic receptor is the α2-receptor (OPTION B IS CORRECT) . This is also known as a presynaptic auto-receptor. It is a G-protein couple receptor . Reference: Stahls Essential Psychopharmacology, Fourth edition, Chapter 2, Page no. 38.

719.q: Which of the following neurotransmitters does venlafaxine act on?
719.e: Venlafaxine has a unique mode of action. In low doses , it acts on the serotonin system only . As the dose increases , it acts on noradrenergic as well as serotonergic neurons. At higher does, i.e., 225 mg or above, it acts on all the three neurotransmitters, i.e. serotonin, noradrenaline and dopamine (OPTION D IS CORRECT) . In a nutshell, venlafaxine blocks the serotonin, noradrenaline and dopamine reuptake. In addition, blocking noradrenaline reuptake in the frontal cortex could increase dopamine neurotransmission in this part of brain. Reference: Stahls Essential Psychopharmacology, Fourth edition, Chapter 7th, Page no. 306.

720.q: Which of the following is the first imaging modality of choice in adenomyosis?
720.e: Transvaginal sonography is generally the first choice imaging modality in symptomatic patients with adenomyosis. It is widely available, safe, and low cost with good accuracy, similar to that reported for MRI. MRI is IOC and shows thickening of junctional zone. Reference: Callens page number 1056

720.q: Which of the following modality is used in cystic lesions of ovary?
720.e: Ultrasound imaging is used to assess whether an ovarian cyst is simple or complex and to determine cyst measurement. Simple Cyst is Anechoic with Posterior Acoustic Shadowing Hemorrhagic Ovarian cyst shows internl debris with fibrin strands giving a fish net/reticular/lacy appearance. Ground Glass appearance on Ultrasound Is suggestive Of Endometrioma/Chocolate Cyst Dot and Dash pattern on ultrasound is suggestive of Dermoid cyst/Mature cystic teratoma Reference: Callens page number - 1019

720.q: Which of the following is the most important feature in determining the malignancy of cystic ovarian lesion?
o: Presence of solid component with colour flow
720.e: The presence of a solid component, with detectable flow by Doppler imaging, within a cystic ovarian mass is the most important sonographic feature for predicting ovarian malignancy. There is also evidence that the larger the solid component within a cystic mass, the higher the risk of malignancy. Reference: Callen's Ultrasonography in Obstetrics and Gynecology, sixth edition page number 924

720.q: The most Sensitive Imaging Investigation of choice to Diagnose Mullerian duct Abnormalities?
720.e: MRI is the investigation of choice for Mullerian Duct Anomalies Newer modality - 3D USG also has high sensitivity and specificity and accuracy comparable to MRI.

720.q: Fetal anomaly scan is usually done around?
720.e: The fetal anomaly scan or TIFFA scan (Target Imaging for Fetal anomaly) is a 2nd trimester ultrasound usually done between 18-20 weeks of gestation primarily used to assess fetal anomaly and detect the presence of any fetal anomalies. Reference: Ultrasound in obstetrics and gynecology by Dr. P. K. shah, Dr. Mandakini megh,

720.q: Myocardial Viability is best evaluated by?
720.e: Myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) using Thallium-201, Sestamibi, or Tetrofosmin assesses blood flow to the heart and is useful for diagnosing coronary artery disease (CAD) and evaluating myocardial infarction. Pyrophosphate scans detect acute myocardial infarction (AMI) or areas of myocardial necrosis. 18FDG PET is used to assess myocardial viability, distinguishing between viable and non-viable myocardium, which is crucial for treatment decisions in CAD and heart failure.

720.q: Best Imaging Modality for Perthes disease is?
720.e: MRI is The IOC for AVN and Perthes Disease(AVN in Young) MRI is also the IOC for Ankylosing Spondylitis, Acute Osteomyelitis and Stress/March Fracture.

720.q: Which of the following sign is seen in mucor mycosis?
720.e: The common imaging features of mucor mycosis is "Black turbinate sign" and non enhancing sino-nasal mucosa, orbital involvement, and diffusion restriction in the optic nerve. Intracranial involvement was seen as perineural extension into the brain, cerebritis, and internal carotid artery involvement. Reference: Yadav T, Tiwari S, Gupta A, Garg PK, Khera PS, Rajagopal R, Goyal A, Soni K, Chugh A, Jain V, Sureka B, Elhence P, Misra S. Magnetic Resonance Imaging in Coronavirus Disease - 2019 Associated Rhino-Orbital-Cerebral Mucormycosis (CA-ROCM) - Imaging Analysis of 50 Consecutive Patients. Curr Probl Diagn Radiol. 2022 Jan-Feb;51(1):112-120. doi: 10.1067/j.cpradiol.2021.09.004. Epub 2021 Nov 3. PMID: 34802841; PMCID: PMC8564981.

721.q: Which of the following is not an ionising radiation?
721.e: Ionizing radiation is the term given to forms of radiation that are energetic enough to displace orbiting electrons from the atoms in the absorbing medium, thus forming positive ions. High Energy Electromagnetic Radiation like X Rays, Gamma Rays, and Cosmic Rays are Ionising Radiation Particulate Radiation Like Alpha, Beta, Protons, Neutrons, and Electrons are Ionising Radiation. Most other electromagnetic radiation like UV rays, Visible light, Infrared Rays, Radiowaves are Nonionising Sound waves used in Ultrasound are also Nonionising. Reference: Bell, D. Ionizing radiation. Reference article, Radiopaedia.org. https://doi.org/10.53347/rID-59177

721.q: At what speed do the x rays travel?
721.e: All electromagnetic Radiation have the same velocity, that is velocity of speed of Light. Reference: Christensen's Physics of diagnostic radiology page 6

721.q: Greatest risk to foetus for malformations due to radiation exposure is between ______ weeks.
721.e: The embryo/foetus is most susceptible to teratogenic effects of radiation during 2-7 weeks as this is the period of organogenesis The foetus is more resistant to the radiation during the second and third trimester. Reference : Yoon I, Slesinger TL. Radiation Exposure In Pregnancy. [Updated 2022 May 8]. In: Stat Pearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): Stat Pearls Publishing; 2022 Jan.

721.q: A 7 week pregnant lady underwent a Chest X ray by mistake, what is to be done?
721.e: Accidental Exposure of Radiation during pregnancy-reassure the patient and continue the pregnancy as the threshold required for fetal damage is very high and termination is usually not advised unless very high exposure Above 10RAD, which is highly unlikely with routine diagnostic modalities.

721.q: All are True about modern Xray tube except?
o: Heat loss is mainly by Radiation
Rhenium is added to tungsten target at Anode
Chief source of Xray generation is by Bremstrahlung effect
721.e: Modern X ray tube has a rotatory anode, not cathode Motor is attached to the anode to make it rotatory The Cathode is made of Tungsten alloyed with Thorium The Target of Anode is made of Tungsten Alloyed with Rhenium The major source of X RAY Generation in Modern X ray tube is Bremstrahlung Radiation/Braking Radiation

721.q: Which of the following is true statement regarding radiation ?
o: Rapidly dividing cells are resistant to Radiation
GI mucosa is one of the most radioresistant tissue in the body
The intensity of Radiation is inversely proportional to the square of distance from the source
Small blood vessels are least resistant to radiation
721.e: According to Inverse square law in radiation, the intensity of radiation is inversely proportional to the square of distance from the source. Rapidly dividing cells , which are less differentiated are actually more radiosensitive Amongst the body cells, the most sensitive are spermatogonia and the least sensitive are nerve cells and muscle fibres Gi mucosa is Radiosensitive Small blood vessels are generally radioresistant

721.q: Thickness of Lead Apron used in Radiation Protection ?
721.e: The most commonly used thickness of Lead in Lead Apron for Radiation protection -0.5mm The Minimum Thickness of Lead in Lead Apron required for radaiation protection -0.25mm

721.q: Assertion: Ultrasound is safe in pregnancy. Reason: It uses radiation
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are false
721.e: Ultrasound does not use ionising radiation and is considered safe for use at all gestational ages in pregnancy. Reference: A Radiologist's Guide to the Performance and Interpretation of Obstetric Doppler US, Anne M. Kennedy and Paula J. Woodward, RadioGraphics 2019 39:3, 893-910

722.q: Which of the following is used in cancer staging ?
722.e: PET-CT is preferred for cancer staging as it evaluates lymph node involvement and metastatic disease in cancer patients. Reference: Jacobson FL, McKean SC. Chapter 105. Introduction to Radiology. In: McKean SC, Ross JJ, Dressler DD, Brotman DJ, Ginsberg JS. eds. Principles and Practice of Hospital Medicine.

722.q: Gastric emptying studies using radionuclides are used in?
722.e: Gastric emptying studies (GES) using radionuclides are performed to evaluate gastric motor function. They are often considered the "gold standard", and "most physiologic" examinations, because of their noninvasive nature, use a physiologic liquid or solid meal, and the resultant quantitative information. Typical indications for GES are evaluation of symptoms such as (postprandial) nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain, gastroesophageal reflux disease, difficult glycemic control in diabetic patients, suspected or known gastroparesis, and assessing response to therapy. Reference: Mc-Graw Hill speciality Board review Radiology page number 739

722.q: What is the investigation of choice for HCC?
722.e: The investigation of choice for HCC is CECT abdomen. CT evaluation of patients with suspected HCC should be done using multiphasic contrast imaging of the liver. HCC shows early arterial enhancement with Rapid Washout

722.q: A 18 year old female patient with primary amenorrhea. On USG examinaltion an echogenic tubular cystic mass with internal echoes was obtained. What is the most probable diagnosis?
722.e: Imperforate hymen is a congenital condition in which the hymen lacks a normal opening. The usual initial imaging modality of diagnosis, it shows a distended fluid-filled vagina (hematocolpos) and uterus (hematometra) with internal echoes representing hemorrhage of various ages. Reference: Imaging the Endometrium: Disease and Normal Variants Kenneth M. Nalaboff, John S. Pellerito, and Eran Ben-Levi RadioGraphics 2001 21:6, page number 1409-1424

722.q: A person is sitting on a 'fast unto death'. As a doctor, you will not allow the person to die because of
722.e: Article 21 of Constitution of India: This ensures 'Right to life,' but does not include the right to die. Hence, forcible feeding of persons going on hunger strike is lawful in India. Declaration of Malta: This deals with respecting the autonomy of the patient and suggests that the doctor should not feed forcibly in such cases. Feeding is allowed when the patient has lapsed into a coma. Article 14 of the Constitution of India: "The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India." Declaration of Sydney: Deals with the determination of death and the recovery of organs. Reference: The Essentials of Forensic Medicine & Toxicology by KS Narayan Reddy, 35th Edition, Page Number-260.

722.q: Which of the following is not radio-opaque?
722.e: The saline is a radio-lucent substance and is not seen on CXR. Iodine, barium and steel are radio-opaque and are easily seen on x rays. Reference: Bell, D. Contrast medium. Reference article, Radiopaedia.org. https://doi.org/10.53347/rID-69081

722.q: Sion procedure is used for visualisation of which of the following structures?
722.e: Normal tubes are isoechoic and are not usually visualised by TVS unless there is fluid contrast. The use of fluid contrast for evaluation of tubes has been described in literature as SION TEST from Mumbai or as SION PROCEDURE of sonosalpingography. Reference: Ultrasound in obstetrics and gynecology by Dr. P. K. shah, Dr. Mandakini megh, Dr. Nandita palshetkar page number 17

722.q: A patient presented with left iliac fossa pain. On USG examination, a large well defined anechoic cystic lesion was found arising from the left ovary. What is the most probable diagnosis?
722.e: Benign serous cystadenomas appear as sharply marginated, anechoic masses that may be large and are usually unilocular. Internal thin walled septations and papillary projections may be seen (in borderline tumours). Reference: Ultrasound in obstetrics and gynecology by Dr. P. K. shah, Dr. Mandakini megh, Dr. Nandita palshetkar page number 41

723.q: Which of the following techniques uses piezoelectric crystals?
723.e: Ans. Ultrasonography Ultrasonography is based on piezoelectric effect. MRI is based on gyeromagnetic property of proton (IP).

723.q: A technology which provides storage and convenient access to images from multiple modalities?
723.e: The picture archiving and communications system (PACS) is an image management system for improving the efficiency and workflow of radiology practices. Reference: PACS and Imaging Informatics: Basic Principles and Applications Radiology 2005 235:3, 740-740

723.q: On which of the following modalities is junctional zone of endometrium best visualised
723.e: MRI was the first imaging technique to permit the visualization of the uterine junctional zone and remains the imaging method of choice to evaluate it and its associated pathology. Junctional zone is a region representing the inner myometrium and is a very important imaging feature in pelvic MR imaging for interpretation of various pathologies. In its intact state, it is usually visualized on MRI as a low T2 signal layer beneath the endometrium. Reference: AIIMS-MAMC-PGI’s Comprehensive textbook of diagnostic radiology page number 224

723.q: Which of the following modalities is most useful in assessing the metastasis of colorectal carcinomas?
723.e: For detecting metastasis of colorectal carcinomas, CECT is helpful as it covers the whole abdomen in it's field and hepatic metastasis can be seen. MRI is used for local staging of disease and in evaluation of local extension into mesorectal fascia. Reference: AIIMS-MAMC-PGI’s Comprehensive textbook of diagnostic radiology page number 1760

723.q: Investigation of choice in pheochromocytoma is:
723.e: Answer is B (Urinary Catecholamines): Pheochromocytomas synthesize and store catecholamines which include norepinephrine, epinephrine and dopamine. The investigation of choice for diagnosis of Pheochromocytomas is determination of elevated levels of catecholamines and their methylated metabolites (metanephrines) in the plasma and urine. CT scan, MRI and MBIG Scintography are all useful diagnostic modalities for localization of pheochromocytoma once the diagnosis is established.

723.q: Which of the following investigation modalities help in categorising the focal hepatic lesions into benign and malignant?
723.e: Magnetic resonance imaging, MRI has more advantages than ultrasound, computed tomography, CT, positron emission tomography, PET, or any other imaging modality in diagnosing focal hepatic masses. With a combination of basic T1 and T2 weighted sequences, diffusion weighted imaging, DWI, and hepatobiliary gadolinium contrast agents, that is gadobenate dimeglumine (Gd-BOPTA) and gadoxetic acid (Gd-EOB), most liver lesions can be adequately diagnosed and differentiated into benign and malignant lesions. Reference: AIIMS-MAMC-PGI's Comprehensive textbook of diagnostic radiology page number 1656

723.q: Which of the following imaging modalities is used to evaluated tube patency?
o: Infusion of saline agitated with air bubbles
723.e: Hysterosalpingography (HSG) has been the traditional imaging modality of choice to evaluate tube patency, newer techniques involving agitated saline and ultrasound contrast agents injected during sono hysterography (SIS) have shown promise as an alternate imaging technique. Although the injection of saline agitated with air bubbles when performing SIS can confirm tube patency Ultrasound contrast "microbubbles" last longer and can be imaged with real-time cine clips and reconstructed two-dimensional and three-dimensional images to confirm tube patency Reference: Callen's Ultrasonography in Obstetrics and Gynecology, sixth edition page number 949

723.q: Which of the following modalities is now preferred for pretreatment staging of rectal cancer?
723.e: MRI is the modality of choice for rectal cancer staging. The high soft-tissue contrast of MRI accurately assesses the extramural tumor spread and relation to mesorectal fascia and the sphincter complex. MRI is the modality of choice for staging rectal cancer to assist surgeons in obtaining negative surgical margins. MRI facilitates the accurate assessment of mesorectal fascia and the sphincter complex for surgical planning. Reference: AIIMS-MAMC-PGI’s Comprehensive textbook of diagnostic radiology page number 1766

724.q: MRI is based on the principles of ?
724.e: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is based on the principles of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). Ultrasound is based on Piezoelectric effect

725.q: Which of the following type of mucor mycosis is commonly seen in COVID 19 pneumonia
725.e: Mucor mycosis can involve nose, sinuses, orbit, central nervous system (CNS), lung (pulmonary), gastrointestinal tract (GIT), skin, jaw bones, joints, heart, kidney, and mediastinum (invasive type), but ROCM is the commonest variety. It should be noted that term ROCM refers to the entire spectrum ranging from limited sino nasal disease (sino-nasal tissue invasion), limited rhino-orbital disease (progression to orbits) to rhino-orbital-cerebral disease (CNS involvement). The area of involvement may differ due to underlying condition. Reference: Singh, Awadhesh Kumar et al. “Mucor mycosis in COVID-19: A systematic review of cases reported worldwide and in India.” Diabetes & metabolic syndrome vol. 15,4 (2021): 102146. doi:10.1016/j.dsx.2021.05.019

725.e: Unilateral hemithorax in a child with sudden breathing difficulty suggests foreign body in lungs. It is removed by rigid bronchoscope, not partial. 725.q: All are features of Kerley A lines except?
o: Due to lymphatic engorgement and edema of septa
725.e: Kerley A lines are Perihilar Lines Kerley B lines are thin horizontal parallel lines perpendicular to pleura at base of Lung Kerley lines on a chest X-ray are thin linear opacities that can be associated with congestive heart failure (CHF). They are often classified into three types: Interstitial Kerley B Lines: Appear as short, horizontal lines at the lung periphery. Indicate interstitial edema, common in CHF. Septal Lines (Kerley A Lines) Vertical lines extending from the hila to the periphery. Result from fluid accumulation in the interlobular septa. Peribronchial Cuffing (Kerley A Lines): Short lines near the hila, representing fluid around bronchi. Suggestive of peribronchial edema. In CHF: X-ray findings often include cardiomegaly (enlarged heart). Increased vascular markings due to fluid retention. Pleural effusions may be present.

725.q: All are features of TOF on chest x ray except
725.e: In Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF), there is a characteristic decrease in pulmonary vascularity(pulmonary oligemia ) rather than pulmonary plethora. This is due to the obstruction of the right ventricular outflow tract (pulmonary stenosis), which results in decreased blood flow to the lungs. As a result, there is reduced vascularity in the lung fields, which can be seen on a chest X-ray. The "boot-shaped heart" appearance on chest X-ray is due to the right ventricular hypertrophy and narrowing of the pulmonary artery, which causes the heart to take on a boot-like shape. Right ventricular hypertrophy occurs because the right ventricle has to work harder to pump blood through the narrowed pulmonary valve. The upward pointed cardiac apex is typically seen in TOF with displaced to the left and may appear rounded or boot-shaped.

725.q: Which Lung Cancer Resembles Pneumonia with Air Bronchogram sign?

These nodules may show air bronchograms, and in some cases, multifocal involvement or pleural changes might be visible. While X-ray provides initial insights, further imaging and histopathological examination are crucial for a conclusive diagnosis. CT angiogram sign is also seen in bronchoalveolar ca

725.q: Which of the following is used in evaluation of lung abnormalities in COVID 19 patients?

725.q: A 2 year old child with sudden onset of breathlessness, wheezing and decreased breath sounds in rt lung. Chest radiograph shows diffuse opacity in right hemithorax. What is the probable diagnosis?
725.e: FB aspiration is most often seen in infants and toddlers (8 months-3 years). The clinical presentation may be acute while more often the symptoms remain indolent. The symptoms and signs can mimic asthma, upper respiratory infection, or pneumonia. The history of aspiration is often not elicited. FB may lead to partial ("ball-valve" effect) or complete obstruction, resulting in hyperinflation or collapse, respectively. Chest radiograph findings include asymmetric lung aeration, lung consolidation or atelectasis, and even pneumothorax or pneumomediastinum. Inspiratory radiographs alone may be normal in up to a third of patients (14-35%) with FBs. The lung volume of the affected lung/segment may be normal, increased, or decreased. Reference: AIIMS-MAMC-PGI's Comprehensive textbook of diagnostic radiology, pg 1052

726.q: Which of the following is seen on CXR in COVID 19 patients?
726.e: Findings of COVID-19 on chest radiographs vary, ranging from normal in the early stages of disease to unilateral or bilateral lung opacities, sometimes with a basilar and strikingly peripheral distribution. Early research reported a relatively low sensitivity (69%) for the diagnosis of COVID-19 using baseline chest radiography. Although underlying comorbidities such as chronic lung disease or congestive heart failure may confound chest radiograph interpretation, studies have shown that many of the hallmark chest CT findings are apparent on chest radiograph Reference: COVID-19 Imaging: What We Know Now and What Remains Unknown Jeffrey P. Kanne, Harrison Bai, Adam Bernheim, Michael Chung, Linda B. Haramati, David F. Kallmes, Brent P. Little, Geoffrey Rubin, and Nicola Sverzellati Radiology 2021 299:3, E262-E279

726.q: Which of the following is a common complication of COVID 19 pneumonia
726.e: COVID-19 may rapidly progress to ARDS, with older patients being at higher risk ARDS seen with COVID-19 is a cytokine release syndrome, in which immune and nonimmune cells release large amounts of proinflammatory cytokines that cause damage to the host. ARDS is characterized by an acute onset of non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema, hypoxemia, and the need for mechanical ventilation. Diffuse alveolar damage is the pathognomonic histologic finding. ARDS is the most common reason for patient admission to the intensive care unit and the main cause of mortality in patients with COVID-19 Reference: Chest CT in COVID-19: What the Radiologist Needs to Know Thomas C. Kwee and Robert M. Kwee RadioGraphics 2020 40:7, 1848-1865

727.q: Which of the following artery is used in management of fetal anemia?
727.e: Fetal Doppler US of the middle cerebral artery is used in two situations: (a) noninvasive assessment of fetal anemia and (b) calculation of cerebroplacental ratio as a measure of fetal brain sparing. In response to hypoxia, the fetus diverts blood flow to the brain, increasing the middle cerebral artery diastolic flow, thereby decreasing the pulsatility index and altering the ratio of the umbilical artery flow to the middle cerebral artery flow. 727.q: A 5-month-old infant presented to the OPD with seizures, hypotonia and hyporeflexia, and neurodevelopmental delay. o: H2O2 mediated breakdown of fatty acids

727.e: The clinical scenario is suggestive of Zellweger syndrome (cerebrohepatorenal syndrome). In this disease, H2O2 mediated peroxisomal beta-oxidation of very long chain fatty acid is affected. Beta-oxidation in peroxisomes is differentiated from that occurring in mitochondria by the formation of H2O2. Beta-oxidation of fatty acids in peroxisomes is not coupled to ATP synthesis. The high potential electrons are transferred to O2 which yields H2O2. This syndrome is a rare inherited disorder characterized by absent peroxisomal enzymes in all tissues leading to accumulation of C26 - C38 poly ionic acids in the brain tissue Reference: Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page Number-210.

728.q: Drop Metastasis due to CSF spread is seen with all except?
728.e: Drop metastasis refers to the spread of tumor cells through the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leading to seeding of the leptomeninges along the spinal cord or brain surface. This phenomenon is seen in certain types of brain tumors, particularly those originating in or near the ventricles or meninges. Medulloblastoma (A), Pineal germinoma (B), and Ependymoblastoma (C) are all types of brain tumors that can spread through the CSF and cause drop metastasis. Oligodendroglioma (D), however, typically does not exhibit this pattern of spread. Oligodendrogliomas are more likely to spread locally within the brain rather than through the CSF.
Cect is better to evaluate small bowel tumors

728.q: A 10-month-old girl had recurrent infections affecting various systems. All immunoglobulins were found to be reduced. Which of the following is not a characteristic seen in classic agammaglobulinemia?

Germinal centers of lymph nodes, peyer's patches, the appendix, and tonsils are underdeveloped. Plasma cells are absent throughout the body. T cell mediated reactions are normal. Reference: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10 th Edition, Page Number-244.

729.q: Some of the other contrast agents used in MRI are ___ and ___
729.e: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contrast agents are either paramagnetic ion complexes or superparamagnetic magnetite particles and contain lanthanide elements such as gadolinium (Gd3+) or transition metal manganese (Mn2+). These elements shorten the T1 or T2 relaxation time, thereby causing increased signal intensity on T1-weighted images or reduced signal intensity on T2-weighted images. Most paramagnetic contrast agents are positive agents. These agents shorten the T1, so the enhanced parts appear bright on T1-weighted images. Dysprosium, superparamagnetic agents and ferromagnetic agents are negative contrast agents. The enhanced parts appear darker on T2-weighted images. Reference: AIIMS-MAMC-PGI's Comprehensive textbook of diagnostic radiology page number 772

730.q: A 50-year-old male, who is a known case of PLHA, has had complaints of headache and dizziness for 2 days. Which of the following cells in the brain are predominantly infected by HIV?
730.e: The clinical syndrome of CNS abnormalities is called HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder (HAND). Microglia, cells in the CNS that belong to the macrophage lineage, are the predominant cell types in the brain that are infected with HIV. It is believed that HIV is carried into the brain by infected T cells or monocytes. The mechanism of HIV-induced damage of the brain remains obscure. Because neurons are not infected by HIV and the extent of neuropathologic changes is less than expected from the severity of neurologic symptoms, most workers believe that the neurologic deficit is caused indirectly by viral products and by soluble factors produced by infected microglia. Reference: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10 th Edition, Page Number-253.

730.q: A 45 year old female presents with recurrent headache, MRI reveals extraaxial, intradural and early enhancing lesion, All are Radiological features of this tumor except?
730.e: Calcification: True. Meningiomas can often exhibit calcifications, which can be seen on imaging. Vascular markings: True. Meningiomas can show prominent vascular markings due to their vascularity. Hyperostosis: True. Meningiomas can cause hyperostosis or thickening of adjacent bone due to their slow-growing nature and pressure effect on bone. Drop metastasis: False. Drop metastasis refers to the seeding of tumor cells along the spinal cord or brain surface via the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), which is not a characteristic feature of meningiomas. It is more commonly associated with medulloblastomas and other tumors that spread through the CSF.

730.q: Where is foramen ovale present in fetus?
730.e: In the fetus, deoxygenated blood is carried to the placenta by the umbilical arteries, which arise from the internal iliac arteries. Oxygenated blood returns from the placenta to the right atrium by way of the umbilical vein, left portal vein, ductus venosus, and inferior vena cava. Flow across the trumpet-shaped ductus venosus produces a defined stream of oxygenated blood that preferentially flows through the foramen ovale to the left atrium, left ventricle, and aorta, diverting the most oxygenated blood to the head and neck vessels and the coronary arteries. The foramen ovale is present in the interatrial septum which allows the blood to flow from right atrium to left atrium. Reference: A Radiologist’s Guide to the Performance and Interpretation of Obstetric Doppler US Anne M. Kennedy and Paula J. Woodward RadioGraphics 2019 39:3,page number 893-910

733.q: What is used in hepatobiliary scintigraphy?
733.e: Tc-99m labelled IDA (iminodiacetic acid) analogs are used for hepatobiliary scintigraphy. Hepatobiliary scintigraphy studies the function and integrity of the hepatobiliary system by visualising the production and flow of bile from the liver through the biliary system into the intestinal tract. Common indications are suspected acute cholecystitis, common bile duct obstruction, bile leak, and congenital abnormalities of the hepatobiliary tree. They have similar uptake, transport and excretion mechanisms as bilirubin. Reference: Mc-Graw Hill speciality Board review Radiology page number 743

733.q: ERCP is indicated in all except?
733.e: Endoscopic retrograde cholangio-pancreatography (ERCP) is considered as the gold standard for the diagnosis of CP because of its superior spatial resolution and its ability to depict the ductal system in distended state. Side branch abnormalities in early CP may be detected. ERCP is an invasive procedure and has inherent procedure-related complications; hence this modality is mostly used with the intent of therapeutic interventions. ERCP is also helpful in diagnosing other obstructive causes of CP such as ampullary lesions, intraductal neoplasms and congenital anomalies such as pancreatic divisum or annular pancreas Reference: AIIMS-MAMC-PGl's Comprehensive textbook of diagnostic radiology page 2032

734.q: Non visualisation of kidney on IVP is seen in?
734.e: In multicystic dysplastic kidney, the kidney is replaced with multiple cysts with non-functioning renal parenchyma. This results in non-visualisation of kidney on contrast study as no uptake of dye occurs by the affected kidney. Reference : AIIMS-MAMC-PGI's Comprehensive textbook of diagnostic radiology page number - 119

734.q: "Ring of fire" appearance is seen in ?
734.e: Ectopic pregnancy refers to the implantation of a fertilised ovum outside of the uterine cavity. The classic presentation is with abdominal pain and bleeding. Positive sonographic findings include: Uterus An empty uterine cavity or no evidence of an intrauterine pregnancy Pseudogestational sac or decidual cyst Decidual cast Thick echogenic endometrium Tube and ovary Simple adnexal cyst Complex extra-adnexal cyst/mass Solid hyperechoic mass is possible but non-specific Ring of fire sign: can be seen on color Doppler in a tubal ectopic, but can also be seen in a corpus luteum An absence of color Doppler flow does not exclude an ectopic Live extrauterine pregnancy peritoneal cavity Free pelvic fluid or hemoperitoneum in the pouch of Douglas Free fluid in the hepatorenal recess Reference: AIIMS-MAMC-PGI’s Comprehensive textbook of diagnostic radiology page number 268

734.q: Radiopaque density on a Abdominal radiograph, which overlaps the vertebra on lateral radiograph is suggestive of?
734.e: Renal stones overlap the vertebral shadows on lateral radiograph Gall stones are anterior to vertebral shadow on lateral radiograph

734.q: Extent of Renal vein invasion by RCC is better diagnosed by
734.e: IOC to evaluate RCC is CECT IOC to evaluate Renal Vein Invasion(vascular invasion) by RCC is MRI

734.q: Bosniak classification of renal cystic disease is based on which modality?
734.e: Bosniak classification is a system to classify the cystic renal masses into benign and malignant and is based on CT appearance of the lesion. Reference : AIIMS-MAMC-PGI's Comprehensive textbook of diagnostic radiology page number 110

734.q: First line imaging modality for evaluation of renal transplant dysfunction is :
734.e: According to American College of Radiology appropriateness criteria for renal transplant dysfunction, US duplex Doppler is the first line investigation. Colour doppler is used to evaluate the status of graft vessels and to detect any areas of focal stenosis or thrombosis. Colour doppler is also primary diagnostic modality for identifying various vascular complications. Reference : AIIMS-MAMC-PGI's Comprehensive textbook of diagnostic radiology page number 179

734.q: Central scar is seen in which type of renal tumour?
734.e: Oncocytomas are the most common benign solid non fat containing renal mass. Central scar is seen in oncocytomas This occurs due to spoke wheel pattern of feeding artery and central areas of fibrous scarring giving rise to a central scar like appearance. Reference : AIIMS-MAMC-PGI's Comprehensive textbook of diagnostic radiology page number - 141

735.q: Which of the following are screening views in mammography?
735.e: Mammography is primarily a screening and not a diagnostic tool. The mediolateral oblique (MLO) and craniocaudal (CC) views are standard screening views, whereas additional views described used mainly for diagnostic evaluation of lesions. Reference: Primer of diagnostic Imaging, sixth edition Page number - 561

735.q: Doppler ultrasound in first trimester is used for?
735.e: In the first trimester, the focus of Doppler US is (a) detection of aneuploidy and an increased risk for congenital heart disease with evaluation of the ductus venosus waveform, and (b) screening for women more likely to develop preeclampsia by evaluation of the uterine artery waveform. 735.q: What is the normal limit of endometrium in postmenopausal women?
735.e: A double-layer thickness of less than 5 mm without focal thickening excludes significant disease and is consistent with atrophy. Homogeneous, smooth endometrium measuring 5 mm or less are considered within the normal range with or without hormonal replacement therapy Reference: Imaging the Endometrium: Disease and Normal Variants Kenneth M. 735.q: Breast within a Breast on Mammography is seen in?
735.e: The breast within a breast appearence refers to the mammographic appearance of breast hamartomas (fibroadenolipomas).
