736.q: Which of the following is used in bone scan?
736.e: The radiotracer most commonly used for bone scan is Tc-99m methylene diphosphonate (MDP), where technetium-99-m is the radioactive component and MDP the biological component. Reference: Mc-Graw Hill speciality Board review Radiology page number 721

736.q: Three phase bone scan is positive in?
736.e: Three phase bone scan is done in osteomyelitis. Characteristic finding in osteomyelitis in a “three-phase bone scan” is increased activity in the blood flow, blood pool phases and delayed phase. Reference: Mc-Graw Hill speciality Board review Radiology page number 726

737.q: Remote after loading is used in:-
737.e: In afterloading procedures, an unloaded applicator is inserted first and the radioactive sources are introduced later . Afterloading has been utilized in many recently described uterine applicators, but the radiation exposure of physicians, nurses, and visitors during the treatment remains a serious problem. In principle, complete elimination of all unnecessary radiation exposure is possible by 'remote after-loading ,' which has been used for small teleradium bombs for more than twenty-five years and is widely applied in industrial radiography with gamma-ray sources. KEY TAKEAWAY - In remote after loading radiation exposure to the surrounding tissue is reduced. Reference: Remote Afterloading with Intracavitary Applicators Ulrich K. Henschke, Basil S. Hilaris, and G.D. Mahan Radiology 1964 83:2, 344-345

737.q: Imaging Studies using ionizing radiation in a female of reproductive age group should be restricted to
737.e: 10-DAY RULE: Radiological Investigations using Ionising Radiation in a female of reproductive age Group Should be Limited to first Ten Days Of Menstrual Cycle to avoid injury to any undiagnosed pregnancy.

737.q: How does radiation affect the cells?
o: Produces a double stranded breaks in cellular DNA
737.e: Double-stranded breaks of nuclear DNA is the most important cellular effect of radiation. in clinical therapy,radiation damage is most commonly indirectly ionizing via free-radical intermediaries formed from the radiolysis of cellular water. Double standard DNA damage is most important step Reference : Mehta, SR & Suhag, Virender & Semwal, Manoj & Sharma, Neelam. (2010). Radiotherapy: Basic Concepts and Recent Advances. Medical Journal Armed Forces India. 66. 158-162. 10.1016/S0377-1237(10)80132-7 page 3

737.q: Multi leaf collimators are used in ?
737.e: Intensity modulated radiation therapy is a state-of-the-art radiation delivery system, which shapes radiation beams to closely approximate the shape of the tumour This type of conformal radiation utilizes beams or multi leaf collimators that can turn on or off or be blocked during treatment, varying the radiation beam intensity across the targeted area Reference : Mehta, SR & Suhag, Virender & Semwal, Manoj & Sharma, Neelam. (2010). Radiotherapy: Basic Concepts and Recent Advances. Medical Journal Armed Forces India. 66. 158-162. 10.1016/S0377-1237(10)80132-7 page 9

o: All gross disease including the abnormally enlarged lymph nodes
Gross disease and the regions which harbour the microscopic disease
Margin around the tissue that allow the variations in treatment set up
737.e: Gross tumour volume (GTV) is all known gross disease including abnormally enlarged lymph nodes. The clinical target volume (CTV) encompasses the GTV plus regions considered to harbour potential microscopic disease. The planning target volume (PTV) provides a margin around the CTV to allow for variations in treatment setup and other anatomic motions during treatment such as respiration. In order to minimize any variation in patient positioning, meticulous immobilization is essential. Reference : Mehta, SR & Suhag, Virender & Semwal, Manoj & Sharma, Neelam. (2010). Radiotherapy: Basic Concepts and Recent Advances. Medical Journal Armed Forces India. 66. 158-162. 10.1016/S0377-1237(10)80132-7 page 5

737.q: What does a Linear accelerator (LINAC) produce in radiotherapy?
737.e: Explanation: LINACs produce both X-rays and electrons , making them versatile for treating different tumor sites. A Linear Accelerator (LINAC) is the most widely used machine for external beam radiotherapy. It works by accelerating electrons at high speed and then using them in two ways: The electrons themselves can be used directly for treatment. Or they can be made to strike a target, producing high-energy X-rays . These X-rays or electrons are then shaped and directed precisely at the patient's tumour to destroy cancer cells while minimising damage to surrounding healthy tissue. LINACs can deliver radiation using modern techniques like IMRT, VMAT, IGRT, SRS, and SBRT . Reference: https://barc.gov.in/ebooks/9788195473359/paper29.pdf https://med.virginia.edu/radiation-oncology/about/advanced-technologies/linear-accelerator-treatments/

738.q: A 70-year-old male patient named Alkeshbhai, a known case of bronchial asthma, presented to the emergency room with acute exacerbation, with severe breathlessness, chest tightness & dizziness. Physician immediately prescribed him salbutamol nebulization. Salbutamol inhalation did not improve the condition of the patient. Later, intravenous corticosteroids and aminophylline were added and the condition improved. What is the mechanism of action of corticosteroids in this condition?
o: They cause bronchodilation when given with xanthenes
They increase bronchial responsiveness to salbutamol
They increase the action of aminophylline on adenosine receptors
738.e: Mechanism of action of steroids in acute attack of bronchial asthma is to increase the bronchodilatory effect of beta 2 agonists, whereas in prophylaxis, their major mechanism is anti-inflammatory. Glucocorticoids are useful in both treatment and prophylaxis of bronchial asthma. Reference: Essentials of Medical Pharmacology by KD Tripathi, 8 th Edition, Page Number-249.

738.q: A 23-year-old young man with a known history of heroin addiction is brought to the emergency room in an unconscious state. On examination, the patient has decreased bowel sounds, depressed respiration, hypothermia, shallow breathing, and pinpoint pupils. Which of the following is the best and fast onset treatment of choice for this patient?
738.e: The decreased bowel sounds (constipation), respiratory depression, pinpoint pupils and history of heroin addiction strongly points toward the diagnosis of acute opioid poisoning. The drug of choice for acute opioid poisoning is intravenous naloxone. Reference: Kaplan & Sadock's Comprehensive Textbook of Psychiatry, 9th Edition, Page Number 1375-76,1384; Essentials of Medical Pharmacology by KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number 511-512.

739.q: Which of the following favours Aortitis?
739.e: Ascending aortic aneurysms can indeed occur in various conditions, including vasculitis and syphilis, but they can also be caused by other factors such as atherosclerosis, genetic conditions (e.g., Marfan syndrome), bicuspid aortic valve, or as a complication of cardiac surgery. These aneurysms involve the section of the aorta that rises from the heart and can be serious if they rupture. Early detection and management are crucial.

739.q: All the following can lead to an increase in temperature of the body in the first two hours following death except:
739.e: Cholera, septicemia, and sunstroke lead to an increase in body temperature in the first two hours following death. It is due to postmortem caloricity. Postmortem caloricity is the condition in which the temperature of the body remains raised for the first two hours or so after death. This occurs: When the regulation of heat production has been severely disturbed before death, as in sunstroke, pontine hemorrhage and in some nervous disorders. When there has been a great increase in heat production in the muscles due to convulsions, as in tetanus and strychnine poisoning, or increased muscular activity as in cases of violent asphyxial deaths (struggle prior to death) etc. When there has been excessive bacterial activity, as in septicemic conditions like cholera and other fevers. Reference: The Essentials of Forensic Medicine & Toxicology by KS Narayan Reddy, 35th Edition, Page Number-114.

739.q: A 30-year-old lady after undergoing miscarriage was found to be positive for the VDRL. Test for confirmation, gold standard investigation using fluorescent treponemal antibody test was done, which was found to be negative. Why was this discrepancy in the result observed?
739.e: Cardiolipin which is the phospholipid with antigenic properties is responsible for this discrepancy. VDRL contains cardiolipin -cholesterol - lecithin mixtures to detect serum antibodies formed against treponema pallidum. This lady who is undergoing further evaluation for her prior miscarriage probably has an anti-cardiolipin antibody. Here, serum that cross-reacts with the component of the VDRL reagent resulting in the biological false positive VDRL. However, the confirmatory test suggests that anti cardiolipin antibody is not due to infection with treponema pallidum but due to some other reason. Reference: Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page Number-200.

739.q: A 13-year-old child had enlarged lymph nodes and weight loss for 8 months. On excision biopsy, he was diagnosed to have EBV positive Burkitt lymphoma. Which of the following is not an effect of the latent membrane protein 1 (LMP 1) gene of EBV?
o: Promotion of B cell survival and proliferation
739.e: LMP-1 prevents apoptosis by activating BCL2. Thus, the virus 'borrows' normal B-cell activation pathways to expand the pool of latently infected cells. Other options - One EBV gene, latent membrane protein-1 (LMP-1), is an oncogene capable of inducing B-cell lymphomas in mice. LMP-1 behaves like a constitutively active CD40 receptor, a key recipient of helper T-cell signals that stimulate B-cell growth. LMP-1 activates the NF-κB and JAK/STAT signaling pathways and promotes B-cell survival and proliferation, all of which occur autonomously (i.e., without T cells or other outside signals) in EBV-infected B cells. Reference: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10 th Edition, Page Number-325.

739.q: A dead body was found at a crime scene. On examining it, you notice that the fixation of hypostasis has already occurred. What is the minimum time required for this finding to occur?
739.e: Fixation of hypostasis occurs 6 - 12 hours after death. Purple or reddish-purple discoloration of the skin due to collection of blood in toneless capillaries in dependent parts of the dead body is called postmortem hypostasis/ post mortem staining/suggillation. Timing of development of postmortem hypostasis: 0 - ½ hour → Absent ½ - 2 hours → Appear as mottled patches 2 – 4 hours → Patches coalesce with each other 4 hours → Well developed. 6 – 12 hours → Fixes (Average: 8 hours) Hypostasis persists till putrefaction sets in. Reference: The Essentials of Forensic Medicine & Toxicology by KS Narayan Reddy, 35th Edition, Page Number-114; Textbook of Forensic Medicine & Toxicology by Anil Aggrawal, 2nd Edition, Page Number-177.

739.q: Step ladder pattern of gas shadow is seen in
739.e: Answer- B. Intestinal obstruction Stepladder sign represents the appearance of gas-fluid distended small bowel loops that appear to be stacked on top of each other, typically observed on erect abdominal radiographs in the setting of small bowel obstruction.
